summary: 32-facet SOTA research: iOS-26 Liquid Glass morphing for the DOCK + the ANIMATION language + the GLASS primitives → a unified morph-facility path-forward + READMEs (batched)

notes.facet: iOS 26 / Apple "Liquid Glass" design language (WWDC 2025) — material principles + morphing controls, mapped onto glass-ui's dock + animation + glass primitives and the unified morph facility
sotaTechniques: MATERIAL MODEL — Liquid Glass is a multi-layer digital meta-material, not a blur. Apple's stack is: (1) a LENSING/refraction layer that bends light through the surface (content seen through it is optically displaced at the rim, not just blurred), (2) a real-time SPECULAR highlight layer that reacts to motion/tilt and 'defines the silhouette' (a moving rim catch-light), (3) a SHADOW/under-shadow layer that lifts the glass off content, and (4) an adaptive TINT + dynamic-range layer that shifts to keep foreground legible over any backdrop. The key insight Apple stresses: lensing (refraction at the edge) — NOT a flat frosted blur — is what reads as 'glass'. Source: WWDC25 session 219, Apple newsroom.

LENSING / EDGE-REFRACTION via SVG displacement (web port) — the browser-native recreation of Apple's lensing is an SVG `feImage`(displacement map)+`feDisplacementMap` filter applied as `backdrop-filter`. The displacement map encodes per-pixel offset in R(=x)/G(=y) channels (128=neutral, ±127 range); a height profile f(distanceFromEdge) — Apple favors the ⁴√(1-(1-x)⁴) squircle convex profile — gives strong displacement at the rim, ~0 in the center, so content magnifies/bends at the bezel exactly like a real lens. `scale` animates without rebuilding the map. Chromatic aberration = different displacement scale per RGB channel. CAVEAT: only Chromium supports SVG-filter-as-backdrop-filter today (Safari/FF use plain `filter`). Source: kube.io, rizroze/liquid-glass, LogRocket.

MORPHING-MERGE (GlassEffectContainer / glassEffectUnion / glassEffectID) — the conceptual heart of 'liquid'. Glass shapes placed in a container with a `spacing` threshold BLEND into ONE gel shape when within that distance and SEPARATE back out as they move apart (metaball/SDF-smin merge). A shared `@Namespace` + `glassEffectID` gives matchedGeometryEffect-style morphing: an element fluidly grows/relocates between two layouts on one spring, the glass 'flowing' between states rather than cross-fading. This is the model glass-ui's dock-collapse↔expand + layer-swap should emulate as ONE morph facility. Source: WWDC25 323, dev.to GlassEffectContainer, Apple 'Applying Liquid Glass to custom views'.

INTERACTIVE PRESS / GEL-SQUISH — `.glassEffect(.interactive())` adds touch feedback: the control scales/bounces and the specular intensifies under the finger ('lift up on touch, quiet at rest'). Canon: a ~0.96 press scale on an individual-transform (`scale:` longhand, not `transform`, to avoid minting a stacking context) keyed off a spring, with the catch-light brightening in lockstep. glass-ui already encodes `--scale-press: 0.96` as 'the canonical iOS Liquid Glass press scale'. Source: WWDC25 323, Apple HIG.

ADAPTIVE-EXPAND NAVIGATION (the dock/tab-bar behavior) — tab bars/toolbars 'shrink to bring focus to the content while keeping navigation accessible' and 'fluidly expand' on scroll-up; controls 'dynamically morph as users need more options'. This is precisely glass-ui's GlassDock collapse↔expand morph. The SOTA shape is a single-spring size+chrome morph with a clip-reveal aperture (box uncovers content laid out once) + a velocity-continuous interruptible retarget. Source: Apple newsroom, WWDC25 219.

NO-GLASS-ON-GLASS + NAVIGATION-LAYER-ONLY — Apple's hard rule: glass floats only in the navigation/overlay layer above content; content itself is never glass, and a glass surface never nests inside another glass surface (stacked blur muddies, the rim doubles). glass-ui already adopts this verbatim (glass.css header, the 3-band z-index rung-pairing). Source: WWDC25 219/323, HIG Materials.

CONCENTRIC CORNERS (ConcentricRectangle / .containerShape) — iOS 26 auto-derives a nested element's radius as outer-radius−padding so inner shapes read as part of the same rounded surface; NEVER nest two stadium pills. Apple uses CONTINUOUS-curvature squircles (`.continuous`), which eliminate the kink where a straight edge meets the arc. Web equivalent: `corner-shape: squircle` (Chrome 139+) over a `border-radius` fallback, plus inner-tile radius = `calc(outer − padding)`. glass-ui already ships both. Source: nilcoalescing, devtechie ConcentricRectangle, Apple HIG.

REGULAR vs CLEAR glass variants — Apple ships two materials: `.regular` (adaptive, legibility-first, default — auto-tints light/dark and dims content behind for contrast) and `.clear` (more transparent, for media-rich backdrops where you control contrast, e.g. over photos/video). A tint variant (`.regular.tint(_:)`) carries brand/phase color. Maps to a glass-ui tier/variant axis + the existing `--glass-tint-source`/`--glass-tint-strength` adaptive-tint recipe. Source: WWDC25 219, HIG Materials.

INTERRUPTIBLE VELOCITY-CONTINUOUS SPRINGS — the practitioner canon (Emil Kowalski, Apple): springs MAINTAIN velocity when interrupted; CSS keyframes restart from zero. A gesture the user reverses mid-flight (collapse→re-expand, esc during open) must retarget the live spring from its current (value, velocity), not dispose+restart. Transform/opacity-first, pointer-capture to resolve scroll/drag conflicts. glass-ui's `useSpring`/SpringProgress already does velocity-continuity; the gap is unifying it as the ONE driver. Source: Emil Kowalski 'Animations on the Web', vercel-labs web-animation-design skill.

WEB-PLATFORM 2025 BASELINE for native morph — `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` + `calc-size()` animate to/from intrinsic sizes (auto/fit-content) (Chrome 129+, NOT Safari/FF — not Baseline); `@starting-style` + `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` + `overlay` animate top-layer entry/exit (Newly Available); View Transitions (same-doc + `view-transition-class`, Newly Available, + 2025 Nested view-transition groups for clip/3D preservation) for cross-state/route morphs; anchor positioning for tethered popovers. glass-ui already wires `@starting-style`/`allow-discrete` (.glass-top-layer), scroll-driven recipes, and a View-Transitions substrate. Source: Chrome 'view transitions in 2025', MDN interpolate-size, css-tricks.

VIEW-TRANSITIONS IS THE WRONG PRIMITIVE FOR A LAYOUT MORPH (but right for route/page morphs) — VT crossfades flat RASTER snapshots: a box that grows shows taffy-stretch/text-blur distortion unless you fight it with `object-fit: cover` on the pseudos; it also can't run two co-mounted same-named transitions. For a continuous size morph (the dock), a single analytic spring writing one scalar is correct; reserve VT for discrete content/route swaps where a cross-fade is desired. This is exactly the AX.W01 verdict. Source: css-tricks cross-document VT gotchas, Chrome VT-2025.
notes.applicability:
"glass-ui is already ~70% of the way to iOS-26 vocabulary — the SOTA here is mostly CONVERGENCE + two genuine additions (lensing, morphing-merge), not greenfield. Concrete mapping:

UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY (the headline 'every element morphs/springs/flows' ask): the path is the AX.W01/W02 design — ONE analytic spring (SpringProgress) writing ONE normalized scalar `--dock-morph-t` (0→1) to the root, with EVERY axis (inline-size, padding, border-radius, scale, bg/border color, child stagger) expressed as `calc()` reads off it. Generalize this beyond the dock into a reusable `useMorph(fromEl,toEl)`/`--morph-t` primitive that any element (dialog, popover, card→detail, tab indicator, segmented toggle) consumes — this IS the web analog of glassEffectID/matchedGeometryEffect. The `--dock-morph-progress` child-stagger already proves the calc-ramp pattern (clamp((t−onset)/window)); promote it to a tokenized `--morph-stagger-step` (replacing the hand-typed nth-child ladder per W02). Keep View-Transitions ONLY for the consumer route-morph seam (preserve the `glass-dock-${useId()}` name), retire it as the dock's own collapse mechanism.

MORPHING-MERGE (the gel blend): glass-ui already has the GooBlob WebGL2 metaball (smin SDF merge) — the iOS GlassEffectContainer 'shapes blend within a spacing threshold' is the same math. A CSS-cheap version for dock controls/icon clusters is the goo-filter trick (blur+contrast threshold on a group) gated to a `.glass-merge-group`; the WebGL blob is the high-fidelity version. This is the most distinctive missing iOS-26 behavior and a natural new primitive.

LENSING (the missing material atom): glass-ui's `.glass-material::before` is a specular catch-light but there is NO refraction/displacement. Add an opt-in `.glass-lens` layer using the SVG `feDisplacementMap`-as-`backdrop-filter` recipe (squircle convex profile, R/G displacement map, `scale` animatable, optional per-channel chromatic fringe — glass-ui already has `--glass-edge-dispersion` for the fringe half). Chromium-only → `@supports`-gate over the existing blur fallback, exactly like the `corner-shape: squircle` gate already in glass.css. This upgrades the rim from 'highlighted' to 'optically bending', the single thing that most separates 'glassmorphism' from 'Liquid Glass'.

SPECULAR (already shipped — needs the W09 tune): the moving `::before` catch-light is correct but blown out (pure-white `hsl(40 30% 100%/0.55)` + 0.35/0.6/0.85 ladder). W09's warm-cream low-alpha + tokenized `--glass-specular-intensity-{rest,hover,active}` ladder + rest-floor-0 + retire-the-dock-double + `useSpecularTracking()` composable is the exact convergence. Tie specular brightening to the press-spring (lockstep) per `.glassEffect(.interactive())`.

SPRING VOCABULARY (already shipped — needs the W05 convergence): the `linear()` spring set (`--spring-dock` (0.32,0.7)/+4.6%, snappy, bouncy, smooth, gentle) is the iOS register; excise the legacy `--ease-apple-spring` cubic-bezier, give each register a named surface-class (dock-morph→dock, control-glide→snappy, playful→bouncy, settle→smooth/gentle), and re-point the slider-in-dock onto the dock register so a control shares its host's curve (the iOS 'one material, one motion' coherence).

PRESS/GEL-SQUISH (already shipped): `--scale-press: 0.96` on the `scale:` longhand is the iOS canon; ensure every interactive surface (button, dock control, slider thumb, switch, card-as-button) carries the four-state press on the SAME spring so the whole UI 'lifts on touch, quiets at rest' uniformly.

CONCENTRIC + SQUIRCLE (already shipped): `corner-shape: squircle` gate + `calc(outer−padding)` inner-tile radius are present; extend the squircle gate to more surfaces and ensure no stadium-in-stadium nesting anywhere.

NATIVE-FIRST size morph: where Chromium-only is acceptable, `interpolate-size`/`calc-size()` could drive intrinsic-size morphs CSS-natively — but the AX history (AV.W9.0 dual-driver race) is the warning: never let it co-drive with the JS spring. One owner per axis."
pitfalls: DUAL-DRIVER RACE (the AX cardinal hazard): never let two systems write the same axis. glass-ui already burned on this — `interpolate-size`/`calc-size` CSS-native width interpolation ran WHILE SpringProgress wrote inline width per frame (AV.W9.0), cancelling the morph and freezing the dock under green gates. ONE owner per concern: size=spring (or VT, never both), opacity=CSS crossfade, visibility=delayed-hold. The unified `--morph-t` facility must be the SOLE driver.

VIEW-TRANSITIONS RASTER DISTORTION: VT screenshots old+new and morphs flat raster — a growing box gets taffy-stretch + text-blur. Do NOT use VT for the dock size morph (continuous layout morph → spring). Co-mounted docks minting the same `view-transition-name` silently DROP the snapshot and red e2e — names must be app-unique via `useId()`.

SPECULAR BLOWOUT: a screen-blended pure-white catch-light over glass-ui's flat warm-cream substrate reads as a hot flash even though it looked fine over the busy aurora it was tuned on. Lower alpha + warm-cream core (L<100%) + rest-floor-0; `screen` of low-alpha white still lifts toward white over LIGHT — keep `screen` on dark, soften over light.

LENSING PERF + SUPPORT: SVG-filter-as-backdrop-filter is Chromium-ONLY and expensive — any shape/size change forces a full displacement-map rebuild (only `scale` is cheap). Pre-bake the map, animate only `scale`, `@supports`-gate over the blur fallback, keep it opt-in, and never put it on the per-frame-resizing dock box mid-collapse.

GLASS-ON-GLASS / OVER-USE: Apple restricts glass to the navigation/overlay band; stacking glass-on-glass muddies blur + doubles the rim, and flooding content with glass hurts legibility (the public iOS-26 a11y complaints). Keep the 3-band rung-pairing; inside a glass panel compose FLAT tiers.

BACKDROP-FILTER COST AT SCALE: blur+displacement+specular is GPU-heavy; many simultaneous glass surfaces (grid-dock tiles, glass-card lists) jank. Budget the count, gesture-scoped `will-change` only, lean on content-visibility/offscreen-pause.

ACCESSIBILITY GATES non-optional: `prefers-reduced-transparency` (flatten to opaque), `prefers-reduced-motion` (snap the spring, drop lensing animation), `prefers-contrast`, `forced-colors` (AX.W36). The morph PRM path must reach 0 motion frames without breaking the layout outcome.

STAGGER-FROM-TIMERS orphans on an interrupted/reversed morph — drive the cascade off the SAME `--morph-t` scalar (calc ramp per child onset) so flick + hover-open both choreograph and an interrupted morph carries the cascade.

STACKING-CONTEXT FLICKER: `transform: scale()` mints a stacking context that flickers a portaled popover under the dock. Use the `scale:` longhand + `scale:1` identity base at rest (glass-ui's AQ.W3 discipline).

TINT COLOR-SPACE: adaptive tint must mix in oklab; `oklch(from …)` lightness shift is unsafe (no gamut-map yet) and an `hsl()` alpha nesting a registered `@property` var computes to 0 in Chromium (drive layer `opacity`, not a per-stop alpha).

notes.facet: SwiftUI Liquid Glass APIs — glassEffect / GlassEffectContainer / glassEffectID / the morph-merge between glass elements
sotaTechniques: glassEffect(_:in:) — Apple's single material modifier. Signature `glassEffect(_ glass: Glass = .regular, in shape: S = .capsule, isEnabled: Bool)`. ONE call applies the full material (adaptive blur + refraction + edge-light rim + specular catch-light) to any view, with `.regular` (default, adaptive), `.clear` (high-transparency media case), `.identity` (conditional disable), plus a chainable `.tint(color)` and `.interactive()` (press-scale + bounce + shimmer + touch-point illumination). The headline lesson: glass is ONE composable material, not per-component CSS.

GlassEffectContainer(spacing:) — the shared sampling region + morph-merge host. Signature `GlassEffectContainer(spacing: CGFloat?, content:)`. It combines multiple glass shapes into ONE rendering pass so they (a) share a single backdrop-sample (Apple's hard constraint: 'glass cannot sample other glass'), (b) blend/merge where they overlap or come within `spacing` pixels (the metaball-like gooey union), and (c) morph between each other on layout change. The spacing scalar is the merge THRESHOLD — elements closer than it fuse into one liquid shape; farther stay discrete. One container = one GPU pass for blur+lighting across N shapes.

glassEffectID(_:in:) + @Namespace — the matched-geometry morph identity. `glassEffectID(id, in: namespace)` tags two glass shapes (e.g. a collapsed pill and an expanded toolbar) with the SAME identity in a shared `@Namespace`; when one is conditionally hidden and the other shown inside `withAnimation(.bouncy)`, SwiftUI morphs the material continuously between them — the glass flows from shape A into shape B rather than crossfading. This is matchedGeometryEffect specialized for the glass material.

glassEffectTransition — the morph style selector. `enum GlassEffectTransition { identity, matchedGeometry (default), materialize }`. `matchedGeometry` is the continuous fly/grow morph; `materialize` is a material-appearance entry. Picks HOW a glass element enters/leaves its container.

glassEffectUnion(id:namespace:) — manual cross-distance merge. Forces glass shapes with matching id + same glass type + similar shape to render as one merged silhouette even when not adjacent — the explicit grouping the auto-spacing-merge can't reach. Use it to make a row of separate buttons read as one continuous glass bar.

iOS `.bouncy` spring as the canonical morph clock — `withAnimation(.bouncy(duration: 0.4))` (or argument-less `.bouncy`) is Apple's recommended curve for every glass morph; the whole merge/expand/collapse rides ONE interruptible spring, which is exactly the single-scalar-one-clock model AX.W01 mandates.

CSS View Transitions + view-transition-name (the web glassEffectID) — name two DOM elements with the same `view-transition-name` and the browser captures old/new geometry and morphs position+size+aspect between them inside `document.startViewTransition(mutate)`. Baseline Newly Available across all engines (Firefox 144, Oct 2025). This is the literal web analog of `glassEffectID` for layout/route morphs — BUT it crossfades rasterized snapshots, so it is the wrong primitive for a live interruptible CONTROL morph (AX.W01's exact diagnosis).

view-transition-class (new 2025) — a non-unique class applied to many tracked elements so a shared morph recipe (`::view-transition-group(.cls)`) drives N rows/panes at once without minting N unique names. glass-ui already ships this as `.gl-list-item` / `.gl-dock-layer` in view-transition.css. The web equivalent of a `GlassEffectContainer` group recipe.

interpolate-size: allow-keywords + calc-size() — Chrome 129+ (not yet Baseline). Lets a length animate TO/FROM an intrinsic keyword (`height: 0 → auto`, `width → max-content`) natively, no JS measure. The native primitive for a content-driven dock-wrap/expand morph (AX.W04) — one end must be a length, and it does not interpolate keyword-to-keyword.

@starting-style + transition-behavior: allow-discrete — Baseline Newly Available (Firefox 129). Defines the first-style-update FROM values so an element animates in on insertion and (with `allow-discrete` swapping `display`/`visibility` at the 50% mark) animates OUT on removal — entry/exit material grammar with NO JS lifecycle. glass-ui already uses this for the top-layer entry grammar (animations.css §TOP-LAYER).

CSS gooey-merge filter (SVG feGaussianBlur → feColorMatrix alpha-contrast) — the web's metaball union: blur sibling shapes so they bleed together, then an alpha-contrast matrix (`0 0 0 18 -7` on the alpha row) snaps the blur into a sharp merged silhouette. This is the pixel-accurate analog of `GlassEffectContainer`'s shape-merge — but the alpha trick renders as plain blur in Safari/Firefox (Chromium-reliable only), so it must be a progressive garnish, never the structural primitive.

corner-shape: squircle (Chrome 139+) — the literal iOS-26 superellipse corner geometry that backdrop-filter, border and shadow all follow; glass-ui already @supports-gates it over the border-radius round in glass.css + dock.css. The geometric half of the Liquid-Glass look.

Practitioner morph idioms (Family.co / Benji Taylor / Emil Kowalski / Rauno Freiberg) — Family's shared-letter text morph (Continue→Confirm by morphing common glyphs), intentional 'sprinkled' morph moments, screen-morph navigation clarity; Emil Kowalski's transform/opacity-first + spring-over-duration rules and 'great animations' interruptibility; Rauno's invisible-interaction-detail craft. The design grammar that says WHERE to morph (selectively, on meaningful state change) and that motion must be interruptible and physical, not timed.
notes.applicability: DOCK: glass-ui's dock is mid-rebuild toward exactly the SwiftUI model. AX.W01 (single-scalar `--dock-morph-t`, one analytic SpringProgress clock, RETIRE the VT fork for the collapse) IS the `glassEffect` + `.bouncy`-one-clock pattern: every axis (inline-size, padding, radius, scale, color, child stagger) as calc() off one normalized scalar — the direct web realization of Apple's 'one container, one spring, the material flows'. The existing useLayerTransition.ts already runs a live `SpringProgress` in PIXEL space with velocity-continuity on interrupt (the iOS interruptible-physics behaviour) and writes `--dock-morph-progress` for the spring-keyed child stagger — that IS the right primitive; W01's job is to delete the parallel VT/FLIP fork so it is the ONLY one. The CRITICAL cross-repo nuance the research confirms: `view-transition-name` is the web `glassEffectID` for ROUTE/page morphs (fourier's viz↔workspace geometry-morph) and MUST be preserved as a seam, while the dock-COLLAPSE VT (snapshot crossfade) is retired — these are SEPARABLE, exactly as AX.W01's CONVERGE folds state. AX.W02 (one orchestrator per dock, fold the inner DockLayerGroup onto the outer driver via DI) is the `GlassEffectContainer` model: the dock IS the container, collapsed↔expanded and pane-swap are both layer transitions in ONE namespace/group on ONE clock — adopt `glassEffectID`-style identity so a collapsed pill morphs INTO the expanded toolbar (matched-geometry), not crossfades. ANIMATION: AX.W05's 'one iOS-spring vocabulary' (excise the legacy apple-spring bezier, govern settle/control/playful registers, pin the dock to (0.32,0.7) `--spring-dock`) is Apple's single `.bouncy` discipline — one curve family for every glass morph; the research backs the 'spring-over-duration, interruptible' rule (Emil Kowalski) as the canon. GLASS: glass.css ALREADY implements the material atoms SwiftUI bundles — the moving-specular `::before` catch-light (interactive() touch illumination, mapped from --mouse-x/--mouse-y), the `--glass-edge-light` full-perimeter rim (the silhouette catch-light WWDC25 calls out), the unified `.glass-material` group so Switch/Button/Dialog read as ONE material, the no-glass-on-glass rung-pairing discipline (Apple's hard rule, verbatim), corner-shape squircle, and the adaptive oklab tint (the `.tint()` analog). UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY (the path forward): build a `GlassEffectContainer`-equivalent web primitive — a composable that (1) hosts a set of glass children in ONE shared-sampling region (single backdrop pass, no glass-on-glass), (2) takes a `spacing`/threshold scalar driving a gooey-merge garnish (SVG filter, Chromium-progressive) so adjacent controls fuse, and (3) exposes a `glassMorphId` matched-geometry seam so any two glass shapes morph between each other on one shared spring. Realize the merge with the existing dock single-scalar clock (one SpringProgress → CSS var → every child's geometry), the existing `view-transition-class` group recipe for the route/discrete case, `interpolate-size`/`calc-size()` for content-driven size morphs (kills the magic-640 wrap chain in AX.W04), `@starting-style`+allow-discrete for entry/exit material, and corner-shape squircle + the `.glass-material` rim/specular for the look — so the dock, the panels, the dialogs, and a future toolbar ALL morph on the same single-clock spring facility, the iOS-26 'morph-merge for every element' goal.
pitfalls: VT is the WRONG primitive for a live control morph — View Transitions crossfade RASTERIZED snapshots and run on a separate clock from any animating ancestor, producing the box-leads-content desync AX.W01 diagnoses; worse, the dock's morph is NOT reliably live-measurable (keyframes proved 181 rAF getBoundingClientRect samples captured NO morph because VT runs on snapshots). Use the live single-scalar spring for the control morph; reserve VT for route/page geometry-morphs only.

view-transition-name must be UNIQUE per element per state — two co-mounted docks both minting `glass-dock-1` DROPS the morph snapshot and reds ~13 e2e (the fourier two-dock collision). Any morph-id seam needs a useId()-scoped unique name; this is a binding-verification-class footgun.

The SVG gooey/metaball merge (feColorMatrix alpha-contrast) renders as PLAIN BLUR in Safari and Firefox — the merge only fuses in Chromium. It must be a progressive garnish over a shape that already reads correctly, never the structural silhouette. Mirrors glass-ui's existing `.glass-chromatic` opt-in discipline.

No glass on glass — Apple's hard constraint ('glass cannot sample other glass'); a glass surface nested in glass muddies the blur, doubles the rim, collapses the read. glass.css already encodes this as rung-pairing; a `GlassEffectContainer` analog must enforce that contained children are FLAT tiers, only the container plate is glass.

interpolate-size/calc-size() is Chrome-129+ ONLY, NOT Baseline — needs an @supports gate with a JS-measure or fixed-size fallback; and it cannot interpolate keyword-to-keyword (one end must be a length). Don't make the content-driven wrap morph depend on it unconditionally.

backdrop-filter blur is the dominant GPU cost — N independent glass plates = N backdrop samples; Apple's whole `GlassEffectContainer` rationale is collapsing them to ONE pass. A web morph facility that stamps backdrop-filter per child will jank; share one sampling surface. Also gate the whole material under prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce (glass.css already flattens blur/opacity there) and prefers-reduced-motion (zero the spring/VT — view-transition.css + the dock PRM path already do).

Spring-as-duration mismatch — driving a morph on a CSS `transition` with a bezier while the size runs on a JS spring forks the clock (the exact AQ.W6→AW accretion AX.W01 unwinds). EVERY axis must read the SAME scalar; no per-engine personality fork, no separate inner-vs-root clocks.

will-change/contain hazards — promoting the morphing box needs on-demand will-change (set at gesture start, cleared on settle, as useLayerTransition already does); a permanent will-change on every glass plate burns memory. corner-shape squircle + overflow:clip single-axis must keep the cross-axis explicitly `visible` (the MDN single-axis-clip-degrades-to-hidden caveat the dock already documents).

Over-morphing — the practitioner consensus (Family, Rauno) is morph SELECTIVELY on meaningful state change; a facility that morphs every element on every change reads as noise, not delight. The facility should make morph cheap but the design grammar should ration it.

notes.facet: The iOS 26 morphing DOCK / toolbar / tab-bar — how it reshapes, merges, splits, and flows as a single liquid body. Apple's model: every control lives on ONE singular floating plane that shape-shifts between app contexts; multiple discrete glass shapes within a proximity threshold visually MERGE into one fluid body and SPLIT apart again as state changes, with the material itself thickening (deeper shadows, more pronounced lensing/refraction) when it flexes to larger sizes. glass-ui already has a sophisticated single-spring/single-clock morph (the AX.W01-W06 rebuild), but it morphs ONE box's box-axis; it does NOT yet model a dock as N discrete shapes that fuse/separate, and it FAKES glass refraction with blur+specular rather than true lensing.
sotaTechniques: GlassEffectContainer + spacing-threshold merge (Apple SwiftUI, iOS 26): a container view defines ONE shared glass sampling region; child glass shapes within `spacing` points of each other visually BLEND/MORPH into a single body (borders blur, interiors flow together) and separate again past the threshold — the dock is a gel, not a row of pills. `glassEffectUnion(id:namespace:)` manually forces distant shapes to merge; `spacing: 30` is the cited example. This is THE mechanism for 'reshapes, merges, splits, flows as a single liquid body.'

glassEffectID + Namespace matched-geometry morph (Apple SwiftUI): the modern matchedGeometryEffect — tag a glass shape with `.glassEffectID(id, in: namespace)`; when a control appears/disappears or swaps context under `withAnimation`, SwiftUI computes the in-between shapes from the container spacing + the shapes' geometry and FLOWS the glass along a matched trajectory (button grows into menu, toolbar item splits into two). sotaTechniques: SwiftUI matchedGeometryEffect — the original primitive: two views sharing an (id, namespace) pair are treated as the SAME element across a state change; SwiftUI reads both frames (position+size) and interpolates one into the other on a single animation transaction (one withAnimation clock), so a small badge morphs into a full card rather than cross-fading. Identity is the matching id; geometry (the bounding frame) is what gets tweened.

SwiftUI matchedTransitionSource + navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID:)) — the iOS-18/26 successor for PRESENTATION morphs: tag the source control with .matchedTransitionSource(id:in:) and the destination sheet/detail with .navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID:in:)); the system zooms+morphs the source's geometry into the presented surface (button literally becomes the sheet) and reverses on dismiss, with a continuous interactive (swipe-to-dismiss) spring. This is the canonical iOS-26 Liquid-Glass 'morph out of the thing you tapped'.

SwiftUI GlassEffectContainer + glassEffectID(_:in:) + GlassEffectTransition — the Liquid-Glass-specific matched-geometry: a single container establishes ONE shared sampling/lighting region; glass children with glassEffectID in one @Namespace MERGE and SPLIT as liquid blobs. A `spacing` parameter sets the distance at which neighbours fuse into one glass shape (low=merge only when nearly touching, high=fuse early/more connected). Add/remove a child and the container runs a liquid merge between neighbours off the geometry — the matched-geometry morph rendered as a metaball-style fusion, not a cross-fade.

Web View Transitions API — shared-element morph via view-transition-name: two elements (old DOM state, new DOM state) carrying the SAME view-transition-name are snapshotted; the browser compares position/size/rotation of the two snapshots and generates a keyframe animation that translates+scales the ::view-transition-group between them — the direct web analogue of matchedGeometryEffect. view-transition-name: match-element (Chrome 137+/FF144+/Safari 18.4+) auto-derives a stable name per element so 100-card lists need no hand-naming.

Element-scoped View Transitions — element.startViewTransition() (Chrome 147, stable): scopes the whole VT machinery to a DOM SUBTREE instead of the document. Multiple/nested scoped transitions run CONCURRENTLY, the rest of the page stays interactive, the scope root auto-applies contain:layout + view-transition-group:contain + automatic overflow:clip on ::view-transition-group-children — i.e. a self-contained component (a dock, a card) can morph its own internals without a document-wide freeze and without the 'uncaptured animating ancestor desync' that document-level VT suffers.

view-transition-group property + nested groups + animation-longhand inheritance (Chrome 140+) — assign a parent group to a ::view-transition-group so the pseudo tree mirrors the real DOM hierarchy; nested groups preserve clipping and 3D transforms during the morph (text stays clipped inside the morphing card), and ::view-transition-group() now inherits duration/easing/fill to its children so a single curve declaration drives the whole group in lockstep.

notes.facet: Liquid-glass MATERIAL optics — lensing, refraction, edge light-bending, the convex meniscus, specular catch-light, the "thick glass" look
sotaTechniques: LENSING vs BLUR (the Apple core distinction) — traditional blur SCATTERS light to a soft diffuse field; Liquid Glass LENSES it, bending and concentrating rays in real time the way a curved glass body physically does, giving the surface optical definition against the backdrop rather than a flat frost. Practically: blur is the FALLBACK, displacement-refraction is the TARGET. (WWDC25 'Meet Liquid Glass' sess.219.)

SVG feDisplacementMap on backdrop-filter (the canonical web recipe) — a pre-baked RGBA displacement map (R=x-shift, G=y-shift, 128=neutral, 0→-scale / 255→+scale) feeds `feDisplacementMap in=SourceGraphic in2=map scale=N xChannelSelector=R yChannelSelector=G`, mounted via `backdrop-filter: blur(...) url(#filter)`. Warps the real backdrop pixels around the element's curved edge = true refraction, not a fake gradient. Chromium-only; @supports-gate it. (kube.io, LogRocket, rizroze.)

Convex-squircle surface profile + Snell's law map generation — the displacement field is computed from a surface height profile `y = ⁴√(1 − (1−x)⁴)` (Apple's preferred squircle corner curve, softer than the spherical `y=√(1−(1−x)²)`), differentiated numerically for surface normals, refracted via Snell (n1=1 air, n2=1.5 glass), magnitude precomputed on one radius then rotated azimuthally. This is what produces the CONVEX MENISCUS — heavy bend at the rim, flat clear core. glass-ui's `#glass-refract` already cites this exact profile but bakes only a crude radial gradient, not the Snell-derived normal map.

Chromatic aberration via per-channel R/G/B displacement (the 'thick-glass' tell) — run THREE staggered `feDisplacementMap` passes at slightly different scales (e.g. R=scale, G=scale+10, B=scale+20, the `[0,10,20]` aberration default), isolate each via `feColorMatrix`, recombine with `feBlend mode=screen`. Each color refracts at a different angle → prismatic rainbow fringing at the lens edge. This is the single biggest visual upgrade missing from glass-ui's current single-pass `#glass-refract`. (rizroze, Z1Code glass-refraction.)

Specular catch-light as a rim/normal-driven highlight (not a flat bloom) — the bright edge-light is a SEPARATE `feImage` (or `::before` radial) whose intensity varies by surface-normal angle vs a fixed light direction, blended `screen` over the refracted result; on real iOS it tracks DEVICE MOTION. On web the practitioner pattern is a pointer-anchored masked radial that rides the surface, exactly what glass-ui already ships — but the SOTA color is a low-alpha WARM-CREAM core (~0.08–0.32), never the pure-white 0.55 glass-ui currently paints.

Full-perimeter edge-light rim that 'defines the silhouette' — a thin inset ring (`inset 0 0 0 0.75px` low-alpha white) wraps the whole plate so the glass body reads as a discrete object lifting off the backdrop; WWDC25 names this the catch-light that defines the silhouette. glass-ui already has this as `--glass-edge-light` promoted across the material group (AW.W22) — correct and current.

Adaptive tint + under-shadow for legibility/thickness — Apple modulates hue/brightness/saturation of the tint adaptively, and raises the under-shadow OVER text (glass reads as lifting off content) vs drops it over solid light. The 0.5px dark bottom-edge under-shadow reads as literal glass THICKNESS. glass-ui ships both (oklab adaptive `--glass-tint-*`, the `--glass-under-shadow-*` rungs, `[data-over-content]` modifier) — current and SOTA-aligned.

GlassEffectContainer smin-merge / metaball morph (the unified-morph heart) — iOS groups multiple glass shapes in a container with a `spacing` threshold; when shapes come within `spacing` they BLEND via a liquid metaball merge (smooth-min SDF union), morphing identity-tracked elements (`glassEffectID` in a namespace) into one another. This is the gel/liquid behavior. The web analog is exactly glass-ui's GooBlob smin SDF — the path to a unified morph is to treat the dock + its children as one smin field, OR to drive the CSS displacement `scale` from the same single-scalar spring as the box morph.

View Transitions for shared-element shape morphs — `view-transition-name` on an element snapshots old+new states and the browser tweens position/size/shape between two DOM states; combine with `::view-transition` for custom easing. Baseline-ish in 2025 (Chrome 111+, Safari 18+, Firefox 144+ same-document). glass-ui already uses VT for route-morph but AX.W01 is RETIRING the VT fork for the dock's own collapse (VT crossfades rasterized pixels — wrong primitive for a layout morph; a single analytic spring → `--dock-morph-t` is the right one).

interpolate-size / calc-size() for animating to intrinsic auto — `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` (or `calc-size(auto, size)`) lets width/height transition to/from `auto`/`max-content`, eliminating the `width:auto` non-interpolation that forces FLIP/VT hacks. Chromium-only (Chrome/Edge 129+), NOT Baseline — so it's a progressive-enhancement layer, not the primary morph driver. glass-ui's GlassDock comment already notes the `width:auto` non-interpolation pain this solves.

@starting-style + @property typed customs for spring-interpolable material — `@starting-style` defines the entry state so a freshly-displayed/top-layer element animates in (the 'materialize by modulating light-bending' analog); registered `@property` typed customs (`--specular-x/y/intensity`, and crucially a registered `--glass-refract-scale <number>`) make custom-property VALUES interpolable so the lens can spring open. glass-ui registers the specular trio but NOT the refraction scale — registering it is the unlock for a springy 'lens materializes' entry.

Spring physics over duration easing for the 'alive' feel — great UI motion mimics real-world spring dynamics (nothing appears/disappears instantly), is interruptible mid-flight, runs at 60fps on transform/opacity only, and uses ease-out / <300ms for snappy interactions. The Liquid Glass 'instantly flexes and energizes with light' on touch is a press-spring (scale + light-flare). glass-ui has the spring runtime (keyframes.js, useSpring*, `--spring-dock` 0.32,0.7) — AX.W05 converges the vocabulary onto ONE iOS-spring.
notes.applicability: "GLASS PRIMITIVES (AX.W09/W20): The single biggest, lowest-risk win is the AX.W09 specular retune AT THE ONE SOURCE (glass.css .glass-material::before). The code today paints `hsl(40 30% 100% / 0.55)` — pure white, directly contradicting its own 'warm-cream' comment and matching the SOTA 'never pure-white' rule's anti-pattern; rest floor is 0.35 not 0 (the @property initial is already 0). Fix: warm-cream low-alpha core (~hsl(40 40% 96%)) at rest~0.08 / hover~0.22 / active~0.32, tokenized as `--glass-specular-intensity-{rest,hover,active}`, and lift the duplicated trackSpecular pointer-write (Card.vue + DockIconButton.vue, verbatim) into `useSpecularTracking()`. This is a 4-line retune + tokenize that beats the consumer-visible blowout. REFRACTION UPGRADE (extends AW.W23's shipped `#glass-refract`): the current filter is a single-pass crude radial-gradient displacement map — upgrade it to (a) a Snell-derived squircle NORMAL map (the profile is already cited in the comment but not computed) and (b) THREE-channel chromatic aberration (R/G/B staggered scale + feColorMatrix isolate + feBlend screen) for the prismatic edge that is the 'thick glass' tell. Keep it @supports-gated PE-only over the blur base (Chromium-only, feDisplacementMap is resize-expensive). Register `--glass-refract-scale` as a typed @property so the lens scale can spring. DOCK (AX.W01-06): the dock is the headline morph surface. The research validates AX.W01's core decision — RETIRE the View-Transitions collapse fork (VT crossfades rasterized pixels, the wrong primitive for a layout morph; Emil/Apple both say layout morphs want continuous physical springs) and drive EVERY axis (width/inline-size, padding, radius, AND the material's `--glass-refract-scale` + specular intensity) from ONE analytic-spring scalar `--dock-morph-t` on ONE rAF clock. interpolate-size/calc-size is the progressive-enhancement that kills the `width:auto` non-interpolation GlassDock.vue already complains about (Chromium-only → keep the spring as the cross-browser primary). The dock's SECOND specular (the `--glass-highlight` hover box-shadow stacking on the moving `::before`) is the worst blowout on the most-hovered surface — AX.W09 retires it. THE UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY (path forward): Apple's GlassEffectContainer smin-merge IS glass-ui's GooBlob smin SDF — the convergence is to express 'every UI element morphs/springs/blends' as ONE facility: a single spring scalar per morph-group writes a typed custom property that drives box geometry + material optics (refract scale, specular intensity) + child stagger in the SAME paint, and proximity-blending between sibling glass surfaces reuses the blob's smooth-min union. The three web primitives that compose this — registered @property (interpolable material values), View Transitions (shared-element route-morph, KEPT for page transitions per AX.W01), and spring-driven CSS customs (the collapse morph) — are all already in the tree; the work is unifying them onto one clock and one vocabulary (AX.W05's single iOS-spring)."
pitfalls: backdrop-filter: url(#svg-filter) is CHROMIUM-ONLY (WebKit bug 245510 open, Firefox not shipping) — the refraction MUST sit behind @supports(backdrop-filter: url(#...)) with a clean blur-only fallback, never a broken url() ref. glass-ui already does this; any chromatic-aberration upgrade must preserve the gate.

feDisplacementMap is RASTERIZATION-HEAVY — simultaneous backdrop blur + pixel-shifting displacement is intensive GPU work that tanks INP. Isolate filtered nodes with `contain: strict` (or layout/paint), keep their physical viewport dimensions SMALL, and NEVER promote refraction to the card/primitive substrate — keep it PE-only garnish on the dock/floating tier. Only the `scale` attr animates cheaply; shape/size changes force a full map rebuild.

Pure-white specular at high alpha = the exact blowout glass-ui ships today (0.55 white, 0.35 rest). The SOTA rule is warm-cream + low-alpha + a true ~0 rest floor; a non-zero rest floor on every band surface (the AW.W22 blast-radius promotion) makes static unwired plates glow. Co-update the gate (proof-glass-material-unified.mjs hardcodes 0.6/0.85) or the retune lands RED.

View Transitions crossfade RASTERIZED PIXELS — using VT for the dock's own collapse produces a fade between two bitmaps, not a continuous geometry morph; box leads content by ~16ms (nextTick→rAF→reflow). Reserve VT for page/route shared-element morphs; use a single analytic spring for the dock collapse (the AX.W01 decision, research-confirmed). keyframes already device-proved the dock morph is NOT reliably live-measurable via getBoundingClientRect under VT.

Duplicate view-transition-name DROPS the morph silently — two docks co-mounted with the same `glass-dock-1` name kill the route-morph (a named regression fixture is needed). Registered @property is required for custom-prop interpolation: a bare unregistered var() in an hsl() alpha computes to 0 in Chromium (glass-ui already hit this — it drives opacity, not per-stop alpha, as a workaround).

interpolate-size / calc-size() are NOT Baseline (Chromium-only, Chrome/Edge 129+) — do not make the morph DEPEND on them; they are a progressive sweetener over the spring/FLIP primary. Same for backdrop-filter url() chromatic aberration — it's a Chromium-only garnish, the warm-cream specular + edge rim + under-shadow must carry the look everywhere.

A11y is mandatory, not optional: prefers-reduced-motion must pin the specular STATIC (glass-ui does, in glass-specular-track.css), prefers-reduced-transparency drops the catch-light and maps blur→none (glass-ui does), and the displacement/refraction garnish should also degrade under reduced-transparency. The WebGL substrate's PRM freeze is separate; the CSS material must self-guard.

Refraction filter region defaults to ~10% beyond the element — insufficient for large displacement scales, causing edge clipping/misalignment; the filter must extend its region (x/y/width/height) to accommodate the displacement range, and the host SVG must be width:0/height:0 (NOT display:none, which breaks same-document filter refs). SVG filters also require same-document refs — Shadow DOM breaks them.

notes.facet: Liquid-glass INTERACTION feedback — touch squish, the elastic press, the fluid hover/active response, the rubber-band
sotaTechniques: SPRING WITH VELOCITY-CONTINUITY RETARGETING (the canonical iOS mechanism). Apple's spring is parameterized as (response, dampingFraction) or the equivalent (duration, bounce); mass=1, stiffness=(2π/response)², damping derived from ζ. The decisive property: when a running spring is RETARGETED (e.g. press→release before the press settled), it seeds the new spring with the velocity it had at the moment of interruption — so the motion never 'jerks to a halt' the way a re-run cubic-bezier does. WWDC23 §10158: 'springs are the only animation that maintains continuity both for static cases and cases with initial velocity.' This is the difference between a press that feels alive and one that feels mechanical.

INSTANT FEEDBACK ON TOUCH-DOWN, SPRING ONLY ON RELEASE (Building Fluid Interfaces / Apple Calculator). The pressed visual (highlight/scale-in) applies IMMEDIATELY on pointerdown with no spring lag (under the ~100ms perception threshold the press reads as 'instant'); the spring physics governs the RELEASE/settle back to rest. Color/highlight = instant; geometry settle = spring. This split is why iOS taps feel crisp yet bouncy.

ELASTIC PRESS / TOUCH-SQUISH SCALE-DOWN (the press register). The element scales toward ~0.96 on active with overshoot on the rebound. Apple's WWDC23 named springs: smooth (bounce 0, gentle settle), snappy (~bounce 0.15, brisk tail), bouncy (~bounce 0.30, noticeable overshoot); bounce>0.4 reads as 'too exaggerated for a UI element'. glass-ui already mirrors these exactly: --spring-smooth(0.50/ζ0.86), --spring-snappy(0.35/ζ0.65 ~+6.8%), --spring-bouncy(0.50/ζ0.45 ~+20.5%), --spring-dock(0.32/ζ0.70 ~+4.6%), and --scale-press 0.96 / --scale-press-btn 0.97.

RUBBER-BAND / NON-LINEAR RESISTANCE (Bas Ording's original iOS scroll-bounce, generalized). Past a boundary, displacement is damped by a power curve — offset = pow(rawOffset, ~0.7) — so motion lessens the further you push, communicating 'this is the edge / this is invalid' while staying responsive. Applies to over-drag on a dock-collapse gesture, an at-limit slider thumb, a swipe-to-dismiss past its travel.

LIQUID-GLASS 'FLEX + ENERGIZE WITH LIGHT' ON INTERACTION (WWDC25 Liquid Glass). The material 'instantly flexes and energizes with light' on touch — gel-like flexibility, the surface morphs/illuminates/refracts in tandem with the gesture rather than just dimming. The interaction lifts a specular highlight + brightens the lens at the touch point. Concretely on web: on active, raise the specular::before opacity + warm the glass tint + scale, all on ONE spring clock so light and geometry move together.

POINTER-TRACKED SPECULAR / LENSING (Rauno 'invisible details' + kube.io refraction). The highlight or lens center tracks the pointer position (a --px/--py custom-property fed from pointermove), so hover reads as light raking across glass, and on press the lens warps toward the contact point. kube.io: glass refraction via SVG feDisplacementMap; the cheap reactive axis is animating the filter `scale` (no map rebuild). Chrome-only for SVG-as-backdrop-filter today.

IMMEDIATE SCALE-DELTA BEFORE THRESHOLD (Rauno). On a drag/long-press the element should feel the scale delta applying continuously from frame 1, THEN snap past a threshold — not wait for the threshold to give any affordance. Zero pre-threshold feedback reads as 'the interface didn't understand my input.'

FORCE/PROGRESS-PROPORTIONAL SCALING (Building Fluid Interfaces flashlight button). scale = 1 + (max-1)*force — the visual responds proportionally to a continuous input (3D-touch force on iOS; on web, drag distance or hold-duration). A held control can GROW/intensify proportional to hold time rather than a binary on/off.

TRANSFORM-ORIGIN / SPATIAL-ORIGIN AWARENESS (Rauno + Emil). Scale and entrance animate FROM the spatial origin of the gesture — a menu grows from the button that spawned it (transform-origin at the trigger), an app from its icon. Origin-correct scaling is what makes a morph read as 'this came from there' instead of 'this popped from nowhere'.

CSS linear() SPRING FOR THE FIRE-AND-FORGET CASE, JS SPRING FOR THE INTERRUPTIBLE CASE (Josh Comeau + Chrome docs). linear() reproduces a spring curve in pure CSS (~40 stops, ~1.3kB for 3 springs, zero fps cost) — but it is a FIXED curve: on interrupt it 'turns around as if it hit a wall' and CSS's reversing-shortening-factor speeds the reversal unnaturally. So: discrete one-shot state transitions (hover-in, entrance) ride linear() tokens; live/interruptible/gesture-driven motion (press-while-settling, drag) needs a real JS integrator that carries velocity.

WEB-PLATFORM ENTRANCE/SIZE PRIMITIVES (2025 baseline). @starting-style + transition-behavior:allow-discrete (Baseline 2024) animate an element from display:none — the entry 'pop'. interpolate-size:allow-keywords animates width/height to/from intrinsic sizes (auto/max-content) — directly relevant to a dock morphing to fit content (NOT yet Baseline; Chromium-only). View Transitions for cross-state morphs. These are the declarative substrate the morph facility should prefer where supported, with the JS spring as the interruptible fallback.

HIGH-FREQUENCY SUPPRESSION + KEYBOARD-NEVER-ANIMATE (Rauno + Emil). Controls hit hundreds of times a day (command menu, keyboard-driven nav) should NOT animate — the same animation on the 100th invocation is cognitive burden and feels slow. Press-squish springs are POINTER-only; keyboard/discrete activations stay on an instant or short non-spring curve.

GESTURE INTENT: PEEK-VS-COMMIT, INTERRUPTIBLE, MOMENTUM-PRESERVING (Rauno + Building Fluid Interfaces). Lightweight reveals fire mid-gesture after a distance; destructive commits require gesture-END. Throws preserve momentum + angle (never perfectly centered). Every in-flight animation must be re-grabbable mid-flight (the App Switcher vs Settings contrast) — interruptibility is the headline property, not a nicety.
notes.applicability:
"glass-ui is unusually well-positioned — the spring substrate already matches the SOTA model. WHAT'S ALREADY RIGHT: useSpring/useSpringPress wrap keyframes.js SpringProgress (a real second-order ODE integrator) and seed initialVelocity, so the velocity-continuity retargeting that WWDC23 calls the headline property is already available — useSpringPress is the canonical touch-squish primitive (response 0.25, ζ0.7, ~5% overshoot, 0→1 → scale(1 - v*0.05)). The --spring-* token cohort is a 1:1 mirror of Apple's smooth/snappy/bouncy presets, generated from the same physics via springLinearStops(); --scale-press 0.96 / --scale-press-btn 0.97 ARE the iOS press values; --scale-press-dock was just unified onto 0.96 (AT.W7). useSpringPress(handlers: pointerdown/up/cancel/leave) already encodes 'release/cancel/leave all spring back', and the precept that keyboard rides --motion-ease-apple (non-spring) already encodes the keyboard-never-animate rule.

WHERE THE GAP IS — TWO MOTION SYSTEMS THAT DON'T MEET. The PRIMITIVES use CSS-only motion: .glass-btn:active{scale:var(--scale-press)} with `transition: scale --duration-normal --spring-snappy`, and dock controls use the same CSS-spring pattern. These are FIXED linear() curves — exactly the case Comeau warns about: a press released mid-settle reverses 'as if it hit a wall' and CSS's shortening-factor accelerates the reversal unnaturally. The JS spring (useSpringPress) that WOULD give velocity-continuity is NOT wired into Button/Card/DockIconButton/glass-btn; it sits as an unbound composable. So the system has the right engine and the right tokens but the interactive primitives don't run on the engine — they run on the lossy CSS approximation.

THE PATH FORWARD — THE UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY. AX.W01's headline (single-scalar analytic-spring → --dock-morph-t → every axis on ONE clock, retire the VT fork, re-derive useLayerTransition from the live ODE) IS the iOS model applied to the dock box; AX.W05 governs ONE spring vocabulary (excise --ease-apple-spring, re-point 5 internal + 4 speedtest consumers onto --spring-*). EXTEND that same single-scalar discipline DOWN to the interaction layer so press/hover/active are the SAME facility as the box morph, not a parallel CSS path:
  (1) A useGlassPress (or extend useSpringPress) that drives a --press-t scalar [0..1] per interactive primitive, off which scale (1 - press*Δ), specular-opacity, tint-warmth, and lens-displacement ALL interpolate via calc() — the AX.W01 single-scalar pattern at the atom scale. One clock, velocity-continuous, interruptible, so a press-while-hover-while-collapse reads as ONE continuous spring (the AX.W01 'reads as one continuous iOS spring' bar, extended to atoms).
  (2) Instant-down / spring-up split: highlight + tint flip on pointerdown with NO spring (under 100ms), geometry settles on release via the spring — codify in the press primitive.
  (3) Pointer-tracked specular: feed --px/--py from pointermove into the existing glass-specular-track::before so hover rakes light and press warps the lens toward contact (composes with AX.W09's useSpecularTracking + tokenized intensity ladder — wire it to the press scalar too, not just hover).
  (4) Rubber-band token: a shared pow(~0.7) resistance helper for over-drag (dock over-collapse, slider at-limit) — currently absent.
  (5) Layering: linear() tokens stay the substrate for discrete one-shots (hover-in entrance, @starting-style pop); the JS spring scalar owns anything live/interruptible/gesture-driven. interpolate-size is the declarative win for the content-driven dock wrap (AX.W04) where supported, JS spring as fallback. This gives EVERY element (AX's iOS-26 goal) the morph/squish/flex facility from one governed engine + one token vocabulary."
pitfalls: CSS linear()/transition springs are NOT interruptible — a press released mid-settle reverses 'as if it hit a wall' and CSS's reversing-shortening-factor speeds the reversal unnaturally (Comeau). This is the single biggest gap: glass-ui's interactive primitives (.glass-btn:active, dock controls) use CSS-spring transitions, so they LOSE the velocity-continuity the JS engine already provides. Don't ship the morph facility on CSS transitions for anything a user can interrupt.

Animating the WRONG properties costs frames. Stay on transform/scale/opacity (compositor-only); never spring padding/width/margin/border-radius for the per-frame interaction layer (layout thrash). Note AX.W01 deliberately drives --dock-morph-t through calc() onto layout props for the BOX morph — that's a once-per-frame custom-prop write, acceptable for the box, but the per-element press squish must stay transform/opacity.

View Transitions are the WRONG primitive for a layout morph — VT crossfades RASTERIZED pixels and desyncs against an animating ancestor (the exact AX.W01 finding: the dock-collapse VT fork is retired). Do not reach for VT for press/squish/flex; use the live scalar. (Preserve the per-instance view-transition-name route-morph seam fourier depends on — a separable concern.)

Springs spend most of their time NEAR the target, so users think the animation finished and re-press — making interruptibility mandatory, not optional (WWDC14/Building Fluid Interfaces). A press primitive that isn't re-grabbable mid-settle will feel broken on rapid taps.

prefers-reduced-motion must strip the SQUISH/overshoot but KEEP a fade/instant state-change — useSpring already honors PRM (snaps to target). But note the CSS-side hazard already documented in dock.css: under PRM the global gate strips `scale` from transition-property, so the hover scale SNAPS (0 morph frames) — verify the unified facility degrades to a clean instant state, not a broken/janky partial.

Pointer-tracked specular + SVG displacement lensing is Chrome-ONLY today (SVG filter as backdrop-filter unsupported in Safari/Firefox — kube.io), and dynamic shape/size changes force a full displacement-map rebuild (only animating filter `scale` is cheap). Treat reactive lensing as progressive enhancement; the press scalar + specular-opacity path is the cross-browser baseline.

interpolate-size:allow-keywords (animate to/from auto/intrinsic) is NOT Baseline — Chromium-only. The content-driven dock wrap (AX.W04) can't rely on it cross-browser; keep the JS spring / measured-size fallback.

Keyboard/discrete activations must NOT get the pointer squish — double-fire risk (the tap-press + focus path firing together, noted in useSpringPress X4 §5 risk 5) and the high-frequency cognitive-burden rule (Rauno/Emil). Press-squish stays pointer-anchored; keyboard rides the non-spring curve.

Don't mint dead spring presets — AX.W05 adds a consumer-coverage assertion (fail-closed on a zero-consumer --spring-*). A unified facility must reuse the governed register (--spring-dock for the dock-and-its-children, snappy/smooth/bouncy elsewhere), not spawn new curves.

Over-bouncy reads as toy-like: WWDC23 caps UI bounce at ~0.4; glass-ui's --spring-bouncy (~+20.5%) is already at the upper edge — reserve it for celebratory one-shots, use the snappy/dock register (~+4.6–6.8%) for press/active so the feedback feels crisp, not wobbly.

stacking-context flicker: scaling on hover/press can mint a stacking context mid-animation and flicker z-index/anchor positioning. glass-ui already guards this (.glass-btn sets `scale:1` at rest to mint the context once) — the unified facility must keep that rest-identity so the scalar interpolation never flickers the layer into being.

notes.facet: View Transitions API (2025) for MORPHING — view-transition-name + the group/old/new pseudo-element tree, same-document + cross-document, applied to glass-ui dock / animation / glass primitives
sotaTechniques: NAMED-ELEMENT MORPH (the core primitive): set the same `view-transition-name` on an element in the old and new DOM state and the browser captures it as an independent ::view-transition-group and interpolates position/size/opacity between the two snapshots — this is the ONE shared-element morph the whole API is built on, and the rest are styling/scoping hooks over it. Baseline Newly Available (same-document) since Firefox 144, Oct 2025.

THE PSEUDO-ELEMENT TREE: a transition mints ::view-transition (overlay root, above all page content) → per name ::view-transition-group(name) (the morph container that tweens transform+width+height) → ::view-transition-image-pair(name) → ::view-transition-old(name) (old snapshot, opacity 1→0) + ::view-transition-new(name) (new snapshot, opacity 0→1). You author the morph by styling these pseudos (animation-duration/-timing-function on the -group; animation-name on -old/-new for custom enter/exit). glass-ui already does this in view-transition.css.

view-transition-class (Chrome 137 / FF 144 / Safari 18.4 — Baseline Newly Available): tag many elements with one CLASS and style `::view-transition-group(.cls)` once instead of minting a unique selector per name — the N-items-one-recipe lever. glass-ui already ships `.gl-list-item` and `.gl-dock-layer` group classes on exactly this mechanism.

TYPED / DIRECTIONAL transitions (Chrome 140+): pass `{ update, types: [...] }` to startViewTransition and select with `:active-view-transition-type(name)` to author asymmetric curves (snappier collapse, softer expand-overshoot — the iOS-feel asymmetry). glass-ui already implements this: `useViewTransition` accepts `{ types }` and view-transition.css authors `dock-expand`/`dock-collapse`/`layer-forward`/`layer-back`.

match-element auto-naming (Chrome 137 / FF 144 / Safari 18.4): `view-transition-name: match-element` lets the browser auto-generate a stable per-element name from element identity, so you no longer hand-mint a unique custom-ident per list row — eliminates the duplicate-name footgun for dynamic collections.

NESTED VIEW-TRANSITION GROUPS via the `view-transition-group` CSS property (Chrome 140+): re-parent a captured group UNDER another captured group so the DOM hierarchy is restored during the transition — this is what enables clipping and 3D/parent-transform to apply to a child morph (e.g. a dock control morphing while its parent dock pill simultaneously resizes and clips it). Plus pseudo-element animation INHERITANCE (Chrome 140+): -old/-new now inherit animation longhands from their -group parent, so one curve on the group cascades to the snapshot pair.

SCOPED / element-level transitions via `element.startViewTransition()` (Chrome 140 behind flag, ~Chrome 147 stable): run a view transition over a SUBTREE with independent pointer handling and its own overlay, instead of freezing the whole document — the right shape for animating ONE dock or ONE panel without pausing the rest of the page (today the document-level call pauses all rendering for the snapshot).

CROSS-DOCUMENT (MPA) ROUTE MORPH via the `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` at-rule (Chrome 126+; FF/Safari ignore it and snap): same-origin navigations morph any element sharing a `view-transition-name` across pages — a persistent dock/header that stays put while the route changes. This is exactly the seam the AX charter PRESERVES: fourier route-morphs the dock via its per-instance `view-transition-name: glass-dock-${useId()}` even though the dock's OWN collapse VT is being retired.

iOS-26 LIQUID-GLASS MORPH (the native reference): SwiftUI's `GlassEffectContainer` + `glassEffect()` + `glassEffectID(_, in: namespace)` make glass surfaces with matching IDs fluidly merge/split; a `spacing` parameter is a MORPHING THRESHOLD — elements within that distance visually blend (gel-like) before separating, and `glassEffectUnion` forces a single shape across gaps. The web analogue is not VT (VT crossfades rasterized snapshots, no real fusion) but the GOOEY/METABALL SVG filter: feGaussianBlur to bleed neighboring shapes together then feColorMatrix (or contrast()) to re-threshold the alpha so they read as one merging mass — the technique for the blend, with VT/FLIP for the position morph.

CSS MORPH ADJACENCIES that do real LAYOUT morphing (the non-snapshot path VT is NOT): `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` + `calc-size()` to animate to/from `auto`/`min-content` (Chrome 129+ only — NOT baseline, no FF/Safari); `@starting-style` + `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` + `overlay` for native top-layer enter/exit (Widely/Newly Available — glass-ui already ships this as `.glass-top-layer` in animations.css); and a single analytic SPRING scalar written to a CSS custom property driving `calc()` on every axis in ONE paint — the FLIP-replacement the AX W01 dock rebuild standardizes on.
notes.applicability: "DECISIVE ARCHITECTURAL FINDING — the AX charter ALREADY made the right call and this research corroborates it. AX.W01 (docs/tranches/AX/AX.md:287-340) RETIRES the View-Transitions fork for the dock COLLAPSE entirely, replacing it with ONE analytic spring scalar `--dock-morph-t` written once per frame to the `.glass-dock` root, with every axis (inline-size, padding, radius, scale, color, child-stagger) expressed as `calc()` off that scalar in the same paint. The web platform pitfalls below confirm WHY: VT snapshots are RASTERIZED images that keep their aspect ratio while the group box resizes, so a continuous width/padding layout morph distorts and reads as a crossfade of two stale frames, not a fluid resize — VT is the wrong primitive for the dock's own collapse. The single-spring path is what iOS actually does (interruptible physics, one clock) and what Emil-Kowalski-school practice prescribes (transform/opacity-or-size on a spring, sub-300ms, interruptible). PATH FORWARD for the unified morph facility, by layer: (1) DOCK COLLAPSE + LAYER SWAP (W01/W02): one `useLayerTransition` rebuilt from first principles (479→~130 lines per W01) driving the box on a single SpringProgress scalar — DELETE the NATIVE_VT fork in useLayerTransition.ts:108 and the VT branch at :119; keep the clip-reveal aperture; export `useLayerTransition` on the `/dock` barrel so value.js deletes its fork (substrate-with-consumer). (2) PRESERVE the per-instance `view-transition-name: glass-dock-${useId()}` seam + `proof:vt-names` for the CROSS-COMPONENT/ROUTE morph (fourier's viz↔workspace geometry-morph) — this is a SEPARABLE concern the prior charter conflated; the name lives for the page transition, NOT the collapse. Retain `useViewTransition`/`view-transition.css` as the morph substrate for THIS, not the dock collapse. (3) The unified `useViewTransition` (already shipped on `/motion-core`, dependency-free, instant fallback, `types` directional support, PRM-via-CSS) is the CORRECT facility for SHARED-ELEMENT/ROUTE/LIST-REORDER morphs across the library — keep and lean on it for `.gl-list-item` reorders, dialog-from-trigger morphs, tab-content swaps, and route morphs; it is NOT the engine for an element's OWN continuous resize (that is the spring). (4) GLASS PRIMITIVES (W09/W20): the Liquid-Glass MERGE/blend (two glass pills fusing as one) is the gooey SVG-filter (feGaussianBlur+feColorMatrix threshold) over the `.glass-material` substrate, NOT VT — but W20 RETIRES the JS `createGlassFilter`/`useGlassRenderer` SVG-displacement path onto CSS-native `.glass-material`, so any merge-blend must be a tokenized CSS/SVG-filter recipe, not a per-frame JS renderer. (5) DOC the decision boundary in the README: VT/`view-transition-name` = SHARED-ELEMENT + ROUTE morph (one element becomes/relocates to another, position+opacity interpolation of snapshots); analytic SPRING + `--*-morph-t` calc = an element's OWN continuous box morph (collapse/expand/resize); gooey SVG filter = surface FUSION (the Liquid-Glass blend). One sentence per primitive, with the 'snapshot crossfade ≠ layout morph' rule front and center."
pitfalls: VT IS A SNAPSHOT CROSSFADE, NOT A LAYOUT-MORPH ENGINE: the captured ::view-transition-old is a rasterized image; while the ::view-transition-group box tweens to the new size the old/new images keep their own aspect ratio and just crossfade — so a continuous width/padding resize (the dock collapse) DISTORTS and reads as two stale frames blending, never as a fluid box resize. This is the exact 'uncaptured-animating-ancestor desync' AX.W01 cites and the reason to retire the dock-collapse VT fork.

SINGLE-NAME-PER-STATE IS A HARD RULE: two rendered elements sharing one `view-transition-name` in the same state SKIP/DROP the entire transition silently (no error). The fourier two-dock co-mount where CanvasControlsDock + EditorControlsDock both minted `glass-dock-1` dropped the morph snapshot and reddened ~13 e2e — the concrete witness. Mint per-instance names (`useId()`), or use `match-element` auto-naming for dynamic collections.

THE DOM CALLBACK MUST BE SYNCHRONOUS: startViewTransition(cb) captures the OLD state, runs cb to mutate the DOM, then captures the NEW state — cb must apply the change synchronously (no await of layout). glass-ui's `useViewTransition` enforces this; an async mutate captures a wrong 'new' frame.

DOCUMENT-LEVEL VT PAUSES ALL RENDERING during the snapshot+animation, and runs only ONE transition at a time (concurrent transitions on different subtrees are not yet shipped except behind the Chrome 140 scoped-VT flag) — so animating one dock with document.startViewTransition freezes the whole page; prefer the spring for an element's own motion and reserve VT for genuine shared-element/route morphs, or adopt element-scoped VT when it ships stable (~Chrome 147).

CONTAINMENT + ANCESTOR TRANSFORMS: a captured element needs layout/paint containment and must not sit under an animating, non-captured ancestor or the snapshot geometry is wrong (glitches/jumps). Nested view-transition-group (Chrome 140+) is the fix for wanting parent clip/transform to apply — but it is Chrome-140-only, so don't depend on it for baseline.

BASELINE IS UNEVEN — gate everything: same-document VT + view-transition-class + match-element are Baseline Newly Available (FF 144, Oct 2025); but `types`/`:active-view-transition-type`, nested groups, pseudo inheritance, scoped element VT are Chrome-140+ ONLY; cross-document `@view-transition` animates only in Chromium (FF/Safari snap); `interpolate-size`/`calc-size()` is Chrome-129+ ONLY (no FF/Safari). glass-ui's pattern is correct: feature-detect (`supportsViewTransitions()`), provide an instant synchronous fallback, and put PRM `animation:none` on the pseudos in CSS — never assume the morph ran.

WILL-CHANGE + COMPOSITOR COST: do NOT leave a standing `will-change` or a permanent `view-transition-name` on idle elements — both pin a compositor layer/VRAM. glass-ui already does on-demand will-change in useLayerTransition (set just before the spring drives, cleared on settle); apply the same discipline to any VT-named element (name it only around the transition window for route morphs).

REDUCED MOTION: the swap must still happen (state mutates) but motion must zero. glass-ui's view-transition.css zeros `animation` on all three pseudo families under PRM — correct; replicate for any new VT recipe and never hide the state change behind the animation.

VT ≠ LIQUID-GLASS FUSION: VT cannot make two glass surfaces physically merge/blend (it crossfades snapshots). The iOS-26 GlassEffectContainer gel-merge has NO direct web equivalent; the only web approximation is the gooey SVG filter (blur→threshold) for the blend plus a spring/FLIP for position — don't promise a true framebuffer-refraction merge from VT.

notes.facet: FLIP + single normalized spring-progress scalar driving the whole box — one clock, every axis off calc() (the W01 --dock-morph-t approach)
sotaTechniques: ONE-SCALAR-DRIVES-ALL via @property-registered number + calc(): register --dock-morph-t as @property{syntax:'<number>';inherits:false} and express EVERY axis as calc() off it (width/padding/radius/scale/shadow-alpha/bg-mix/per-child opacity). The scalar is the only thing that moves; structurally one clock, zero cross-axis lead/lag. Registered props interpolate composited off the main thread. This IS the W01 mechanism and the CSS expression of iOS-26's morph-one-shape-into-another.

iOS-INTERRUPTIBLE ANALYTIC SPRING as the clock: the JS SpringProgress (keyframes.js, wrapped by useSpring.ts) writes the scalar 0->1 per rAF. Decisive iOS property is velocity-continuity: a re-toggle mid-flight re-seats the SAME solver's target from live (value,velocity) (the existing AV.W9.2 retarget). linear() CANNOT (Comeau: reversing-shortening-factor, 'turns around as though it hit a wall'). JS spring drives the morph; linear() stays for discrete micro-interactions.

linear() SPRING TOKENS as the analytic bridge (already shipped): regen-spring-tokens.mjs samples the SAME ODE SpringProgress integrates, emitting --spring-dock etc. as 48-stop linear() arrays. Bit-identical motion between CSS-transition surfaces and the JS driver (one ODE source: response 0.32, zeta 0.7, +4.6% overshoot). ~1.3kB/3 springs, no framerate cost.

FLIP measured ONCE per morph, not per axis: capture start, apply end, read end, drive one normalized progress; no mid-animation reflow since only the registered scalar + composited transforms change. Correction: one FLIP, one box, one scalar; the legacy bug is two FLIP instances (.dock-layers + .dock-layer-stack) each forking a clock. Collapse to one orchestrator: active layer = expandedState x activePane (W02).

RETIRE View-Transitions as the morph primitive: VT snapshots are rasterized (::view-transition-old keeps its ratio while resizing) and don't capture an animating ancestor (the box-leads-content desync). VT is right only for discrete route/page morphs of distinct NAMED elements. Kill the dock-COLLAPSE VT fork; keep the per-instance view-transition-name route-morph seam (fourier).

interpolate-size / calc-size() KNOWN-BAD as a second driver (our AV.W9.0): it lets CSS transition to intrinsic sizes but is Chromium-only (129+) AND second-driving the dock width alongside the JS spring FROZE the dock. Do NOT use on the morph axis; viable only standalone for a simple height-auto reveal the spring doesn't touch.

CONCENTRIC RADIUS morph (W04): inner=outer-padding keeps nested corners concentric as the box morphs; both radii off --dock-morph-t so pill(stadium)->card(finite) glides with width. iOS-26 uses squircles (superellipse(2)); arriving web primitive is corner-shape:squircle as progressive enhancement over border-radius.

GlassEffectContainer / gooey-merge material layer (iOS-26 shapes blend+re-absorb): feGaussianBlur bleeds neighbour shapes, feColorMatrix snaps alpha contrast to a single fluid mass, then they part. Web analogue for dock icons coalescing into the pill on collapse. The feColorMatrix trick degrades to plain blur in Firefox -> enhancement only, never load-bearing.

MATERIAL-RESPONDS-TO-MORPH (iOS-26 thicker glass when larger): drive shadow-alpha, blur, specular-intensity, border-light off the SAME scalar so the expanded card reads thicker than the collapsed pill. glass-ui already has the moving-specular ::before + registered --specular-* props (glass.css); tie intensity to morph progress (W09).

ONE MOTION VOCABULARY (W05): excise --ease-apple-spring cubic-bezier(0.175,0.885,0.32,1.275) (+27.5% bezier-approx overshoot); re-point consumers onto --spring-dock / the JS spring so dock+aurora+blob+primitives share one register. A bezier can't encode true spring settle the sampled ODE does.

SPRING-KEYED CHILD STAGGER off the same scalar: each child's opacity onset is a clamp() threshold against --dock-morph-t (offset = index x --dock-stagger-step), so the cascade rides the physical morph and survives an interrupt with no orphaned timers. glass-ui already does this via --dock-morph-progress; fold the hand-typed 0.08/0.16 ladder onto one token x nth-child.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD, grounded in source. W01 CORE: replace the VT-vs-FLIP fork in src/components/custom/dock/composables/useLayerTransition.ts (479 lines, two engines) with a ~130-line single driver: one SpringProgress (response 0.32, zeta 0.7 = DOCK_SPRING) writes a normalized 0->1 to --dock-morph-t on the .glass-dock root per frame, NOT pixel-space width (today's per-frame width:${w}px is one JS-owned axis and the box-leads-content source). Register --dock-morph-t via @property{syntax:'<number>';inherits:false}. Delete NATIVE_VT, startViewTransition, directionTypes, the pin/measure/clearDim pixel dance; keep FLIP-measure-once + spring + scalar-write + AV.W9.2 retarget. dock.css ALREADY transitions padding/radius/scale/bg/border on --dock-motion-resize and writes --dock-morph-progress, but on a SEPARATE clock from the JS width spring (the desync) -> convert each to calc(... * var(--dock-morph-t)); keep the [data-morphing] clip-reveal aperture. WIDTH off two measured extents (--dock-collapsed-w/--dock-expanded-w) x the scalar, no per-frame el.style.width (the AV.W9.0 freeze). W02: nested DockLayerGroup defers to the one orchestrator (active=expanded x pane). W03: useDockHold feeds held as a synchronous morph-state edge. W04: concentric inner=outer-padding radius off the scalar; one radius token; drop interpolate-size on the morph axis. W09: tie --specular-intensity + shadow-alpha + blur to the scalar. Re-export useLayerTransition on /dock so value.js deletes its fork. Gate proof:dock-animation-live (box geom + child opacity on one rAF, onset <=1 frame) passes by construction since every axis is a function of one value sampled once per frame.
pitfalls: TWO AUTHORITIES ON ONE AXIS is the recurring killer (AV.W9.0 PROVED it: interpolate-size second-driving width alongside the JS spring FROZE the dock). One driver per length; never also write el.style.width per frame.

DRIVING WIDTH IN PIXEL SPACE (today's bug) couples the driver to one axis and defers it a frame behind the CSS-transition'd padding/radius (box leads content ~16ms). Write a UNITLESS scalar; let calc() compute every length in the same paint.
UNREGISTERED custom properties do NOT interpolate and run on the main thread; --dock-morph-t MUST be @property-registered as <number> to interpolate composited.

VIEW-TRANSITIONS rasterize the box (::view-transition-old keeps its aspect ratio while resizing) and can't capture an animating ancestor. Retiring the COLLAPSE VT must NOT remove the per-instance view-transition-name route seam (fourier's J+K path + proof:vt-names); two co-mounted docks minting the same name DROP the snapshot and red ~13 e2e.

linear() spring tokens CANNOT do velocity-continuity (reversing-shortening-factor, turns around as though it hit a wall) -> never drive the interruptible morph; only the live JS solver re-seats from (value,velocity).
calc-size()/interpolate-size is Chromium-only (129+, no Safari/Firefox); the gooey feColorMatrix merge degrades to plain blur in Firefox -> neither is load-bearing on the geometric morph.

INHERITANCE BOMB: animating an INHERITED custom prop (--phase-color/--shadow-color) per frame forces a whole-subtree recalc; --dock-morph-t must be inherits:false and color shifts route through discrete class swaps (useLayerTransition F5).
STANDING will-change holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an idle dock; promote only for the gesture, clear to auto on settle (preserve the AV.W7 F3 lifecycle).
MULTIPLE FLIP INSTANCES per dock double-animate the same pixels on a simultaneous collapse+swap; one orchestrator per dock, measured once (W02).

FIXED-MS STAGGER TIMERS orphan on interrupt; key the stagger off --dock-morph-t via clamp() so a retarget carries the cascade. Clamp progress to [0,1] so the +4.6% overshoot doesn't push child onset past full reveal.
OVERSHOOT BUDGET: --spring-dock is +4.6% (AW.W2 retune off +18.5%); the single-scalar morph must compose with it with no re-bounce. Excise the +27.5% --ease-apple-spring bezier (W05), don't layer it.

notes.facet: CSS interpolate-size + calc-size() (2025) — animating to/from auto/intrinsic sizes; the size-morph primitive the dock collapse/expand needs
sotaTechniques: interpolate-size: allow-keywords (the document-level opt-in) — a single inherited property, set once at :root, that flips the engine from its default `numeric-only` (which refuses to interpolate any intrinsic keyword) to allowing a transition/keyframe to run between a <length-percentage> and an intrinsic size (auto, min-content, max-content, fit-content, content for flex-basis). Mechanism: once allowed, the browser resolves the keyword to its used pixel length at both ends and tweens the lengths on its own clock — zero JS measurement, no pin/measure/re-pin. This is the canonical 'animate to height:auto' since Chrome/Edge 129.

calc-size(<basis>, <calc-sum>) — the calculating sibling. `<basis>` is exactly ONE intrinsic keyword (or `any`, or a nested calc-size), and the `size` token in the second arg references that basis's resolved length, so you can do math on an intrinsic size that plain calc() forbids: `width: calc-size(max-content, size + 2rem)` or `calc-size(auto, size)`. Including calc-size() ANYWHERE in a value auto-applies `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` to that element — so it is both the math primitive AND a scoped opt-in. The single-intrinsic-keyword rule (`max-content - min-content` is invalid) keeps layout well-defined.

calc-size(auto, size) as the morph destination — the dock-relevant idiom. Instead of the JS FLIP dance (read getBoundingClientRect, pin px, swap, re-measure, drive a spring in pixel space), the expanded state simply declares `inline-size: calc-size(auto, size)` (or `max-content`) and the collapsed state declares a fixed pill width; a `transition: inline-size <spring-ish-easing>` then morphs auto↔length entirely on the compositor's layout pass. This is the exact capability the dock's `useLayerTransition` hand-rolls in 479 lines.
