@starting-style + interpolate-size for entry morphs — pairing the keyword-interpolation opt-in with @starting-style lets a newly-inserted / popover / top-layer element animate FROM height:0 TO height:auto on first paint with no JS: `.item{height:auto; @starting-style{height:0}}`. This is the disclosure/accordion/dock-layer-reveal pattern as pure declarative CSS, and it composes with the AQ.W5 `.glass-top-layer` @starting-style grammar already in animations.css.

::details-content + interpolate-size — the native bidirectional disclosure morph. Chrome shipped the `::details-content` pseudo so a `<details>`/`<summary>` accordion animates open AND closed to auto height (the open-only limitation of raw interpolate-size on `height` is lifted by animating the content wrapper). Relevant as the accordion/collapsible primitive baseline, distinct from the dock's bespoke morph.

View Transitions API (same-document, 2025) as the SEPARATE morph primitive — `document.startViewTransition()` snapshots before/after and generates a FLIP-style group animation (position+size+rotation) across a DOM mutation. This is the RIGHT primitive for a route/geometry morph between two DIFFERENT layout trees (fourier's viz↔workspace), and the WRONG one for a same-element size morph (it rasterizes pixels → blur, and an uncaptured animating ancestor desyncs). 2025 adds `view-transition-class`, auto-naming `view-transition-name: match-element`, `:active-view-transition-type()` for directional curves, and the `types` overload — all of which glass-ui's useViewTransition already wraps.

interruptible spring as the easing function, not the size driver — Emil Kowalski / Family.co / iOS-26 practice: the value being animated should be a layout size (let CSS/interpolate-size own the geometry) while the MOTION CURVE is a single interruptible spring re-seated from live (value, velocity) on retarget. The SOTA separation is 'one authority owns the size, one analytic spring owns the timing' — which is precisely AX.W01's single-scalar `--dock-morph-t` thesis, and what calc-size() would let you express WITHOUT the per-frame inline-width writes.

iOS-26 Liquid Glass GlassEffectContainer morph model — Apple's controls 'dynamically morph as users need more options', with a container that blends overlapping glass shapes and runs smooth shape/size morphing keyed by a proximity/spacing parameter, plus real-time lensing + specular that track the morph. The web-platform analog is: calc-size()/interpolate-size for the size axis + a single spring scalar driving radius/padding/specular/refraction in lockstep (the unified facility), so the dock pill↔card morph reads as one liquid material rather than independent property tweens.
notes.applicability: DOCK (the headline use): The dock's entire size morph is a hand-rolled FLIP in useLayerTransition.ts (479 lines) precisely BECAUSE width:auto historically would not interpolate — the comments R1+R6 ('the width:auto non-interpolation diagnosed') are the literal motivation. interpolate-size/calc-size() is the native primitive that retires that motivation: the collapsed↔expanded inline-size becomes `calc-size(max-content, size)` (or auto) with a spring-shaped transition, and the browser owns the geometry on one layout clock with ZERO getBoundingClientRect, zero nextTick→rAF→reflow, zero inline-px writes — which directly serves AX.W01's 'one driver owns the entire box on one clock' and is the cleanest path to the ~479→~130 line collapse. HARD CAVEAT grounded in this repo: AV.W9.0 ALREADY TRIED the calc-size arm and it FROZE THE DOCK (dock.css:584 — the `@supports` block that opted the subtree into auto-to-length width interpolation ran the browser's clock WHILE SpringProgress wrote inline width per frame = a dual-driver race over the same property that cancelled the morph; born-RED under proof:dock-animation-live). The lesson for AX.W01 is NOT 'avoid calc-size' but 'calc-size must be the SOLE size authority' — you cannot keep the JS SpringProgress writing inline width AND have CSS interpolate calc-size on the same property. The path forward is a clean fork: EITHER (A) go fully declarative — express expanded width as `calc-size(max-content, size)`, drive the spring timing via a linear()-baked easing or a single CSS custom-property scalar, delete the inline-width writes entirely (this is the W01 'no transition on root / one scalar' ideal, but loses true mid-flight velocity-continuous interruption because CSS transitions retarget from current value at zero velocity); OR (B) keep the analytic SpringProgress as the single authority and DO NOT use calc-size for size at all — instead use the spring's normalized 0→1 scalar `--dock-morph-t` to drive radius/padding/specular/scale and write only the box size, treating calc-size() purely as the ONE-TIME natural-size MEASUREMENT primitive (`width: calc-size(max-content, size)` read once to get the target, then animate to it) rather than a second animator. Given W03's interruptible-spring + velocity-continuity contract (the iOS feel) and the AV.W9.2 retarget logic, option B (spring stays sole authority, calc-size used only to MEASURE intrinsic size cleanly without a hidden-clone reflow) is the lower-risk fold; option A is the purer single-clock ideal only if the team accepts CSS-transition retarget semantics (no live velocity carry). ANIMATION language: interpolate-size at :root (behind @supports) unlocks declarative height:auto for accordion/collapsible/details/expandable-container/dock-layer reveals — replacing the @keyframes collapsible grammar in animations.css with native keyword interpolation, and composing with the existing @starting-style top-layer entry grammar. GLASS primitives: the morph is where Liquid-Glass shape-shift lives — radius pill↔card, padding, specular-track intensity, and glass-refract displacement should all ride the SAME single morph scalar (the AX.W01 --dock-morph-t) so the size change and the material change are one liquid event; calc-size handles only the size axis of that bundle. UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY (path forward): a `useMorph(scalar)` / `--morph-t` convention where ONE analytic spring publishes a normalized 0→1, every visual axis (size via calc-size-measured target, radius, padding, scale, specular, refraction, child-stagger) is pure calc() off that scalar, interpolate-size handles intrinsic-size cases declaratively where no velocity-continuous interrupt is needed (entry reveals, accordions), and View-Transitions is reserved strictly for cross-tree route morphs (fourier) — never for the same-element dock collapse. This is the web-platform expression of GlassEffectContainer's morph model.
pitfalls: DUAL-DRIVER RACE (this repo's lived scar): interpolate-size/calc-size on a property that a JS spring is ALSO writing inline = two animators on one property; they cancel and freeze. AV.W9.0 retired exactly this arm after it froze the dock under proof:dock-animation-live. Any AX.W01 reintroduction MUST make calc-size the sole size authority — never coexist with SpringProgress writing inline width.

BROWSER SUPPORT is Chromium-only and STILL NOT BASELINE as of mid-2026: Chrome/Edge 129+ (Sept 2024); Safari and Firefox do NOT ship interpolate-size or calc-size(). MDN flags calc-size() as Experimental / Limited Availability. This is ~2/3 of users — so it is a PROGRESSIVE-ENHANCEMENT layer behind @supports(interpolate-size: allow-keywords), never the only path. The dock's spring-FLIP fallback must remain the universal driver; glass-ui's repo discipline (the VT-vs-FLIP fork comments) already reflects this multi-engine reality.

LAYOUT-THRASH / per-frame reflow: both interpolate-size and calc-size animate BOX-MODEL properties (width/height/flex-basis), which trip layout on every frame — Chrome's own docs say 'avoid animating box model properties to cut down on layout events'. For a dock this is bounded (small subtree, gesture-scoped) but the morphing subtree should be contained (`contain: layout`/content-visibility) and `will-change` promoted ONLY for the gesture duration (the repo's AV.W7 F3 on-demand will-change discipline already does this) — never a standing hint.

PERCENTAGES inside calc-size() are deceptive: `calc-size(auto, size + 50%)` adds 50% of the CONTAINING BLOCK, not 150% of the size. Use multiplication (`size * 1.5`) for proportional math. Easy footgun when tokenizing dock padding/insets off the morph.

TWO INTRINSIC KEYWORDS CANNOT INTERPOLATE TOGETHER: you cannot animate fit-content→max-content or auto→max-content. One endpoint must be a length/percentage. So a dock that wants to morph between two DIFFERENT content-driven widths still needs a measured length endpoint (calc-size used to MEASURE, not to tween keyword-to-keyword).

CSS-transition retarget has NO velocity continuity: a pure interpolate-size transition, when interrupted mid-flight, retargets from the current value at ZERO velocity (snap-restart feel) — which is exactly the non-iOS re-toggle the AX charter flags and AV.W9.2 solved with the analytic spring's (value, velocity) re-seat. Going fully declarative trades the line-count win for losing interruptible-spring physics; this is the central design tension of W01.

OPEN-ONLY on raw height: animating `height:auto` via interpolate-size animates OPEN cleanly but the CLOSE direction needs ::details-content (for <details>) or explicit from/to handling. Relevant if accordion/collapsible primitives adopt it — verify bidirectional behaviour, don't assume symmetric.

VIEW TRANSITIONS is the WRONG primitive for a same-element size morph: it rasterizes snapshots (blur on text/glass), and an uncaptured animating ancestor desyncs (the fourier two-co-mounted-docks duplicate view-transition-name collision is the concrete witness in the charter). Reserve VT for cross-tree route morphs; use calc-size/spring for the dock's own collapse. Do not conflate the two.

calc-size() auto-enables interpolate-size on the element (inherited to descendants) — a stray calc-size() can silently flip keyword-interpolation on for a whole subtree, surprising unrelated transitions. Scope intentionally; prefer the explicit `interpolate-size` property for simple cases and reserve calc-size() for where math is genuinely needed.

interpolate-size INHERITS — setting it at :root globally permits keyword interpolation everywhere, which can re-animate intrinsic-size transitions that were previously inert by design across the whole app. The opt-in is a behavioural change; gate it and audit existing width/height transitions.

notes.facet: CSS @starting-style + transition-behavior: allow-discrete + overlay — the native entry/exit morph for popovers / dialogs / the top layer
sotaTechniques: THE FOUR-FEATURE TOP-LAYER ENTRY/EXIT GRAMMAR (the canonical primitive). Native CSS now owns the full open->paint->close lifecycle for [popover] and <dialog> with zero JS. Four interlocking pieces: (1) @starting-style {} supplies the 'before-open' values the element interpolates FROM when it enters the DOM / flips display:none->shown (without it the first style change has no prior state and the transition is suppressed); (2) transition-behavior: allow-discrete lets the discrete properties display and overlay participate in a transition instead of swapping instantly; (3) display in the transition list keeps the box display:block through the WHOLE exit so the leave animation is visible; (4) overlay in the transition list defers the element's removal FROM the browser top layer until the animation finishes (overlay is browser-SET-ONLY — you list it to animate it, you cannot assign it). glass-ui ALREADY ships this verbatim in animations.css .glass-top-layer (opacity+scale+display+overlay, allow-discrete, @starting-style nested in :popover-open / [open]).

CASCADE-ORDER DISCIPLINE (the two load-bearing ordering rules). (a) transition-behavior: allow-discrete MUST be declared AFTER any transition shorthand, because the shorthand resets transition-behavior back to 'normal' and silently kills discrete transitions. (b) @starting-style MUST be authored AFTER the open-state rule (or nested inside it), because @starting-style declarations do not automatically win the cascade — placed before the open rule they get overridden and the entry never interpolates. glass-ui's current block follows BOTH rules correctly (it uses the longhand transition-property/duration/timing trio, and nests @starting-style inside the :popover-open selector).

ORIGIN-AWARE MORPH via transform-origin / position-area (the practitioner upgrade — Emil Kowalski / Radix). A popover/menu must scale-in FROM ITS TRIGGER, not from its own center. The default transform-origin: center reads as 'appeared out of nowhere'; setting it to the trigger edge (e.g. bottom-center for a menu above a button) makes the surface read as 'grew out of the control I just tapped' — exactly Apple's Liquid Glass 'the bubble pops open right where you tapped, communicating a direct button->content relationship.' Radix exposes --radix-popover-content-transform-origin; the platform-native equivalent is to derive the origin from CSS anchor positioning (the popover is tethered to its anchor, so the origin is computable).

CSS ANCHOR POSITIONING (the positioning companion to the entry morph). position-area / anchor() / position-try-fallbacks tether a top-layer popover back to a non-top-layer trigger with no JS (replaces Floating UI for the common cases). It reached Baseline 2026 (Chrome 125+, Safari 26, Firefox 147). It is the structural partner of the entry morph: anchor gives you WHERE the surface lives + a derivable transform-origin, @starting-style gives you HOW it materializes from there. Together they reproduce the Liquid Glass 'menu flows out of the control' behaviour in pure CSS.

interpolate-size: allow-keywords / calc-size() (animating to intrinsic keywords — height:auto, max-content). Opts a subtree into interpolating between a length and an intrinsic-size keyword, so a disclosure/menu/dock-pane can transition height:0 -> height:auto with no JS measurement. calc-size() auto-enables interpolate-size for the property it's used in. CAVEAT: Chromium-only (129+) as of 2026, NOT in Firefox/Safari — strictly progressive-enhancement, must keep a measured/FLIP fallback. Directly relevant to the dock's clip-reveal aperture and DockLayerGroup pane height morph.

DISCRETE @keyframes + animating display (the animation-side twin of allow-discrete). display and content-visibility can now be set inside @keyframes; unlike normal discrete props that flip at 50%, display flips at the START when animating in and the END when animating out, so a fade-out keyframe ending in display:none stays visible for the whole fade. This is the keyframe-grammar alternative to the transition-grammar allow-discrete path — useful when the entry is a multi-stage @keyframes (e.g. the floating-panel-in blur+scale glass materialize) rather than a two-state transition.

::backdrop ANIMATED INDEPENDENTLY with registered @property gradient stops. The modal scrim is its own pseudo-element; it animates on a separate transition/@keyframes track (blur + dim + gradient). Registering gradient color-stops as @property <color> makes them interpolable so the scrim can fade a tinted blur in/out rather than hard-cutting. glass-ui already animates dialog.glass-top-layer::backdrop (backdrop-filter blur + background-color dim with @starting-style) — the SOTA refinement is the @property-registered gradient stop.

PROGRESSIVE ENHANCEMENT via @supports (overlay: auto). Because overlay/allow-discrete were 'Newly Available' (and overlay is still Chromium-leaning for full smoothness), the entire morph grammar is wrapped in @supports (overlay: auto); a non-supporting engine simply shows the surface instantly — an acceptable degradation for a native top-layer element. glass-ui already gates its whole .glass-top-layer block this way. @starting-style itself is now Baseline Newly Available (Chrome 117+, Safari 17.5+, Firefox 129+), so the @starting-style HALF could be ungated; the overlay/display-discrete half stays gated.

REDUCED-MOTION CARVE (flatten morph to a fade, shorten duration). Native top-layer transitions are NOT auto-skipped under prefers-reduced-motion (same as View Transitions — the browser does not skip them for you). The discipline: under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), drop the scale/translate axis to a pure opacity fade and shorten the duration. glass-ui already does this (scale:none + --duration-fast in the PRM block). This is the same per-surface PRM contract the rest of glass-ui's motion sheet enforces.

ASYMMETRIC ENTER/EXIT TIMING + EASING (Emil Kowalski / iOS feel). Exits should be FASTER than entrances (enter ~300ms, exit ~200ms) and use ease-IN on exit (accelerate away, 'releasing a bowstring') vs ease-OUT / spring on enter (decelerate to rest, feels responsive). glass-ui's transitions.css ALREADY encodes this asymmetry in its Vue-Transition classes (dialog-scale enter = --duration-slow + --spring-bouncy, leave = --duration-normal + --ease-standard) — but the native .glass-top-layer block currently uses ONE symmetric duration+spring for both directions, so the native path is the one place the house asymmetry is not yet applied.

View Transitions API — the WRONG primitive for this facet (an explicit anti-pattern, per AX.W01). VT rasterizes the old/new states into flat snapshot images and cross-fades/morphs THEM; during the transition the element is an image, so font-size/backdrop-filter/text no longer respond, non-matching aspect ratios stretch ('taffy'), and a captured animating-ancestor desyncs. For a top-layer ENTRY/EXIT and for the DOCK layout-morph, the @starting-style + spring path keeps every element LIVE and is the correct tool; VT is reserved for cross-route/page geometry morphs (the named-element seam fourier route-morphs through), which is a SEPARABLE concern from the in-component open/close.
notes.applicability:
PATH FORWARD — fold this facet into glass-ui's unified iOS-26 morph facility:

1. THE NATIVE TOP-LAYER GRAMMAR IS ALREADY SHIPPED AND CORRECT — animations.css §TOP-LAYER (.glass-top-layer) is a textbook-correct implementation: longhand transition trio + allow-discrete LAST, @starting-style nested in :popover-open/[open], @supports(overlay:auto) gate, PRM carve, scale: longhand (not transform) so it composes with the identity-base work and mints no stacking context. The research VALIDATES the existing approach; the work is REFINEMENT + EXTENSION, not a rebuild.

2. W20 BUG IS REAL AND THIS FACET PROVES IT — the dialog.glass-top-layer::backdrop rule (animations.css ~L353-365) uses hsl(var(--background) / 0) and hsl(var(--background) / var(--top-layer-backdrop-dim)). --background is already a complete hsl() color, so hsl(var(--background)/a) is the double-wrap anti-pattern CLAUDE.md forbids and AX.W20 flags — it never paints, so the scrim dim is currently DEAD. Fix to color-mix(in srgb, var(--background) calc(--top-layer-backdrop-dim * 100%), transparent) per the house alpha-derivative pattern. This is the single highest-signal concrete defect this research surfaces.

3. APPLY THE HOUSE ENTER/EXIT ASYMMETRY TO THE NATIVE PATH (W05/W09 alignment) — the native .glass-top-layer block uses ONE --duration-normal + --spring-bouncy for both directions. Split it: enter = spring/ease-out at the entrance duration; exit = ease-in at a SHORTER duration (the transitions.css dialog-scale classes already encode exactly this asymmetry for the Vue-Transition path). Drive both off the ONE governed --spring-* register W05 establishes (the native top-layer and the reka Dialog spring opt-in should breathe on the same vocabulary, not two).

4. ORIGIN-AWARE + ANCHOR-POSITIONED is the iOS-26 'flows out of the control' upgrade — today .glass-top-layer scales from center (no transform-origin set). To get Apple's 'menu pops open right where you tapped,' set transform-origin from the trigger, derived via CSS anchor positioning (position-area/anchor()) so popovers tether to their invoker AND scale from it with no JS. This is the cleanest single addition that moves the surface from 'fades in' to 'materializes from its origin' — the core Liquid Glass morph read. Pair with a --top-layer-origin token so consumers retune.

5. UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY — this facet is the TOP-LAYER lobe of the same one-clock morph the dock waves (W01-W06) build for the COLLAPSE/EXPAND lobe. Both want: one spring vocabulary, scale/opacity (compositor-only) axes, a clip/aperture reveal of live content, transform-origin awareness, PRM flatten-to-fade, and NO View-Transitions for in-component open/close. Author them as ONE documented 'glass morph contract': (a) native CSS top-layer grammar for [popover]/<dialog> (this facet); (b) the single-scalar useSpring/SpringProgress driver for the dock + spring-mount Dialog/Sheet (useSpringMount already exists and is the JS twin); (c) interpolate-size/calc-size as the progressive-enhancement height:auto path for panes, with the FLIP measure as the universal fallback. The research-backed README frames @starting-style as the declarative native lobe and useSpring as the imperative interruptible lobe of one facility.

6. EXTEND THE GRAMMAR'S CONSUMERS (substrate-with-consumer) — today .glass-top-layer has exactly ONE consumer (GlassDialogNative, demo-gated). Per the wire-before-retire/no-overfit precept, either wire a 2nd consumer (the muster+speedtest native-drawer ask in W20 CONVERGE-fold b: popover='manual' + scroll-snap detents + scroll-driven @property backdrop) or keep it pilot-scoped. interpolate-size and anchor-positioning each need their own >=2-consumer justification before shipping as substrate.
pitfalls: NESTED hsl() NEVER PAINTS (the live bug). dialog.glass-top-layer::backdrop uses hsl(var(--background) / a) — --background is ALREADY a full hsl() color, so this is the double-wrap CLAUDE.md forbids; the scrim dim silently resolves to nothing. The whole point of this facet (animate the backdrop in/out) is currently DEAD on the modal path. Must be color-mix(in srgb, var(--background) N%, transparent).

allow-discrete RESET BY THE SHORTHAND. Writing `transition: ...; transition-behavior: allow-discrete;` is correct ONLY if allow-discrete comes AFTER the shorthand — the transition shorthand resets transition-behavior to normal. If a consumer later overrides with a `transition:` shorthand and forgets to re-add allow-discrete, the exit animation silently breaks (element vanishes instantly). glass-ui sidesteps this by using longhands (transition-property/duration/timing) — KEEP that, do not refactor to the shorthand.

@starting-style PLACED FIRST LOSES THE CASCADE. @starting-style does not auto-win; if authored before the open-state rule its values are overridden and the entry never interpolates (element just appears). Must be nested in / after the :popover-open/[open] rule.

overlay IS BROWSER-SET-ONLY + CHROMIUM-LEANING. You cannot assign overlay; you only LIST it in the transition to defer top-layer removal. Full smoothness is Chromium-strong; Safari/Firefox lag on overlay specifically. Hence the whole grammar stays @supports(overlay:auto)-gated — a non-supporting engine shows the surface instantly. Do not assume cross-engine parity for the overlay half.

MULTIPLE TOP-LAYER ELEMENTS WITHOUT overlay JUMP. If a second popover transitions out WITHOUT overlay in its transition list, it drops out of the top layer immediately and jumps BEHIND the first popover before its animation even starts. overlay in the list is what keeps stacked top-layer exits visually ordered. Relevant if glass-ui ever stacks a popover over a native dialog.

NATIVE TOP-LAYER TRANSITIONS ARE NOT AUTO-PRM-SKIPPED. Like View Transitions, the browser does NOT honor prefers-reduced-motion for you on @starting-style transitions — you must carve it manually (flatten scale/translate to a fade, shorten duration). glass-ui does this; any new axis (translate, the origin scale) must be added to the PRM carve too or it regresses.

backdrop-filter ANIMATION IS EXPENSIVE. Transitioning backdrop-filter blur (the scrim materialize) re-samples the backdrop every frame and can jank, especially layered with the per-rung glass blur. Prefer animating opacity/background-color of an already-blurred backdrop, or animate a short distance; respect prefers-reduced-transparency (glass.css already zeroes blur there — ensure the top-layer backdrop honors it too).

transform-origin: center IS WRONG FOR ANCHORED SURFACES. A menu/popover scaling from center reads as 'appeared from nowhere' and breaks the Liquid Glass origin->content relationship. Adding the origin is low-risk but it INTRODUCES a transform; ensure it uses the scale: longhand (not transform: scale) to stay consistent with the identity-base / no-extra-stacking-context discipline already in the codebase.

interpolate-size / calc-size IS CHROMIUM-ONLY (2026). Animating height:auto via interpolate-size works in Chrome/Edge 129+ but NOT Firefox/Safari — it is strictly progressive enhancement. Do not let a pane's open/close DEPEND on it; keep the FLIP/measured fallback as the universal path (the dock already drives size via SpringProgress FLIP — correct).

VIEW TRANSITIONS IS THE WRONG TOOL FOR IN-COMPONENT OPEN/CLOSE. VT rasterizes to snapshots: live properties (font-size, backdrop-filter, text) freeze, mismatched aspect ratios stretch into 'taffy', and captured animating ancestors desync — the exact failure AX.W01 retires for the dock. Use @starting-style + spring for top-layer entry/exit and the dock morph; reserve VT for cross-route page-geometry morphs only (a separable named-element seam).

notes.facet: CSS anchor positioning (2025) — anchored morphing surfaces (popover/menu) that track + reshape to their trigger
sotaTechniques: CSS Anchor Positioning core (anchor-name / position-anchor / anchor() / anchor-size()) — an absolutely-positioned element pins itself to a named anchor element anywhere in the DOM (not just an ancestor); anchor(top/left/right/bottom/center) reads the anchor's box edges and anchor-size(width/height) reads its dimensions, so a popover tracks + can size to its trigger with zero JS. Baseline 2026 in Chrome 125+, Safari 26, Firefox 145+ (behind a flag in FF); ~91% traffic. This is the native replacement for Floating UI / Popper that reka-ui's Popover/HoverCard/DropdownMenu still ship.

position-area (the 3x3 grid) + position-try-fallbacks (flip-block / flip-inline / flip-start + named @position-try blocks) — position-area places the element in one of 9 logical cells around the anchor ('span-bottom right' etc.); position-try-fallbacks declares an ordered fallback list the engine walks when the primary position overflows the viewport, picking the first that fits. This is native collision-avoidance — the exact job reka-ui delegates to Floating UI's flip/shift middleware.

AIM — Anchor-Interpolated Morph (Adam Argyle / nerdy.dev, Jan 2026) — a pure-CSS FLIP: set the popover/dialog's @starting-style (and :not([open]) exit) to the anchor's geometry via left/top: anchor(...) + width/height: anchor-size(...), set the open state to its natural render, and let `transition` invert+play. The surface literally grows OUT OF its trigger and collapses back into it — the web's closest analog to Apple's 'button morphs into the menu' Liquid-Glass behavior. Requires interpolate-size: allow-keywords to animate to width/height: auto.

interpolate-size: allow-keywords + calc-size() — opts a subtree into interpolating between a length and an intrinsic keyword (auto/min-content/max-content/fit-content), making `transition: width/height` to `auto` actually animate instead of snapping. calc-size() auto-enables it locally. CRITICAL GATE: Chromium-only (Chrome/Edge 129+); Safari + Firefox snap. This is the load-bearing dependency of AIM's size-morph half.

@starting-style + transition-behavior: allow-discrete + overlay — the platform entry/exit grammar for top-layer surfaces ([popover]/<dialog>): @starting-style supplies the from-state, allow-discrete animates the discrete display/overlay flips, overlay keeps the element in the top layer through its exit. glass-ui ALREADY ships this as the `.glass-top-layer` grammar in animations.css, @supports (overlay: auto)-gated — it is the entry substrate AIM layers a geometry-morph on top of.

Anchored container queries — container-type: anchored + @container anchored(fallback: flip-block) (Chrome 143) — lets the popover restyle itself based on WHICH position-try fallback won, in pure CSS: flip the caret/arrow, swap transform-origin, re-round the corner nearest the anchor, change the morph direction. Solves the 'flipped popover now points the wrong way / morphs from the wrong edge' problem without a JS observer.

Origin-aware transform-origin (Emil Kowalski) — a popover/menu must scale FROM its trigger's edge, not center; set transform-origin to the trigger side (Radix exposes --radix-popover-content-transform-origin; reka-ui exposes the equivalent --reka-* var). With anchor positioning the origin can be derived from the active position-area, so a flipped popover scales from the correct corner. Modals stay transform-origin: center (no single anchor). This is the cheap, universally-supported 80% of the Apple morph feel.

Apple Liquid-Glass morph semantics (WWDC25 'Meet Liquid Glass') as the design target — a menu/popover originating from a glass button MORPHS the button into the overlay (matchedGeometry via GlassEffectContainer + glassEffectID + glassEffectTransition), and the glass GETS THICKER as it flexes/enlarges (deeper shadow, more pronounced lensing/refraction, softer light scatter) to read as more substantial material. The web mapping: AIM = the geometry morph; a thickness-interpolation of --glass-blur/--glass-material-rim/shadow along the same scalar = the material-thickening; corner-shape: squircle = the superellipse silhouette.

anchor-scope (Chrome 131+) — scopes an anchor-name to a subtree on a common ancestor so repeated triggers in a list (toolbar buttons, table rows) each resolve to THEIR OWN anchor instead of all binding the last-in-DOM-order one. Mandatory hygiene for any list/grid of anchored popovers (a dock of icon buttons each spawning a flyout).
notes.applicability: "DIRECT FIT — the popover/menu/flyout surfaces (NOT the dock-collapse morph). glass-ui's Popover/HoverCard/DropdownMenu/Combobox + the custom HoverPopover + the dock's `.dock-popover` flyouts currently position through reka-ui (Floating UI JS). The SOTA path is: (1) keep reka-ui for focus/dismiss/top-layer/a11y semantics (which it does well), but (2) progressively REPLACE the JS positioning with native anchor-name/position-anchor + position-area + position-try-fallbacks under @supports (anchor-name: --x) — dropping a JS positioning loop per open popover and getting native collision-avoidance for free. (3) Layer AIM on top so a dock flyout grows OUT of its DockIconButton and collapses back in — this IS the Apple 'button morphs into the menu' behavior, and it's the unified-morph win the charter is reaching for. (4) Add the origin-aware transform-origin now (universally supported, cheap) as the 80% feel even before full AIM. KEY TENSION WITH THE DOCK-COLLAPSE MORPH: AX.W01 deliberately RETIRED View Transitions for the dock box morph in favor of a single analytic spring writing --dock-morph-t once per frame to the root, on the explicit grounds that VT rasterizes pixels (wrong for a layout morph) and desyncs box-vs-content. That same first-principle applies to AIM: AIM animates real layout properties (top/left/width/height) which is layout-thrashy and tied to interpolate-size (Chromium-only) — so for the DOCK'S OWN expand/collapse, the single-scalar transform/clip-aperture spring stays canonical; anchor positioning is for the SEPARATE concern of where teleported popovers LAND and how they morph FROM their trigger. The convergence: express the AIM popover morph on the SAME --spring-dock register (W05's dock spring vocabulary) and the SAME --glass-material thickening tokens, so the dock box-morph and its flyout-morphs read as one motion language. The material-thickening axis (Apple's thicker glass when flexing) is the one genuinely-missing Apple behavior glass-ui can add cheaply: interpolate --glass-blur-* + --glass-material-rim + shadow along the morph scalar; corner-shape: squircle (already @supports-gated in glass.css) supplies the silhouette. Anchored container queries map cleanly onto glass-ui's existing data-attribute-restyle idiom for caret/origin/corner flips per fallback."
pitfalls: interpolate-size (AIM's size-morph) is CHROMIUM-ONLY — Safari + Firefox snap to size instantly. Any AIM adoption MUST be @supports (interpolate-size: allow-keywords)-gated with the @starting-style fade as the universal fallback; do NOT ship AIM as the only entry animation or Safari/FF users get a teleport. This is the same progressive-enhancement discipline glass-ui already applies to overlay:auto and corner-shape.

Animating top/left/width/height (AIM) is layout-thrashing — it is NOT the compositor-cheap transform/opacity/clip path glass-ui's skeleton/morph work deliberately uses. For the DOCK-COLLAPSE morph this would re-introduce exactly the per-frame reflow AX.W01 engineered out; keep AIM scoped to teleported popovers (laid out once in the top layer, off the document flow) and never to the dock box itself.

Multiple triggers sharing an anchor-name silently bind the popover to the LAST one in DOM order — a dock/list of icon buttons each spawning a flyout will all anchor to the wrong button without anchor-scope on the common ancestor (Chrome 131+). Mint a per-instance anchor-name (the same useId() idiom GlassDock already uses for view-transition-name).

reka-ui portals popover content OUT of the trigger's subtree (PopoverPortal) — anchor positioning works cross-DOM by design so this is fine, BUT the polyfill historically struggled across shadow/portal boundaries (only fixed in polyfill 0.7.0 for same-shadow-DOM), and any consumer-side scoped CSS custom properties (--spring-dock, --glass-*) won't reach the portaled node. glass-ui already handles this via global animations.css rules + data-glass-dock-portal attributes; AIM tokens must ride the same global-rule path, not scoped SFC styles.

Safari vs Chrome containing-block divergence: Safari shifts the positioned element into the containing block (can cover the anchor), Chrome shifts only block-axis; Safari's behavior is spec-correct (open Chromium bug). Workaround place-self: anchor-center. position-area also auto-disables margin:auto now (CSSWG fix), retiring the old manual `margin: unset` requirement — but older Safari needs the manual reset.

transform-origin: center is wrong for almost every anchored popover/menu — it makes the surface scale from its middle instead of from the trigger, breaking the spatial-continuity illusion that is the whole point of the Apple morph. Derive origin from the active position-area / fallback. Conversely modals MUST stay center (no anchor).

A flipped popover (position-try-fallbacks fired) morphs from / points at the WRONG edge unless you detect the active fallback. Pre-Chrome-143 this needs a JS read or an arrow per side; anchored container queries (Chrome 143+) do it in CSS but are very new — gate and fall back.

Do NOT rip out reka-ui's popover machinery wholesale. Anchor positioning + the popover attribute replace Floating UI's POSITIONING, but reka-ui still owns focus management, light-dismiss, Escape, ARIA wiring, and collision semantics the design system depends on (and the MEMORY 'binding-verification' hazard — stale reka prop bindings silently no-op). Treat anchor positioning as a progressive-enhancement layer UNDER reka, not a replacement for it.

interpolate-size: allow-keywords inherits — setting it broadly can unexpectedly animate width/height keyword changes on unrelated descendants (skeletons, accordions). Scope it to the morphing surface, or use calc-size() locally instead of the global property.

notes.facet: Shape interpolation on the web — border-radius morph, clip-path morph, the pill↔card↔circle reshape — applied to glass-ui's dock + animation + glass primitives toward an iOS-26 Liquid-Glass unified morph facility.
sotaTechniques: corner-shape + superellipse() (Chrome 139+, @supports-gated): native superellipse corner geometry that interpolates SMOOTHLY between distinct shapes — superellipse(1)=circle, (2)=squircle, ∞→square, negative=scoop/notch. Unlike border-radius (circular arcs only) it animates/transitions on hover/focus/state and the backdrop-filter, border, and shadow all follow the corner. This is the literal iOS-26 corner. MECHANISM for us: pill↔card↔circle becomes a corner-shape interpolation (round↔squircle) layered on the existing border-radius tween — already adopted in glass.css AW.W23 and dock.css shape-card, but only as a static rest-state PE, NOT yet animated on the morph clock.

Single-scalar morph driver via @property-registered custom property: register `@property --dock-morph-t { syntax:'<number>'; inherits:false; initial-value:0 }` so the browser TYPES it and can interpolate it on the GPU (untyped custom props animate discretely = no tween). One analytic spring writes 0→1 to `--dock-morph-t` once per frame; EVERY axis (inline-size, padding, border-radius, scale, bg/border color, child stagger) is a pure `calc()` off that one scalar — one clock, one paint, no per-axis transition races. This IS AX.W01's target and the canonical web translation of Apple's 'one material moving in tandem with your interaction'.

interpolate-size: allow-keywords + calc-size() (Chrome/Edge only, NOT baseline): enables animating between a length and an intrinsic keyword (auto/max-content/fit-content) — the long-missing 'animate to height:auto'. MECHANISM: lets a dock/accordion/drawer morph from a fixed collapsed size to its natural content size with pure CSS, no JS measure/pin. CAVEAT — glass-ui's dock EXPLICITLY RETIRED this arm (AV.W9.0) because it second-drove width on Chrome 129+ and froze the dock when it raced the JS spring; it is a single-driver-only tool, viable only if it OWNS the axis (e.g. a content reveal the spring never touches), never alongside the spring.

View Transitions API — same-document now Baseline (Oct 2025, incl. Firefox 144): `::view-transition-group` auto-morphs a tagged element's width/height/position/transform from old→new box (the 'morphing rectangle'). view-transition-class, auto view-transition-name:match-element, :active-view-transition-type for directional curves. MECHANISM: the right primitive for ROUTE/shared-element morphs (a card→detail page geometry morph) where the element is genuinely replaced. The Bram.us border-radius fix is load-bearing: VT CROSS-FADES border-radius by default (two snapshots fade) — to MORPH the corner you `display:none` the ::view-transition-old and put a real `transition: border-radius` on the live element so it tweens in parallel with the group's box morph.

VT is the WRONG primitive for a same-element layout morph (AX.W01 diagnosis, corroborated): VT rasterizes pixels and cross-fades two snapshots — for a dock COLLAPSE (same element reshaping in place) this desyncs the box from its content (uncaptured-animating-ancestor) and a duplicate view-transition-name silently DROPS the snapshot. Rule: VT for element-to-element/route morphs; a single-scalar CSS-property spring for same-element in-place reshape. glass-ui keeps the per-instance view-transition-name SEAM for consumer route-morphs (fourier) while retiring the dock-collapse VT fork.

SwiftUI GlassEffectContainer + glassEffectID (iOS 26) — the design oracle: a container merges multiple glass shapes into ONE shape; a `spacing` threshold makes near elements BLEND/fuse (gel coalescence); glassEffectID(_:in:namespace) makes views fluidly morph into one another (default matchedGeometry transition = the morph; .materialize / .identity alternatives); glassEffectUnion fuses siblings under one id. MECHANISM/translation: the web analog of the merge-blend is an SVG/CSS gooey filter (feGaussianBlur→feColorMatrix alpha-threshold) over sibling glass pills so they fuse when close; the morph is our single-scalar matchedGeometry equivalent. This is the gold-standard mental model for a UNIFIED morph facility — every glass element shares one container clock and a namespace of morph ids.

clip-path basic-shape interpolation (compositor-thread, broadly supported): clip-path animates on the compositor when you stick to circle()/ellipse()/inset()/polygon-with-matched-vertices. inset(r round R) gives an animatable rounded rect; circle()↔inset() is the circle↔pill↔card reveal. CRITICAL: vertex count must MATCH across keyframes or the shape POPS. MECHANISM: clip-reveal aperture (already the dock's `overflow:clip` + data-morphing pattern) — content laid out once at natural size, the morphing box uncovers it. Use inset() for the reveal so the radius rides the same morph scalar.

CSS shape() function (Safari 18.4 + Chromium, NOT baseline — Firefox missing): SVG-path-like commands as an animatable CSS value; interpolates between two shape()/path() values IFF same command count/type. MECHANISM: arbitrary fluid silhouettes (a blob/liquid edge) that border-radius can't express — the high-end 'liquid' tier for a goo/aurora-adjacent morph. Treat as progressive enhancement only; border-radius+corner-shape is the baseline contract.

Interruptible analytic spring with velocity continuity (the iOS physics contract): on a re-toggle mid-flight, RE-SEAT the live solver's target from its current (value, velocity) instead of dispose+reconstruct-from-rest, so the morph is continuous through a retarget. glass-ui already does this (keyframes.js SpringProgress, AV.W9.2). This is what separates 'springy' from 'eased' — Family/Emil Kowalski's whole 'fluid, gesture-driven, never restarts' feel reduces to velocity-preserving retargets on one spring.

Shared-element / matched-geometry continuity (Family.co practitioner canon): if a component persists across states it should MORPH not recreate — buttons glide across trays, buttons morph into trays and back, trays morph to full-screen, even text morphs through shared letterforms (Continue→Confirm via 'Con'). MECHANISM: a stable identity (view-transition-name on web / glassEffectID native) + one measured geometry delta animated on a spring. The web kit is VT for cross-component and FLIP/single-scalar for same-component.

Compositor-safe morph property discipline + on-demand will-change: animate ONLY transform/opacity/clip-path/registered-@property scalars per frame; NEVER tween an INHERITED custom property (forces whole-subtree style recalc every frame — the 'inheritance bomb'); set will-change:<dim> ONLY for the gesture duration and clear to auto on settle (a standing hint pins a compositor layer + VRAM on an idle element). glass-ui's useLayerTransition already encodes both rules — they are the perf floor for any morph facility.
notes.applicability:
THE PATH FORWARD — a UNIFIED morph facility for glass-ui, mapped to the existing code and AX waves:

(1) MORPH ENGINE = one @property-typed scalar per surface. AX.W01 already targets `--dock-morph-t` (one analytic spring → one CSS var → every axis as calc()). Generalize this from the dock into a library-wide `useMorph(rootRef, springReg)` composable on /motion: it owns one keyframes.js SpringProgress, writes a registered `@property --morph-t {syntax:'<number>'}` 0→1, and exposes velocity-continuous retarget. EVERY morphable surface (dock, drawer, dialog, card, sheet, popover) consumes the same primitive — that is the iOS-26 'one material' facility. dock.css's existing `border-radius var(--dock-motion-resize)` transition-list approach is the transition-based cousin; the W01 single-scalar form is strictly better (one clock, calc()-derived radius, no transition-property race).

(2) THE pill↔card↔circle RESHAPE = border-radius calc(off --morph-t) + corner-shape interpolation. The codebase ALREADY rides border-radius on the dock spring (dock.css L337) and ALREADY ships `corner-shape: squircle` @supports-gated on .glass-card/.glass-btn/.btn-pill (glass.css L615) and the big-dock shape-card (dock.css L416). The MISSING piece: animate corner-shape ON the morph clock — interpolate `corner-shape: superellipse(var(--morph-corner))` where --morph-corner is a calc() from --morph-t (e.g. round→squircle as pill→card), so the corner GEOMETRY morphs, not just its arc radius. Express collapsed/expanded radii as `border-radius: calc(var(--radius-pill) + (var(--dock-card-radius) - var(--radius-pill)) * var(--dock-morph-t))`.

(3) ROUTE/SHARED-ELEMENT morph stays on View Transitions — and stays SEPARATE from in-place reshape. Keep the per-instance view-transition-name seam (fourier consumes it for viz↔workspace route-morphs; AX.W01 CONVERGE fold (a)). Retire the dock-COLLAPSE VT fork (it's the wrong primitive for same-element reshape — VT cross-fades the radius and desyncs box-from-content). For ANY card→detail morph, adopt the Bram.us recipe: display:none the ::view-transition-old + a real `transition: border-radius` on the live element so the corner morphs in parallel with the group box.

(4) GLASS COALESCENCE (the gel-fuse) = the GlassEffectContainer analog. For a future tier, an SVG gooey filter (feGaussianBlur→feColorMatrix alpha threshold) over sibling glass pills makes them BLEND when within a spacing threshold — the web translation of glassEffectContainer(spacing:). Lower priority than (1)-(3); it's the dock-icons-merge / multi-pill-fuse flourish.

(5) GLASS SURFACE morph composes with the specular/material work. AX.W09 (specular tune) + W20 (retire the JS SVG-displacement GlassPanel onto CSS-native .glass-material) mean the glass LOOK is pure CSS — so it inherits the morph for free (backdrop-filter, border, shadow all follow corner-shape). The morph facility and the material grammar are orthogonal and compose: one drives geometry (--morph-t), the other drives surface (--glass-* tokens + @property specular). Apple's 'thicker material at larger sizes = deeper shadow/more lensing' maps to a calc() coupling shadow-tier and blur to --morph-t (a `--shadow-dock-wrap` lift on the same spring is already AX.W04's scope).

(6) ATOMS that already exist and just need WIRING TOGETHER: useLayerTransition (single SpringProgress, velocity-continuity, on-demand will-change, inheritance-bomb guard — AX.W01 re-exports it on /dock so value.js drops its FLIP fork), useViewTransition (the startViewTransition substrate, /motion-core), the `data-morphing` clip-aperture pattern, corner-shape squircle @supports blocks, @property-registered specular vars. The facility is a CONVERGENCE of these onto one named primitive, not a from-scratch build.
pitfalls: interpolate-size/calc-size() is Chrome/Edge-ONLY and NOT baseline — glass-ui already got BURNED by it (AV.W9.0): it second-drove dock width on Chrome 129+ and FROZE the dock when it raced the JS spring. Use it only where it solely OWNS an axis (e.g. a content reveal the spring never touches); never alongside the spring driver. Two drivers on one axis = the dual-driver race.

corner-shape + superellipse() is Chrome 139+ ONLY (no Safari/Firefox as of 2026). MUST stay @supports(corner-shape: squircle)-gated with border-radius round as the un-gated fallback — a leak onto the base rule breaks the round fallback on partial-support engines. The squircle is the BETTER tier, the arc is the CONTRACT (not a degraded fallback). glass.css already enforces this discipline.

View Transitions CROSS-FADES border-radius by default — it does NOT morph the corner. Two snapshots fade through each other (ugly). The fix (display:none ::view-transition-old + a live `transition: border-radius` matching the VT duration) is non-obvious and must be authored per morphing element.

VT is the WRONG primitive for a same-element in-place reshape (rasterizes pixels, cross-fades two snapshots) → box leads/lags content, the uncaptured-animating-ancestor desync. A DUPLICATE view-transition-name (two co-mounted docks both minting glass-dock-1) silently DROPS the snapshot and reds ~13 e2e — the concrete witness. Single-scalar CSS spring for in-place; VT for element-to-element only.

clip-path/polygon morph POPS if vertex count differs across keyframes — you cannot animate a 4-point to a 6-point polygon smoothly. shape() has the same same-command-count constraint. For variable-complexity silhouettes this means padding both ends to equal vertex/command counts.

Untyped custom properties animate DISCRETELY — `--dock-morph-t` without an `@property` registration will JUMP, not tween. The @property `syntax` + `inherits` descriptors are MANDATORY for the GPU interpolation. Easy to forget and silently produces a step animation.

The INHERITANCE BOMB: tweening an INHERITED custom property (e.g. --phase-color/--shadow-color) per frame forces a whole-subtree style recalc EVERY frame. The morph scalar must be `inherits:false` and color shifts must route through a DISCRETE class swap, never a per-frame interpolation of an inherited var. useLayerTransition already documents this as F5.

Standing will-change pins a compositor layer + VRAM on an IDLE element. Set will-change:<dim> ONLY for the gesture duration; clear to auto on settle/transitionend. A permanent hint on a dock that's collapsed 99% of the time is pure waste.
shape() is Safari 18.4 + Chromium but Firefox-MISSING → not baseline; treat as a progressive-enhancement tier only, never the contract.

backdrop-filter under a morphing/clipped element is expensive and can flicker — the dock uses `overflow: clip` (paint-only, not a scroll container) precisely to avoid the scroll-box dance; a careless `overflow:hidden` re-introduces it. Animating border-radius while backdrop-filter is active is a known repaint hotspot; keep the blur on a stable layer where possible.

Per Apple HIG: Liquid Glass is for the NAVIGATION/control layer floating ABOVE content, not for content itself — over-applying the morph/glass to every element (content cards, list rows) is the documented over-use anti-pattern and hurts legibility. The morph facility should be scoped to chrome (dock, sheets, dialogs, controls), not splashed across content.

notes.facet: Web matched-geometry / shared-element transitions — morphing one element into another across a layout/route change
sotaTechniques: VIEW TRANSITIONS API same-document (Baseline Newly Available Oct 2025: Chrome 111+/Edge 111+/Firefox 144/Safari 18+): wrap a synchronous DOM mutation in document.startViewTransition(cb); browser snapshots every uniquely view-transition-name'd element old AND new and auto-interpolates position/size/border-radius between them - a true MATCHED-GEOMETRY morph (200px thumbnail to full-screen modal). The web's native matchedGeometryEffect.

CROSS-DOCUMENT (MPA) VIEW TRANSITIONS - Chrome 126+/Edge 126+/Safari 18.2+ (not Firefox): same named-element morph across a full page navigation, opt-in via @view-transition{navigation:auto}; pageswap/pagereveal events set up names. This is the route-morph machinery glass-ui's fourier consumer route-morphs the dock through (viz-workspace).

view-transition-class (Chrome 125+/Firefox 144) - one shared class drives many tracked elements' VT curve: ::view-transition-group(.gl-list-item){duration/timing}. glass-ui already uses .gl-list-item/.gl-dock-layer. Decouples LOOK (CSS) from the per-element unique name (MANDATORY: <=1 element per name per state or it silently skips).

VIEW TRANSITION TYPES - :active-view-transition-type(t) + startViewTransition({update,types:['dock-expand']}) (Chrome 140+; degrades to symmetric curve on Firefox 144). Direction-specific curves (snappier exit, softer entry-overshoot - the iOS asymmetry). glass-ui ALREADY ships this in view-transition.css (dock-expand/collapse/layer-forward/back).

AUTO-NAMING view-transition-name:match-element (Chrome 2025, same-document) - browser mints a stable name per element identity, so N rows morph without hand-minting N names. Eliminates the name-collision class (fourier's duplicate glass-dock-1 DROP) for lists/grids.

NESTED VIEW-TRANSITION GROUPS + view-transition-group CSS property (normal|contain|nearest; Chrome 140+) - the pseudo-tree nests hierarchically so a morphing parent CLIPS/contains its children's snapshots. Fixes the squish/distortion of contents during an aspect-ratio-changing morph - the exact dock box-morph hazard.

SCOPED (element-scoped) VIEW TRANSITIONS - element.startViewTransition() on any element with contain:layout (Chrome 147 stable; flag from 140). Runs MULTIPLE concurrent transitions with different roots, nests them, fixes position:fixed layering, keeps the page interactive. The substrate for a unified facility where EVERY UI element morphs independently/simultaneously without one document-global VT serializing them.

FLIP (First-Last-Invert-Play; Paul Lewis) - measure getBoundingClientRect before, mutate, measure after, apply inverting transform, play to identity. Framework-agnostic shared-element morph on EVERY engine (no VT needed). Modern: invert with translate/scale (not transform) so it STACKS; even inside VT override the auto group keyframes with translate-only FLIP to keep it on the COMPOSITOR (default group anim animates width/height = main-thread). glass-ui's useLayerTransition is a spring-driven FLIP.

ANALYTIC-SPRING single-scalar driver (glass-ui AX W01) - one SpringProgress ODE writes a normalized 0-1 scalar to --dock-morph-t once per frame; EVERY axis (inline-size/padding/radius/scale/color/child-stagger) is pure calc() off that scalar. One clock, one paint, no per-engine fork. Velocity-continuous on interrupt (solver re-seats target from live value+velocity - the iOS interruptible-spring contract). SUPERIOR to VT for same-surface layout morph (VT crossfades rasterized pixels - blurs text, can't interrupt, desyncs an uncaptured animating ancestor).

SWIFTUI LIQUID-GLASS MORPH MODEL (the design target) - glassEffectID(id,in:namespace) links two glass shapes so SwiftUI morphs geometry between them across conditional render; GlassEffectContainer with a spacing threshold makes nearby shapes blend/fuse (proximity merge); glassEffectUnion merges distant same-id shapes into one hardware-looking unit; matchedTransitionSource + .navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID:)) morphs a sheet OUT OF the button presenting it. Curve .bouncy / .spring(response:0.3,dampingFraction:0.6). Web analog: VT/FLIP geometry + a shared spring + a gooey-merge filter for proximity fusion.

GOOEY/METABALL PROXIMITY-MERGE (web analog of GlassEffectContainer spacing) - SVG feGaussianBlur(stdDeviation) then feColorMatrix whose alpha row snaps the blurred fringe to a hard edge, so two glass shapes FUSE into one fluid outline as they approach then pull apart. Chrome/Edge only (Safari/Firefox render plain blur - graceful degrade to discrete shapes). Pair feDisplacementMap for refractive lensing. How the web fakes the liquid 'shapes flowing together'.

interpolate-size:allow-keywords + calc-size() (Chrome/Edge 129+; not FF/Safari) - CSS transitions/@starting-style animate to/from height:auto purely declaratively (progressive-enhancement on :root). USEFUL for entry/exit reveals, but glass-ui DELIBERATELY RETIRED it as a dock width second-driver (AV.W9.0) because it RACED the JS spring (two authorities on one axis froze the dock). Rule: only for axes the spring does NOT touch.

@starting-style + transition-behavior:allow-discrete + native top-layer (Baseline) - pure-CSS entry/exit for popover/<dialog>/display:none surfaces (glass-ui ships .glass-top-layer). The facility's discrete-property half: enter/exit a surface without JS coordination, composing with the VT/spring geometry morph.

SPRING INTERRUPTIBILITY canon (Emil Kowalski/Family.co/Linear) - springs preserve VELOCITY on interrupt; CSS keyframes & VT snapshots restart from zero. A spring morph smoothly REVERSES from its current position mid-flight (expand then Escape). Animate only transform/opacity (width/height last resort) to stay 60fps on the compositor; never animate keyboard-initiated actions; one cohesive motion vocabulary; respect prefers-reduced-motion. Why glass-ui's single-scalar SpringProgress beats the VT fork for the dock's own collapse.
notes.applicability: DIRECT, and glass-ui is already further along than most of the web. The facet bifurcates into TWO separable morph concerns the AX charter (W01 CONVERGE fold a) explicitly disentangles; the path forward keeps both. (1) THE DOCK'S OWN COLLAPSE/LAYER MORPH (same surface, layout change): AX.W01/W02 RETIRE the View-Transitions fork here and re-derive useLayerTransition (479 to ~130 lines) onto ONE single-scalar analytic SpringProgress writing --dock-morph-t to the .glass-dock root, every axis (inline-size/padding/border-radius/scale/bg+border color/child-stagger) expressed as calc() off that scalar in ONE paint. CORRECT and SOTA: VT is the wrong primitive for a same-surface layout morph (crossfades rasterized pixels - blurs text, can't interrupt, desyncs because only .dock-layers is VT-named so root chrome morphs on a separate clock - slice 0 F0/F1, slice 1 F0/F1/F5, slice 5 F0/F1). One spring gives iOS interruptible velocity-continuity for free on EVERY engine, fixes box-leads-content-by-16ms (one clock, same paint), composes with the published (0.32,0.7) --spring-dock token (no re-bounce). W02 folds the inner DockLayerGroup pair onto the outer driver via the existing dockContext DI so a dock is ONE orchestrator (state = expandedState x activePane), unifying the doubled .dock-layer/.dock-layer-item-host vocabularies onto one .is-active/.is-leaving contract and the hand-typed 0.08/0.16 stagger ladder onto one --dock-stagger-step x index. The clip-reveal aperture (data-morphing single-axis overflow:clip, the box IS the aperture) STAYS - it lets content lay out once at natural size. (2) THE CROSS-ROUTE/CROSS-ELEMENT MORPH (one element to another across a route/layout swap): PRESERVE the per-instance view-transition-name seam (glass-dock-${useId()}, app-scoped, collision-free, sanitized; gated by proof:vt-names invariant eta). This is what fourier's J+K critical path route-morphs the dock through (viz-workspace), SEPARABLE from concern (1): W01 retires the COLLAPSE VT fork while keeping the named-element route-morph seam. The unified MORPH FACILITY ('the iOS-26 morphing facility for EVERY UI element') is built by promoting this pattern library-wide: every glass primitive that can morph into another (dock to sheet, button to dialog, card to detail) gets a stable view-transition-name + view-transition-class seam + a shared --spring-* curve so the VT group animation runs the SAME spring as the JS FLIP (parity already in view-transition.css). SCOPED view transitions (element.startViewTransition + contain:layout, Chrome 147) are the substrate to make MANY morph concurrently/independently without one document-global VT serializing them. The PROXIMITY-FUSION liquid feel (SwiftUI GlassEffectContainer spacing) maps onto a gooey feGaussianBlur+feColorMatrix merge filter layered on the existing .glass-material/--specular-* substrate (W09 specular work), Chrome-only with graceful degrade. PATH FORWARD: a small useMorph/useMatchedGeometry composable (sibling to useViewTransition) that (a) on VT-capable engines for cross-element/cross-route swaps drives the native named-element morph with a view-transition-class bound to a --spring-* token; (b) for same-surface layout morphs drives the single-scalar SpringProgress to --x-morph-t pattern (the dock's W01 driver generalized off the dock); (c) shares ONE spring vocabulary (W05: excise --ease-apple-spring, govern settle/control/playful registers from the regen pipeline so token-CSS and runtime-ODE are bit-identical); (d) exposes the rebuilt useLayerTransition on the /dock barrel so value.js DELETES its local FLIP-width fork (substrate-with-consumer). Expose it as the one morph seam every glass element binds - the way SwiftUI exposes glassEffectID.
pitfalls: VT crossfades RASTERIZED snapshots - wrong primitive for a same-surface layout morph: blurs text mid-morph, CANNOT be interrupted/reversed mid-flight (no velocity), desyncs if an uncaptured ANCESTOR animates. Documented root of glass-ui's dock desync (W01 retires it). Use VT for cross-element/cross-ROUTE morphs; use a single-scalar spring for same-surface layout morphs.

DUPLICATE view-transition-name DROPS the morph silently - MANDATORY is <=1 element per name per visual state. Two co-mounted docks both minting glass-dock-1 (fourier CanvasControlsDock + EditorControlsDock) drop the snapshot and red ~13 e2e. Mitigate with app-scoped useId (done) or view-transition-name:match-element for lists.

DEFAULT ::view-transition-group keyframes animate width/height = main-thread jank even when dimensions are unchanged - tanks mobile FPS. Fix: override with translate-only FLIP keyframes (Bram.us) or rely on Chrome 144+ no-op-dimension compositor optimization. glass-ui's spring driver sidesteps this by owning size in pixel space.

interpolate-size/calc-size second-driving an axis a JS spring also owns = a RACE that FREEZES the surface - the exact bug glass-ui hit and retired (AV.W9.0): two authorities on the dock width fought and locked it. Rule: interpolate-size only for axes the spring does NOT touch; never co-drive.

GOOEY feColorMatrix alpha-merge and SVG-filter-as-backdrop-filter refraction are CHROME-ONLY - Safari/Firefox render plain blur (no merge) or drop backdrop SVG filters. Must graceful-degrade to discrete shapes + CSS backdrop-filter blur. Animating SVG filter props (stdDeviation, displacement scale) forces a costly displacement-map REBUILD per frame - keep the filter static and morph geometry via transform/the spring.

STANDING will-change holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an idle surface - glass-ui correctly promotes will-change ONLY for the morph duration, clears to auto on settle. A facility setting will-change permanently on every morphable element would leak compositor memory UI-wide. Keep the on-demand lifecycle.

INHERITANCE-BOMB: animating an INHERITED custom property (--phase-color/--shadow-color) per frame forces a whole-subtree style recalc every frame. glass-ui routes color shifts through a DISCRETE class swap and keeps per-frame animation on transform/opacity/width/height/registered-@property non-inherited vars. A facility tweening inherited tokens would recalc the subtree each frame.

TWO spring vocabularies DRIFT: the build-time linear() CSS token and the runtime ODE MUST sample the SAME analytic spring or the VT-group curve and the JS-FLIP curve diverge (glass-ui mirrors DOCK_SPRING {0.32,0.7} to the PRESETS regen row; a retune must touch BOTH). AX.W05 excises legacy --ease-apple-spring and its 5 internal + 4 external (speedtest) consumers - deleting a token leaves var() resolving empty = transitions degrade to instant with NO error (silent clean-break breakage). Sweep consumers before excising.

prefers-reduced-motion must zero the morph on BOTH paths - VT pseudos via @media(prefers-reduced-motion){::view-transition-*{animation:none}} (state still swaps instantly) AND the JS spring via respectReducedMotion + an explicit synchronous-swap fast-path (the FLIP fallback needs the explicit JS gate; CSS can't reach the rAF). The native top-layer @starting-style half also needs PRM handling.

Listeners on a reka-ui FORWARDING component (SliderRoot) are DROPPED across the Slot/forwardRef boundary - the binding-verification class: vue-tsc + unit tests PASS, only e2e catches it. The keepDockOpen hold (a first-class morph-state input) has NEVER worked through a real drag for this reason; fix with native addEventListener on the resolved host element (AX.W03 useDockHold).

HEADLESS-GREEN over a VISUALLY-BROKEN morph - the cardinal AW failure. VT runs on invisible ::view-transition-* snapshots and the FLIP SpringProgress clock is internal, so 181 rAF getBoundingClientRect samples captured NO morph. A live morph gate must DETERMINISTICALLY drive the readable FLIP arm (force it via PRM/test-flag, lower collapse-delay, real page.hover) and assert box-geometry vs a child's opacity onset in the SAME frame - never rely on live getBoundingClientRect alone; pair with a screenshot-diff + a live 'reads as one continuous iOS spring' audit.

notes.facet: Compositor-only morph PERFORMANCE — transform/opacity/clip only, will-change discipline, the GPU path, layout-thrash avoidance
sotaTechniques: COMPOSITOR-PROPERTY TIER LADDER (the S/C/D-tier law) — only `transform`, `opacity`, `filter`, `clip-path` run entirely on the compositor thread and survive a busy main thread; `background-color`/`color`/`border-radius`/`box-shadow`/`mask-image` are C-tier (paint); `width`/`height`/`top`/`left`/`margin`/`padding`/`gap`/`grid-template` are D-tier (full layout pipeline every frame). The morph vocabulary MUST be expressible as transform+opacity+clip; anything else is a perf regression by construction. (Motion.dev tier list; Emil Kowalski.)

ON-DEMAND will-change WITH transitionend/settle TEARDOWN — `will-change` (or `translateZ(0)`) forces a standing compositor layer that holds VRAM/tile-pool budget for an IDLE element; the canonical discipline is to PROMOTE only at gesture start and DEMOTE to `auto` on `transitionend`/spring-settle, after the final paint, never as a static hint. Excessive standing layers trigger Chromium `cc` tile eviction → synchronous re-raster → dropped frames ('layer explosion'). (Chrome compositing docs; browser-rendering.com; Motion.dev 'use will-change sparingly'.)

FLIP for layout morphs (measure-once, animate transform/scale instead of width/height) — capture FIRST and LAST geometry in ONE forced-reflow batch, then drive the delta on `transform`/`scale` (B-tier: A/S-tier + a single upfront DOM measurement) so the box appears to resize while only compositor properties animate; the alternative (tweening `width`) is D-tier layout-thrash. (Motion.dev B-tier; Emil Kowalski 'never animate width/height'.)

INTERRUPTIBLE PIXEL-SPACE SPRING over View-Transitions for a LAYOUT MORPH — View Transitions are C-tier overall: the size/position half animates D-tier dimensions on snapshot pseudo-elements and CANNOT be interrupted responsively (a re-toggle mid-flight restarts from a frozen rasterized snapshot). A second-order damped spring that integrates in PIXEL space and RE-SEATS target from current `(value, velocity)` is the iOS interruptible-spring contract — the correct primitive for a gesture the user can reverse. (Motion.dev; Emil Kowalski 'springs maintain velocity when interrupted, CSS restarts from zero'.)

INHERITANCE-BOMB AVOIDANCE — never tween an INHERITED CSS custom property per frame — changing a CSS variable ALWAYS triggers paint on every element that reads it, and an INHERITED variable forces a whole-subtree style recalc (benchmarked at 1300+ elements eating an entire frame budget). Mitigation: register animated vars with `@property { inherits: false }` to scope the invalidation, and route color/phase shifts through a DISCRETE class swap, not a per-frame interpolation. (Motion.dev CSS-variables warning.)

clip-path / single-axis overflow:clip AS THE REVEAL APERTURE — `clip-path` (with `inset()`/`circle()`/`ellipse()`/compatible polygons) is compositor-eligible (and Chromium is moving it + `background-color` to automatic HW-acceleration); a single-axis `overflow: clip` is PAINT-ONLY (not a scroll container, no scroll-anchoring participation) and makes the growing box an aperture that uncovers content laid out ONCE at natural size — a layout morph with zero per-frame reflow of the revealed content. (Chrome hardware-accelerated-animations; css3shapes; Motion.dev S-tier.)

GlassEffectContainer / one-orchestrator-many-shapes morph-merge (iOS-26) — a SINGLE container batches blur+lighting+lensing ONCE for a GROUP of glass shapes and morphs individual children (tracked by id, matchedGeometry-style) into a coalesced surface within a spacing threshold; this is BOTH the visual liquid-merge AND the perf win (one unified compositing/blur pass instead of N independent backdrop-filter layers). The mental model: one clock/one driver orchestrates many child shapes' morph. (WWDC25 'Meet Liquid Glass'; GlassEffectContainer guides.)

backdrop-filter / blur COST DISCIPLINE — `backdrop-filter` auto-promotes a compositor layer AND its GPU cost escalates sharply with EVERY pixel of blur radius and with LAYER SIZE; many independent glass surfaces = many blur layers = GPU-memory blowout. Coalesce glass into fewer larger surfaces, cap blur radius via token, and never animate blur radius per frame on a large layer. (Motion.dev blur/backdrop-filter memory note.)

content-visibility:auto + contain + offscreen-pause — `content-visibility:auto` (Baseline Sept 2025) turns on layout+style+paint containment and SKIPS rendering work for offscreen subtrees (~7x initial-render win); pair with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto <fallback>` to remember last-rendered size; for always-running canvases, PARK the rAF loop when content-hidden (`contentvisibilityautostatechange`), scrolled offscreen (IntersectionObserver `rootMargin:200-500px`), or tab-backgrounded (`document.hidden`). (web.dev content-visibility; MDN; browser-rendering.com viewport-scoped promotion.)

PRM-FREEZE OWNED AT THE ENGINE, not the CSS — a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` `matchMedia` change-listener that LIVE-monitors and paints ONE static frame then parks is the engine-level reduced-motion contract; a CSS `animation: none` reset cannot reach a JS/WebGL rAF loop, so motion that lives in script must own its own PRM freeze + re-monitor. (Emil Kowalski 'respect prefers-reduced-motion'; WCAG 2.2.2 / W00 charter.)

EASE-OUT + sub-300ms + purpose-gated motion — `ease-out` (fast start, slow settle) reads as instant response; keep interaction durations under ~300ms; SKIP animation on rapidly-repeated keyboard-initiated actions where repetition amplifies perceived lag. These are the UX-craft constraints that keep a compositor-cheap morph from also feeling sluggish. (Emil Kowalski 'great animations'.)
notes.applicability: grounded
pitfalls: VIEW TRANSITIONS FOR A LAYOUT MORPH IS A TRAP — VT is C-tier: the size/position half is D-tier dimensions on rasterized snapshot pseudo-elements that CANNOT be interrupted; a re-toggle mid-morph restarts from a frozen pixel snapshot (the exact dock-desync AX.W01 retires). Use VT ONLY for the consumer route/page morph (named-element), never the dock's own interruptible collapse.

DOUBLE-DRIVING WIDTH — running an `interpolate-size`/`calc-size` CSS arm AND the JS FLIP spring on the same box freezes the morph (the AV.W9.0 regression already fixed — useLayerTransition.ts:69-71 notes the `calc-size` arm was retired). One driver writes inline size, never two.

STANDING will-change / translateZ(0) — a permanent promotion holds a compositor layer + VRAM per element; at scale this is 'layer explosion' → Chromium tile eviction → synchronous re-raster → jank. Always teardown on settle/transitionend; never ship `will-change` as a static stylesheet rule.

TWEENING AN INHERITED CSS CUSTOM PROPERTY PER FRAME — always paints, and inherited = whole-subtree style recalc (1300+ element frame-budget blowout). The `--phase-color`/`--shadow-color` inheritance bomb is already guarded; any NEW per-frame var must be `@property inherits:false` and feed only compositor properties (opacity/transform), never a paint property.

ANIMATING blur RADIUS or growing a backdrop-filter LAYER — blur cost escalates sharply per pixel of radius AND per layer area; many independent glass surfaces = many blur layers = GPU-memory blowout. Coalesce glass (GlassEffectContainer model), cap blur via token, never tween radius on a large surface.

ANIMATING A C/D-TIER PROPERTY 'because it looks right' — `box-shadow`, `border-radius`, `background-color`, `gap`, `grid-template-columns` all leave the compositor; the offset-stamp cartoon shadow + radius morph must be expressed via transform/clip/pseudo-element layers, not by tweening the shadow/radius itself (the cards.css cartoon-surface hover should fade an opacity layer, not animate box-shadow geometry).

transform: scale() RE-MINTING A STACKING CONTEXT per animation — use the `scale:` longhand (house pattern) with a `scale:1` identity base so the stacking context is minted ONCE; a `transform: scale()` on a portaled-popover-bearing dock can drop the popover below the dock mid-hover (the AQ.W3 stacking-context guarantee).

FLIP READ/WRITE INTERLEAVING (F-tier thrash) — calling getBoundingClientRect after a style write inside a loop forces sync layout each iteration; batch ALL reads then ALL writes (useLayerTransition already measures in ONE rAF origin — keep that invariant; don't add a stray read mid-drive).

content-visibility:auto WITHOUT contain-intrinsic-size — collapses offscreen elements to zero and produces scrollbar jump/CLS; always pair with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto <fallback>` so the last-rendered size is remembered.

LIVE-MEASURING THE MORPH IN A GATE — keyframes already device-proved 181 rAF getBoundingClientRect samples captured NO morph (VT runs off-main-thread, off the rAF DOM clock; AX.W00 §gate-feasibility). A perf/correctness gate must drive the morph deterministically and assert onsets in the SAME frame on the spring timeline, not poll getBoundingClientRect alone.

notes.facet: iOS spring physics — the SwiftUI .spring(response,dampingFraction) / .smooth/.snappy/.bouncy presets + the perceptual (duration,bounce) mapping, and how it grounds glass-ui's unified single-scalar morph facility
sotaTechniques: PERCEPTUAL-DURATION SPRING PARAMETERIZATION (the iOS-17+ canon). Apple deprecated the raw (response, dampingFraction) dial in favor of (duration, bounce), where `duration` is a PERCEPTUAL duration (time-to-the-meaningful-part, held constant as bounce changes) and `bounce` in [-1,1] is the overshoot dial. The closed-form physics map (Apple Dev Forums / kvin.me): mass=1; stiffness=(2pi/duration)^2; damping = (1-bounce)*4pi/duration for bounce>=0, else 4pi/(duration*(1+bounce)). bounce relates to the old damping ratio as bounce = 1 - dampingFraction (zeta). This is WHY a designer can say 'half a second, a little springy' and get a predictable settle.

CANONICAL PRESET TABLE (the targets to converge on). All three default to duration 0.5s: .smooth = bounce 0.0 (critically/over-damped, no overshoot, zeta=1), .snappy = bounce ~0.15 (small overshoot, zeta~0.85, lively), .bouncy = bounce ~0.3 (visible overshoot + brief ring, zeta~0.7). Default .spring() is response 0.55 / dampingFraction 0.825 (some refs cite 0.75). .interactiveSpring is a fast low-blend variant for gesture-tracking. These are the iOS-system motion vocabulary every Apple control breathes on.

INTERRUPTIBLE LIVE-SPRING WITH VELOCITY HANDOFF (the load-bearing iOS feel). The defining quality of iOS motion is that re-targeting MID-FLIGHT preserves current position AND velocity — the spring re-solves from where it is, never jump-cuts. SwiftUI's interpolatingSpring(...initialVelocity:) and the gesture->spring release handoff embody this. On the web this REQUIRES a live JS integrator (a per-frame ODE solve), because a CSS transition/linear() interrupt uses the spec's 'reversing shortening factor' which destroys velocity (a 1600ms spring re-runs at 400ms). Named in the literature as the single reason to choose a JS spring over a CSS spring.

iOS 26 LIQUID-GLASS MORPH = GlassEffectContainer + glassEffectID (the morph facility blueprint). Multiple glass shapes inside a `GlassEffectContainer(spacing:)` share ONE sampling region; tagging views with `.glassEffectID(id, in: namespace)` lets SwiftUI fluidly MORPH one shape into another on a state change, driven by `withAnimation(.bouncy(duration: 0.4)) { ... }`. The container's `spacing` is a gooey merge threshold — elements closer than it blend/coalesce like metaballs. `.glassEffect(.regular.interactive())` adds press-scale + shimmer + touch-point illumination that radiates to neighbors. Apple explicitly recommends the .bouncy curve for these morphs.

CSS linear() SPRING TOKEN (the build-time GPU half). The spring ODE is sampled to a `linear(0, ... , 1)` timing function (~48-75 stops for a faithful overshoot; <25 clips the peak). This gives a GPU-composited, main-thread-safe spring for FIRE-AND-FORGET transitions (entrances, hovers, non-interrupted state). ~1.3KB gzip for three max-accuracy springs; negligible runtime cost. Tools: kvin.me/css-springs, Easing Wizard, spring-easing (okikio), Open Props easings.css. The hard limit: NOT interruptible with velocity — pair it with a JS integrator for the interactive path (the two-track CPU/GPU model).

SAME-SCALAR SINGLE-CLOCK MORPH (one driver -> calc() every axis). Express a whole morph (size + radius + padding + scale + color + child stagger) as pure calc() interpolation off ONE normalized 0->1 scalar written once per frame to a CSS custom property on the root, fed by ONE analytic spring. This is the web translation of iOS's single Animatable progress driving every property in the same paint — it eliminates the multi-clock lead/lag desync (box-leads-content) that plagues split CSS-transition-vs-JS-spring designs.

VIEW TRANSITIONS API — right tool ONLY for route/shared-element morphs, NOT for a live collapse. 2025 VT is now cross-browser (Chrome 126+ cross-doc, Safari 18.2, Firefox 144) with view-transition-class, auto-naming (view-transition-name: match-element), :active-view-transition, and nested groups (Chrome 140+). But VT animates a RASTERIZED SNAPSHOT crossfade between two states — it cannot react to input mid-transition and cannot run interruptible physics. Correct for page/route morphs and thumbnail->detail shared-element expansion; WRONG for a continuously interruptible dock collapse.

WEB-PLATFORM 2025 INTRINSIC-SIZE BASELINE (interpolate-size / calc-size + @starting-style + allow-discrete + overlay). `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` and `calc-size()` finally let height/width animate to/from `auto`/intrinsic keywords (Chrome 129+; still Chromium-only as of 2025). `@starting-style` (Baseline) + `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` + `overlay` give pure-CSS entry/exit for top-layer surfaces (popover/dialog/::backdrop) without per-frame JS. These are the native substrate for the FIRE-AND-FORGET half of a morph system; @supports-gate them over a JS fallback.

PRACTITIONER CONSENSUS (Emil Kowalski / Family.co / Josh Comeau): springs over fixed-duration easings for anything that can be interrupted or reflects a physical object; ease-out (fast-start) under ~300ms for one-shot UI feedback; animate ONLY transform + opacity (composite-only, main-thread-safe); always honor prefers-reduced-motion by SIMPLIFYING (snap-to-target / fade) not deleting the feature; store spring curves as design tokens, never inline.
notes.applicability: "glass-ui is already FAR along this curve and the SOTA validates the existing architecture and the AX charter direction. Current state: an analytic SpringProgress ODE engine (in @mkbabb/keyframes.js) wrapped by useSpring/useSpringPress/useSpringMount (src/composables/motion/), named iOS presets in TWO synced sources — the JS SPRING_PRESETS table in useSpringMount.ts and the CSS --spring-{smooth,snappy,bouncy,gentle,dock} linear() tokens regenerated by scripts/regen-spring-tokens.mjs from the SAME (response, dampingFraction) pairs. THIS DUAL-TRACK (live JS integrator for the interruptible path + build-time linear() for fire-and-forget GPU transitions) IS the SOTA two-track model, already implemented.
