WHERE THE SOTA SHOULD STEER THE WAVES: (1) PERCEPTUAL-DURATION RE-PARAMETERIZATION — glass-ui's presets are keyed on the OLD (response, dampingFraction) dial; the iOS-17+ canon is (duration, bounce). W05's 'small governed iOS-spring vocabulary (settle/control/playful)' should adopt (perceptualDuration, bounce) as the authoring surface (regen-spring-tokens.mjs PRESETS table gains duration+bounce, derives response/zeta via bounce=1-zeta and the stiffness/damping closed form) so the vocabulary speaks Apple's current language and 'settle/control/playful' map cleanly to smooth(0.0)/snappy(0.15)/bouncy(0.3). (2) W01 SINGLE-SCALAR ONE-CLOCK MORPH is textbook-correct and SOTA-blessed: the charter's '--dock-morph-t written once per frame, every axis as calc()' is precisely iOS's single-Animatable-progress model, and 'RETIRE the View-Transitions fork' is validated by the 2025 VT-is-a-rasterized-snapshot finding (VT cannot run the interruptible layout morph; it is right ONLY for fourier's route-morph named-element seam, which W01 correctly preserves separately). The live-SpringProgress-on-every-engine decision is mandated by the CSS-linear()-cannot-preserve-velocity limitation. (3) THE UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY (path forward) is glass-ui's GlassEffectContainer analog: generalize W01's dock single-scalar driver into a reusable useMorph(targetScalar, {preset})-style primitive that ANY glass primitive binds — Button press (useSpringPress already does this), Card hover, dialog mount (useSpringMount), dock collapse, layer crossfade — all reading ONE shared spring vocabulary so the whole system 'breathes on the same spring' (W05's explicit goal: slider-in-dock and dock on one curve). The gooey-merge GlassEffectContainer(spacing:) maps to the existing GooBlob metaball smin work — a future 'glass elements within N px coalesce' container is the natural iOS-26 parity target. (4) W09 specular/press-illumination is the .interactive() analog (press-scale + touch-point light radiating to neighbors); tie the specular intensity ramp to the same press spring scalar so light and squish share one clock. (5) W20's native-top-layer @starting-style/allow-discrete grammar (already in animations.css §TOP-LAYER) is the correct fire-and-forget native substrate — keep it @supports-gated over the JS spring path, exactly as the two-track model prescribes."
pitfalls: VELOCITY-LOSS ON INTERRUPT is the #1 hazard and the whole reason for the dual-track. Any axis that falls back to a CSS transition / linear() / View-Transition for an INTERRUPTIBLE gesture (drag-release, rapid collapse-toggle, collapse-while-switching) will jump-cut on re-target — the spec's reversing-shortening-factor discards inertia. Every interactive morph axis MUST be driven by the live SpringProgress integrator, not the linear() token. This is exactly the W01 'one live spring on every engine' mandate; do not regress an axis onto CSS-transition for convenience.

linear() SAMPLE-COUNT UNDER-REPRESENTS OVERSHOOT. The regen pipeline already learned this (raised 24->48 samples in AM-W2 because ζ=0.45 bouncy clips its peak at 24). Any new lower-damping/higher-bounce preset needs the peak verified against the analytic 1+exp(-ζπ/√(1-ζ²)) — a coarse grid silently flattens the bounce and the token lies about the curve. The proof:spring-tokens-synced gate must render overshoot at runtime from the imported constant, not a hand-typed number (W05 fold).

PERCEPTUAL vs SETTLING DURATION CONFUSION. If the vocabulary is re-keyed to (duration, bounce), `duration` is PERCEPTUAL (the meaningful-motion window), NOT the full settle time — a bouncy spring keeps ringing well past `duration`. Conflating them makes settle-threshold tuning and any 'animation done' gate wrong. The settleThreshold/velocitySettleThreshold in useSpring are the real end-of-motion signal; don't gate on duration.

VT IS THE WRONG PRIMITIVE FOR A LAYOUT MORPH — but the per-instance view-transition-name SEAM is a real cross-repo dependency. W01 must retire the COLLAPSE VT fork while PRESERVING glass-dock-${useId()} for fourier's route-morph (the charter flags this; the two-co-mounted-docks duplicate-name collision that drops the snapshot is the corroborating witness). Killing the name outright reds ~13 fourier e2e.

SILENT TOKEN-DELETION CLEAN-BREAK. Excising --ease-apple-spring/--motion-ease-apple-spring (W05) leaves var(--ease-apple-spring) resolving EMPTY in 5 internal + 4 external speedtest sites -> transitions degrade to instant/linear with NO error. A no-survivor sweep across library AND consumers must gate the excision (W05 explicitly).

prefers-reduced-motion MUST SIMPLIFY, NOT DELETE. useSpring's respectReducedMotion snaps-to-target (correct). But the WebGL substrate freeze and the CSS @media PRM carve are SEPARATE gates; a morph axis that lives only in calc() off --dock-morph-t needs its own PRM path (snap the scalar) — a CSS reset cannot reach a JS-written custom property. Audit every morph axis for an independent reduce path.

OVER-BOUNCE READS AS BROKEN, NOT PLAYFUL. The AW.W2 retune already walked the dock spring DOWN from +18.5% to ~+4.6% overshoot because the playful register read as 'not iOS-smooth / alive in a bad way'. iOS system controls sit in the snappy/control register (bounce ~0.15, ζ~0.85), NOT bouncy. Reserve bouncy (~0.3) for deliberate emphatic moments (dialog entrance, success), keep structural morphs (dock, layout) in the control register.

COMPOSITING / STACKING-CONTEXT TRAPS. Animate transform + opacity only (composite-only). Prefer the `scale:`/`translate:` longhands over `transform: scale()` where you must avoid minting a stacking context (animations.css already does this for the top-layer grammar). A morph that animates width/padding/border-radius (layout/paint) on the main thread is acceptable for the dock box BUT must stay off the per-child hot path — keep child stagger on transform/opacity.

DON'T MINT DEAD PRESETS. W05's overfitting census is real: a generated --spring-* with zero consumers is substrate-without-consumer. Keep the governed vocabulary SMALL (the SOTA is literally three: smooth/snappy/bouncy). glass-ui's smooth/snappy/bouncy/gentle/dock is already at the edge — justify each against ≥1 live consumer or fold it.

notes.facet: Interruptible / retargeting fluid transitions — velocity-preserving re-aim mid-flight (the iOS gesture-driven feel)
sotaTechniques: VELOCITY-PRESERVING RETARGET (the core primitive). When a target changes while a spring is still integrating, the new motion seeds its initial velocity from the spring's CURRENT velocity at the moment of interruption — the closed-form solution is re-derived from the live (position, velocity) pair, not reconstructed from rest. This is what 'the iOS feel' literally IS: a flicked/redirected element keeps its speed and arcs to the new destination. Reference engines: jtrivedi/Wave ('retargeting is the process of preserving an animation's velocity even as its target changes'), b3ll/Motion, SwiftUI UISpringTimingParameters.

GESTURE-VELOCITY HANDOFF. At gesture-end (pointerup/touchend) the pointer's instantaneous velocity is computed and fed as the spring's initialVelocity, normalized to remaining distance: relativeVelocity = |pointerVelocity| / distanceRemaining. The animation continues from exactly the speed the finger left it at — no perceptible discontinuity between drag and settle. Apple's canonical 'Building Fluid Interfaces' pattern (Nathan Gitter / WWDC).

SPRING-AS-SINGLE-CLOCK over DURATION. Springs are the ONLY interruptible primitive because they carry state (position+velocity) frame to frame; duration/keyframe animations restart from zero on interrupt (the jarring snap). 'Try to avoid thinking about duration… forcing a duration on a spring feels unnatural.' Parameterize by (response, dampingFraction/bounce) — Apple's response+bounce model is easier to reason about than mass/stiffness/damping. Emil Kowalski: 'Springs maintain velocity when interrupted — CSS animations and keyframes restart from zero.'

INTERRUPTIBLE/REDIRECTABLE-BY-DEFAULT doctrine. Every auto-running animation must be stoppable AND re-aimable mid-flight at any time (UIViewPropertyAnimator stopAnimation/startAnimation). 'Interruption is critical — because springs spend most of their time near their final value, users think it's done and interact again.' Chrome Modern Web Guidance 2025 echoes it as a platform rule: 'All animations must be smoothly interruptible mid-sequence; users should never feel locked into waiting.'

iOS-26 LIQUID GLASS MORPH via matched IDs. SwiftUI glassEffectID + GlassEffectContainer: when glass views appear/disappear due to hierarchy changes and share an ID, the glass SHAPE morphs fluidly between states (one continuous transform, not a crossfade). The web analog is a shared-element layout morph driven by ONE spring — geometry interpolated, not pixels crossfaded. The 'interactive' modifier adds scale/bounce/shimmer on touch.

SINGLE-SCALAR MORPH ORCHESTRATION. Drive EVERY animated axis (width/inline-size, padding, radius, scale, color, child-stagger onset) from ONE normalized spring scalar (0→1) written once per frame to a CSS custom property, expressed via calc()/interpolation. One clock = no lead/lag desync between box and content; an interrupt retargets the single scalar and the whole composite re-aims coherently (no orphaned per-axis timers). This is the AX.W01 charter design.

PROGRESS-KEYED CHILD STAGGER (physical, not timer-based). Map child opacity/transform onset to a per-child THRESHOLD against the morph spring's normalized progress scalar, not a fixed setTimeout ladder. A fast flick and a slow hover both choreograph correctly, and an interrupted morph carries the cascade with it — no orphaned timers to cancel. glass-ui already does this (--dock-morph-progress, AW.W3).

FLIP WITH VELOCITY CARRY (layout morph in JS). First-Last-Invert-Play measures start/end boxes and animates the delta on transform; the SOTA refinement (Motion's layout engine) makes the Play phase a SPRING that carries velocity across interrupts, so a re-layout mid-animation re-measures and re-aims from the live transform without snapping. Interruptible, doesn't block pointer events, handles concurrent animations — unlike the naive precalc-stomps-in-flight FLIP.

CSS linear() SPRING — interruptible-FRIENDLY but NOT retargetable. A real spring curve baked into a many-point linear() easing gives CSS transitions overshoot/bounce; a CSS TRANSITION (not @keyframes) can be interrupted and will smoothly redirect to a new value. BUT linear() is a fixed sampled curve — it does NOT preserve velocity on retarget (the browser re-runs the same baked curve from the current value at default speed). Good for entrances/non-interactive bounce; insufficient for gesture-driven re-aim.

interpolate-size / calc-size() for intrinsic-size morphs. Chrome 129+ enables transition/animation between pixel lengths and intrinsic keywords (auto, min-content, fit-content). Lets a content-driven box animate width/height to:auto natively. CAVEAT (glass-ui learned this at AV.W9.0): pairing interpolate-size CSS width with a JS spring that ALSO writes inline width creates two drivers that fight and freeze the morph — pick ONE size authority.

@starting-style + top-layer entry/exit. Baseline-2025 grammar for animating popover/dialog/[data-state] surfaces from a defined start state on first paint (no JS mount-tween needed for the enter). Composes with the spring facility for the press/interactive state; the entrance rides @starting-style, the interactive re-aim rides the JS spring.
notes.applicability: SEE facet/applicability fields — bound to glass-ui source: useLayerTransition.ts AV.W9.2 retarget (lines 311-439), AX.W01 single-scalar charter, useSpring/useSpringPress initialVelocity wiring gap, AX.W03 useDockHold gesture handoff, AX.W20/W09 glass-material morph substrate.
pitfalls: VIEW TRANSITIONS ARE UNINTERRUPTIBLE. VT snapshots pixels and plays a fixed curve; interrupting it mid-flight visually breaks or no-ops. It is the WRONG primitive for any gesture-driven/retargetable layout morph. The two-co-mounted-docks VT-name collision in fourier (both mint glass-dock-1 → dropped snapshot, ~13 red e2e) is the concrete witness. Use VT only for one-shot route/page morphs; never for the dock's own collapse or a draggable surface.

TWO SIZE AUTHORITIES FIGHT AND FREEZE. AV.W9.0 hit this: interpolate-size/calc-size CSS second-driving width while a JS spring also writes inline width froze the dock on Chrome 129+. Pick ONE size authority per morph — either the CSS interpolate-size arm OR the JS spring's per-frame inline write, never both. The JS driver must hold `transition: none` on the element it owns.

DISPOSE-ON-INTERRUPT ZEROES VELOCITY. The anti-pattern is dispose()+new-spring-from-rest on a re-toggle — the morph snaps from zero velocity (the jarring non-iOS re-toggle). MUST re-seat target on the LIVE solver (the AV.W9.2 fix). Guard: only reuse if the spring is non-null, unsettled, AND driving the same element (springEl === el && !spring.settled).

linear() CANNOT RETARGET. A linear() spring is a baked sample of a curve; on interrupt the browser re-runs that same curve from the current value at default rate — no velocity preservation. Fine for entrances and non-interactive bounce; insufficient for the gesture re-aim tier. Do not reach for linear() to get 'interruptible iOS feel' on interactive surfaces.

INHERITANCE BOMB — never tween an inherited custom property per frame. Animating an inherited var (--phase-color, --shadow-color) forces a whole-subtree style recalc every frame. glass-ui's convention (useLayerTransition F5) is correct: spring drives only transform/opacity/width/height; color shifts ride a DISCRETE class swap, never frame interpolation. The morph facility must keep this.

STANDING will-change holds a compositor layer + VRAM for idle surfaces. Promote will-change:<dim> ONLY for the gesture duration; clear to auto on settle/transitionend (the AV.W7 F3 lifecycle). A permanent hint on an idle dock is a memory/perf regression.

ORPHANED setTimeout STAGGER ladders desync on interrupt. A fixed-ms child stagger (0.08/0.16/…) cannot follow a retargeted or flicked morph and leaves dangling timers. Key the stagger off the spring's normalized progress scalar instead (timer-free, interrupt-carrying).

OVERSHOOT past 1 on the progress scalar — clamp [0,1] when driving child-stagger thresholds; an under-damped spring pushes progress past 1 (children already revealed) and a non-clamped onset would non-monotonically re-arm. glass-ui clamps; keep it.

prefers-reduced-motion must SNAP, not spring — and the gate is needed on BOTH the JS spring (respectReducedMotion) AND any CSS path; the FLIP/JS fallback needs an explicit JS PRM gate (useLayerTransition lines 296-305) because the CSS VT PRM gate doesn't reach it. A unified facility must not lose this belt-and-suspenders.

Settle-detection races the last paint. Clear will-change / clip-aperture / stagger AFTER the final settle frame, not before, or the clear flashes the last frame. Plus a safety setTimeout(cleanupDelayMs) in case the settle callback is missed — the morph must never strand an inline width.

notes.facet: Morph CHOREOGRAPHY — the order/stagger of sub-element morphing, lead-follow, and content reveal in-step with the box (the unified iOS-26 Liquid-Glass morph facility for glass-ui's dock + animation + glass primitives)
sotaTechniques: SINGLE-SCALAR ONE-CLOCK MORPH (the choreography spine): drive EVERY animated axis of the box AND its children off one normalized analytic-spring progress scalar (0->1) written once per frame to a CSS custom property on the root; express width/padding/radius/scale/color AND each child's reveal as pure calc() off that one scalar so box and content settle in the same paint, never on separate clocks. This is the prerequisite for lead-follow: a single progress timeline you can phase per-element. (glass-ui's AX.W01 names this exactly --dock-morph-t; today the FLIP path writes --dock-morph-progress per frame but the root chrome still rides separate CSS transitions, so box leads content ~16ms.)

MATCHED-GEOMETRY / SHARED-ELEMENT MORPH (the box-shape continuity primitive): the box itself does not fade between states - the SAME element's geometry (frame, corner-radius, shadow) interpolates from source to destination. SwiftUI's glassEffectID(_:in:namespace) + matchedGeometryEffect and the web's view-transition-name are the two implementations: tag the persistent element with a stable identity and the engine morphs its box rather than crossfading two boxes. Apple's GlassEffectTransition.matchedGeometry is the DEFAULT transition. The corollary discipline: name the element that should morph, NOT its wrapper (name the image not the card) or the wrong box morphs.

BACKDROP -> CONTAINER -> CONTENT -> ACTIONS ordering (Emil Kowalski's canonical lead-follow sequence): elements enter in depth order - the scrim/backdrop first, then the container box morphs, then the content reveals, then the interactive actions land last. The box LEADS; content FOLLOWS in-step (not after). This is the choreography ordering glass-ui's per-child onset ladder already approximates outer->in, but the named depth ordering is the canonical refinement.

FOLLOW-THROUGH & OVERLAPPING ACTION (Rauno Freiberg, Disney-principle applied to UI): things do not stop all at once - sub-elements lag the main transition by a small delay so the row settles in a cascade, not a block. Rauno's concrete number: icons and labels appear with 100-200ms subtle delays after the main transition; Emil's: 30-60ms BETWEEN staggered items, never >100ms (that reads as a slideshow). Crucial nuance: the stagger should ride the MORPH's progress, not a wall-clock timer, so a fast flick and a slow hover-open both choreograph correctly.

MATERIALIZE vs CROSSFADE (Liquid-Glass content-reveal idiom): revealed content does not opacity-fade in - it 'materializes' by gradually modulating light-bending/refraction so the glass surface appears to solidify into view. SwiftUI exposes GlassEffectTransition.materialize for this. On the web the analog is the clip-reveal aperture (content laid out once at natural size behind a growing overflow:clip box that uncovers it) + @starting-style scale/opacity entry on the newly-revealed elements - NOT a height/opacity keyframe that re-lays-out per frame.

PROXIMITY/SPACING-BASED MERGE + UNION (GlassEffectContainer): nearby glass shapes within a spacing threshold automatically blend and morph into one unified shape during a transition (the spacing param is the merge distance, ~<=40pt); shapes too far to merge naturally are explicitly grouped via glassEffectUnion(id:). The container provides ONE shared sampling region so glass never samples glass (the nesting pitfall). This is the 'singular floating plane' concept: controls read as one continuous surface reshaping, not discrete objects.

INTERRUPTIBLE / RE-TARGETABLE SPRING (Family/Wave principle): every morph is re-targetable - changing the destination mid-flight re-seats the spring from its CURRENT (value, velocity) and arcs to the new target rather than snapping from rest. This is what makes a re-toggle-while-animating read as iOS-fluid. glass-ui ALREADY does this via SpringProgress velocity-continuity (AV.W9.2 set target re-seat); the charter's job is to make it the ONLY path (universal, not FLIP-only).

NATIVE CSS SIZE-INTERPOLATION + ENTRY GRAMMAR (web-platform 2025 baseline for the box+content reveal): interpolate-size:allow-keywords / calc-size() animate a container to width/height:auto so the box grows to its content's intrinsic size; @starting-style + transition-behavior:allow-discrete + overlay animate the newly-revealed content's entry (the platform owns the per-frame interpolation, no JS rAF). Chrome 129+ only (no Safari/FF as of 2025) - progressive enhancement, not a contract. CAUTION: must be mutually exclusive with a JS spring on the same property (glass-ui's AV.W9.0 retired exactly this dual-driver race that froze the dock).

NESTED VIEW-TRANSITION GROUPS + ANIMATION INHERITANCE (Chrome 140, 2025): ::view-transition-group can nest to restore DOM hierarchy during a transition (clipping, 3D) and a parent group's animation-* longhands INHERIT to its child pairs - so a container morph and its contained element morphs stay synchronized by construction, with the children able to morph independently within the parent's clock. view-transition-name:match-element auto-names list items; element.startViewTransition() scopes a transition to a subtree (multiple concurrent roots). This is the web's structural answer to GlassEffectContainer's coordinated nested morph.

GOVERNED SPRING VOCABULARY (settle/control/playful, the iOS smooth/snappy/bouncy register): one small named spring set, NOT per-surface bezier forks. iOS ships smooth (no overshoot), snappy (~small overshoot, lively), bouncy (clear overshoot+oscillation, playful) as the defaults across the OS; .bouncy at 0.3-0.4s is the documented glass-morph preset. The choreography rule: the box and EVERYTHING inside it (a dock and its slider thumb) share ONE register so the whole assembly breathes on the same curve (glass-ui AX.W05 excises the legacy --ease-apple-spring and pins the dock register to the published (0.32,0.7) ~+4.6% --spring-dock).
notes.applicability: Glass-ui is already ~70% of the way to the SOTA morph facility and the AX charter codifies the rest. CONCRETE MAPPING: (1) AX.W01 single-scalar one-clock morph IS the choreography spine - it converges the current split (root chrome on CSS transitions in dock.css:326-340 vs inner width on the SpringProgress in useLayerTransition.ts:409) onto one --dock-morph-t scalar the box AND children read, which is exactly what makes 'content reveal in-step with the box' true rather than the current ~16ms box-leads-content desync. The per-child opacity/translate calc ramp (dock.css:754-795) is ALREADY the right primitive - it just needs to read the unified root scalar, not a FLIP-only --dock-morph-progress that the VT path never arms. (2) The lead-follow ORDER should adopt Emil's backdrop->container->content->actions depth ordering: today the onset ladder is a flat outer->in nth-child cascade (0/0.08/0.16/0.24/0.32/0.4); AX.W02 already plans to replace the hand-typed ladder with one --dock-stagger-step token x child-index - that token's value should land in Emil's 30-60ms-equiv window (as a fraction of morph progress) and the SEPARATOR/structural children should onset before the action buttons (depth, not just position). (3) The clip-reveal aperture (dock.css:111-161, data-morphing-gated single-axis overflow:clip) IS the web's materialize idiom - content laid out once at natural size, the growing box uncovers it. Keep it; it is the correct Liquid-Glass content-reveal mechanism and already PRM-safe. (4) GlassEffectContainer's matched-geometry box morph maps to the dock's pill<->card radius interpolation (dock.css:332-337, border-radius on the same spring) and the per-instance view-transition-name seam (GlassDock.vue:280) that fourier route-morphs through - AX.W01's critical constraint is to retire the COLLAPSE VT fork (wrong primitive for a layout morph) while PRESERVING the named-element ROUTE morph (the right primitive for a shared-element page transition). These are the SwiftUI 'glassEffectID identity morph' applied at two scales: collapse=intra-component, route=cross-route. (5) GlassEffectContainer spacing/union -> the dock's 'singular floating plane' is the DockLayerGroup; AX.W02 folds the inner layer-group onto the outer driver (one orchestrator) which is precisely the 'one shared sampling region, don't nest glass-in-glass' discipline. (6) Re-targetable spring: glass-ui's SpringProgress velocity-continuity already IS Wave's retargeting - AX.W01 makes it universal. THE PATH FORWARD (unified morph facility): expose a single useMorph(rootRef, {axes}) composable on the /dock and /motion barrels that owns one SpringProgress, writes --morph-t once per frame, and lets ANY primitive (dock, dialog, drawer, popover, glass-panel) opt EVERY axis (size/radius/shadow/scale/color/child-stagger) into pure-calc interpolation off that one scalar - the generalization of useLayerTransition from dock-only to the whole glass family. This makes the iOS-26 'every UI element morphs' goal a library-wide primitive, not a dock special case. Pair it with the governed settle/control/playful spring register (AX.W05) so a dialog, a dock, and a drawer all breathe on the same curves.
pitfalls: DUAL-DRIVER RACE (the #1 hazard, glass-ui already hit it): never let two authorities drive the same property on the same axis. AV.W9.0/W9.1 retired the native interpolate-size CSS arm AND the discrete-visibility arm precisely because they second-drove width/opacity while the SpringProgress wrote inline px per frame - cancelling the morph and FREEZING the dock at runtime. Rule: one owner per concern (size=spring/VT, opacity=CSS crossfade, visibility=delayed-hold). interpolate-size and a JS spring are mutually exclusive on the same property, always.

BOX-LEADS-CONTENT DESYNC (~16ms): the current split-clock arrangement (root chrome on synchronous CSS-class-flip transitions vs inner width on a JS spring deferred a frame behind via nextTick->rAF->reflow) makes the box visibly arrive before its content. The single-scalar one-clock morph is the ONLY robust fix; any architecture with separate root-vs-inner clocks reintroduces it.

VIEW-TRANSITIONS IS THE WRONG PRIMITIVE FOR A LAYOUT MORPH: VT crossfades RASTERIZED pixels of old vs new - acceptable for a shared-element page/route morph (fourier's viz<->workspace), wrong for a continuous in-place box resize (it produces the uncaptured-animating-ancestor desync and the two-co-mounted-docks duplicate-view-transition-name collision that DROPS the snapshot + reds e2e). Use a live spring for the layout morph; reserve VT/matched-geometry for cross-route shared elements. Keep the two seams SEPARABLE.

STAGGER TOO LONG READS AS A SLIDESHOW: >100ms between items (Emil) or stagger that ignores the morph's actual duration. The cascade must ride the morph's normalized progress (a fraction-of-morph onset), not a fixed setTimeout/animation-delay wall clock - otherwise a fast flick desyncs the cascade from the box and an interrupted morph orphans timers. glass-ui's progress-keyed ramp is correct; do not regress it to a timer cascade.

INHERITANCE BOMB (per-frame inherited-custom-property tween): animating an INHERITED custom property (--phase-color, --shadow-color) per frame forces a whole-subtree style recalc every frame. glass-ui's F5 convention is correct - tween only transform/opacity/width/height; route color shifts through a discrete class swap, never a per-frame interpolation of an inherited var.

STANDING will-change / permanent compositor layer: a permanent will-change holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an idle surface. Promote only for the gesture duration (set at morph start, clear to auto on settle/transitionend), exactly as glass-ui's F3 on-demand lifecycle does. Apple's parallel guidance: let glass REST in steady states, avoid continuous animation - it is GPU/thermal-bound on older devices.

GLASS-ON-GLASS SAMPLING (SwiftUI) / clip-lift-at-frame-0 (web): nesting .glassEffect() inside .glassEffect() produces sampling errors - always one shared container/sampling region. The web analog: lifting overflow:clip to visible at frame 0 (bound to the synchronous expanded state) leaves NO aperture to reveal through - gate the clip on data-morphing so it holds for the WHOLE gesture and lifts only on the final paint (glass-ui AW.W2 fixed exactly this).

PRM (prefers-reduced-motion) must collapse the WHOLE choreography, not just the box: under reduce the stagger must flush synchronously (no cascade), spatial axes (width/translate/scale) strip from transition-property, and the materialize flattens to an instant reveal. A morph facility that only PRM-gates the box but still cascades children fails WCAG 2.3.3 / reads as motion. glass-ui gates this at multiple layers (FLIP fast-path returns before the spring, CSS arms children only while data-revealing) - any new morph primitive must inherit all of them.

NAMING THE WRONG ELEMENT for a shared-element morph: tag the persistent element that should morph (the image, the dock-layer box), NOT its surrounding wrapper/card - else the browser morphs padding+background+caption and the intended element jumps. And a DUPLICATE view-transition-name across two co-mounted instances drops the snapshot entirely (the fourier two-dock collision) - names must be per-instance unique (useId-derived).

notes.facet: The @mkbabb/keyframes.js SpringProgress runtime — driving a morph off it, linear() spring-token generation, and the existing dock spring
sotaTechniques: Single-scalar analytic spring → one CSS custom property (the iOS-26 morph kernel). The whole 'every UI element morphs' facility reduces to: integrate ONE second-order damped-harmonic ODE (SpringProgress) to produce a normalized 0→1 scalar per frame, write it once to a CSS var on the root (`--dock-morph-t`/`--morph-t`), and express EVERY animated axis — width/inline-size, padding, border-radius, scale, bg/border color, child-stagger — as pure calc()/interpolation off that one scalar. One clock, one paint, zero per-axis CSS transitions. This is exactly Apple's 'singular floating plane the controls live on' model and is AX.W01's headline. glass-ui already HAS the engine (SpringProgress via useSpring) and the high-water reference impl in git e8380d7 (~135 lines); the live regression is accreted multi-authority drift.

linear() spring-token generation (build-time CSS-native spring). springLinearStops({response, dampingFraction, sampleCount}) samples the SAME SpringProgress ODE at N uniform points and emits a `linear(0, v1 p1%, v2 p2%, …, 1)` string — a piecewise-linear approximation of the spring curve that cubic-bezier physically CANNOT express (bezier only makes S-curves; linear() overshoots and returns → real bounce/overshoot). This is the Jake Archibald/Adam Argyle linear()-easing-generator technique, productionized in glass-ui's regen-spring-tokens.mjs. Baseline: Chrome/Edge 113+, Firefox 112+, Safari 17.2+ (broadly shippable). It is the GPU/CPU-shared curve — a `transition: width var(--spring-dock)` samples the identical motion the JS integrator does.

Sample-count fidelity rule for overshoot faithfulness. The linear() approximation must REPRESENT the solver, not a clipped version. glass-ui raised SAMPLE_COUNT 24→48 (~2% grid) precisely because a coarse uniform grid straddles and clips the first peak — bouncy ζ=0.45 analytically peaks at 1 + exp(-ζπ/√(1-ζ²)) ≈ 1.2054 but a 24-sample grid reads ~1.1833 (~2pp under-represented). 48 samples lands bouncy 1.2048 / snappy 1.0680 within target. The token-peak is a trivially-falsifiable gate input (`--spring-dock` linear() ramp peak ≤ published +4.6%).

The governed iOS-spring vocabulary as (response, dampingFraction) source-of-truth. Apple's modern API is `spring(duration, bounce)`; glass-ui's canonical pairs are response (angular period, s) + ζ (damping ratio: 1=critical/no-overshoot, <1=rings, >1=overdamped). The named register: smooth (0.5,0.86), snappy (0.35,0.65,+6.8%), bouncy (0.5,0.45,+20.5%), gentle (0.7,1.0 critically-damped), dock (0.32,0.7,~+4.6% — iOS-control settled). One table is the truth; both the JS runtime (SPRING_PRESETS in useSpringMount) and the CSS tokens (regen script) MUST encode the identical pairs, lockstep-enforced.

Interruptible velocity-preserved spring (the iOS 'feels alive' property). SpringProgress integrates a live ODE that carries velocity across a mid-flight re-target: re-seating `.target` hands the current (position, velocity) into the new trajectory with NO jump. This is THE reason springs beat duration-easing for gesture UI (Emil Kowalski: 'springs maintain velocity when interrupted; CSS keyframes restart from zero'). useSpringMount already exploits it — drag re-seats target every pointermove, release decides bounce-back (target=0) vs dismiss (target=1) and the spring continues from live velocity. The morph facility should run this LIVE spring universally (not only a FLIP fallback), so collapse/expand interrupted mid-flight reverses smoothly.

FLIP measured-morph off the spring scalar (animating layout the GPU-cheap way). useLayerTransition measures natural box geometry before/after a slot swap, then drives the delta with the SpringProgress scalar — the spring interpolates between two fixed pixel values so `width:auto` non-interpolation is sidestepped and the morph stays on transform/opacity where possible. The keyframes.js LIGHT-barrel `flip()` trigger is the canonical primitive (avoid a third hand-roll). Pair with clip-reveal aperture: lay content out ONCE at natural size, the box uncovers it (no reflow per frame).

iOS-26 GlassEffectContainer + glassEffectID (the shared-element morph model to mirror in CSS). SwiftUI's container merges neighboring glass shapes when within a `spacing` threshold (droplets fusing) and morphs shape A→B via `.glassEffectID(id, in: namespace)` (the matchedGeometryEffect successor). The web analogue is View-Transitions named elements (`view-transition-name`) for cross-state/route geometry morphs — the right primitive for shared-element/route morphs, the WRONG primitive for the dock's OWN collapse (VT crossfades rasterized snapshots → desync with an animating ancestor). AX.W01 separates these: retire the collapse-VT fork, PRESERVE the per-instance `view-transition-name` route-morph seam fourier consumes.

interpolate-size + calc-size() (the CSS-native intrinsic-size morph). `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` + `calc-size(auto, size)` make width/height interpolate to/from intrinsic keywords (auto/max-content) natively — the long-missing 'animate to height:auto'. Chrome/Edge 129+ only (no Safari/Firefox as of 2025), so it is an @supports-gated PROGRESSIVE-ENHANCEMENT over the FLIP+spring fallback, NEVER a co-driver. glass-ui learned this the hard way: the AU.W8b native container-morph arm raced the SpringProgress FLIP over the same `width` property and FROZE the dock (AV.W9.0 retired it). One authority per property, always.

Concentric shape interpolation + material-thickness response (the Liquid-Glass look layered on the morph). Apple morphs the capsule geometry concentrically (mirrored radii, hardware-concentric corners) and as glass flexes larger it simulates thicker material — deeper shadows, more pronounced lensing/refraction, softer specular scatter. Mapped to glass-ui: interpolate `--dock-card-radius`, `--shadow-dock-wrap` (card-tier shadow on the wrapped silhouette), and the `--glass-specular-intensity-*` ladder off the SAME `--morph-t` so the surface reads thicker as it expands (AX.W04 shadow/radius + AX.W09 specular ladder). The press micro-spring (`--dock-press-spring`, transform-only scale/rotate squish) is the small-end of the same vocabulary.

Reduced-motion as a spring fast-path, not a separate code path. Apple's Reduce Motion 'disables elastic properties' of the material; the web rule is animate only transform/opacity and snap-to-target under PRM. SpringProgress's `respectReducedMotion` snaps to target instantly (no integration phase) so the morph is linear-equivalent and gestures still resolve — useSpring/useSpringMount already bracket this. The global PRM gate in utilities.css strips width/translate/min-height from transition-property so spatial morph degrades to an opacity snap with zero per-component PRM branches.
notes.applicability: THE PATH FORWARD for a unified morph facility (every element gets the iOS-26 springy/liquid morph): (1) Promote SpringProgress to ONE morph orchestrator per surface. AX.W01 collapses the dock onto a single live SpringProgress writing `--dock-morph-t` (0→1) to the `.glass-dock` root once per frame; every axis (width/padding/radius/scale/color/child-stagger) is calc()/interpolation off that scalar — no root CSS transition, no VT-vs-FLIP fork, no inner-vs-outer clock. AX.W02 folds the nested DockLayerGroup onto the SAME orchestrator via provide/inject (model the dock as one stack whose active layer = expandedState × activePane). This is directly generalizable beyond the dock: expose a `useMorph(rootRef, target)` primitive (SpringProgress + the FLIP measure + the `--morph-t` write) on the /dock and /motion subpaths so ANY container (sheet, popover, card, configurator) becomes a one-scalar morph host — and value.js DELETES its local FLIP-width fork (substrate-with-consumer). (2) Keep the linear() token pipeline as the CSS-native arm for non-interruptible, declarative morphs (transitions/keyframes that never need mid-flight re-target) — regen-spring-tokens.mjs already ties (response,ζ) → linear() from the SAME solver, so CPU spring and GPU transition sample one curve. AX.W05 governs ONE vocabulary: excise the legacy `--ease-apple-spring` cubic-bezier (+27.5%, a SECOND spring vocabulary), re-point its 5 internal + 4 speedtest consumers onto the governed register, and make the dock + its slider thumb breathe on the SAME `--spring-dock` curve. (3) Held/gesture state is a FIRST-CLASS morph input (AX.W03): `useDockHold(rootRef)` attaches native pointerdown/touchstart on the resolved host (fixing the reka forwarding-drop), and `held`/drag-velocity feed the spring's target/re-seat synchronously — interruptible by construction. (4) Layer the Liquid-Glass LOOK on the morph scalar: concentric radius (`--dock-card-radius`, AX.W04), card-tier shadow on the wrapped/expanded silhouette (`--shadow-dock-wrap`), and the warm-cream tokenized specular ladder `--glass-specular-intensity-{rest,hover,active}` that intensifies as the surface 'thickens' (AX.W09, with `useSpecularTracking`). The native intrinsic-size morph (interpolate-size/calc-size) and View-Transitions named-element route-morph are @supports/feature-gated PROGRESSIVE upgrades over the universal SpringProgress+FLIP baseline — never co-drivers on the same property. Net: SpringProgress is the single physics kernel; linear() tokens are its build-time CSS projection; FLIP is its layout adapter; the glass material tokens are its visual skin — one engine drives the whole 'every element morphs' facility.
pitfalls: DUAL-DRIVER RACE on the same property is the #1 hazard and a PROVEN dock-freeze. The AU.W8b native container-morph (`@supports` auto-to-length width interpolation on the browser's clock) ran WHILE SpringProgress wrote inline `width` per frame → the two cancelled and froze the dock (born-RED, retired AV.W9.0). Rule: exactly ONE authority per animated property per engine. interpolate-size/calc-size and the FLIP spring must be mutually exclusive (@supports-gated), never both.

VT is the WRONG primitive for a self-contained layout morph. View-Transitions crossfade RASTERIZED `::view-transition-*` snapshots; an animating ancestor desyncs and the morph reads as a cross-dissolve, not a continuous spring. The fourier two-co-mounted-docks collision (both mint `glass-dock-1` → duplicate name DROPS the snapshot, reds ~13 e2e) is the corroborating witness. Retire the collapse-VT fork but PRESERVE the per-instance `view-transition-name` seam consumers route-morph through — these are separable concerns the charter previously conflated.

Box-leads-content desync from multi-clock authorship. Root padding/radius on synchronous CSS-class-flip transitions + inner width on a JS spring deferred a frame (nextTick→rAF→reflow) makes the box lead content by ~16ms. The fix is structural: ONE spring → one scalar → every axis in the SAME paint. Any new morph that splits 'chrome on CSS transition' from 'size on JS spring' re-introduces this.

linear() under-sampling clips overshoot. A coarse uniform grid (24 samples) straddles the first peak and silently under-represents bouncy by ~2pp — the token then lies about the curve. Keep SAMPLE_COUNT high enough (48) that the analytic peak is captured, and gate on the parsed token peak. Conversely, excessive stops bloat the CSS string.

Two spring vocabularies drift apart. The legacy `--ease-apple-spring` cubic-bezier (+27.5%) coexisting with the regen `--spring-*` linear() cohort means the dock and the slider inside it can breathe on DIFFERENT curves (the concrete symptom). Excise the bezier; one governed register. Also: a generator can mint a DEAD `--spring-*` preset with no consumer (overfitting) — gate consumer-coverage, fail-closed on zero.

Silent clean-break breakage in external consumers. Deleting `--ease-apple-spring` leaves `var(--ease-apple-spring)` resolving EMPTY in speedtest's 4 sites → transitions degrade to instant/linear with NO error. Any token excision must sweep consumers (library + constellation) and re-point or gate behind the consumer-adoption PR.

The reka-ui forwarding-drop binding-verification class. `@pointerdown`/`@touchstart` on a reka `<SliderRoot>` forwarding component are DROPPED across the Slot/forwardRef boundary — vue-tsc + units PASS, only e2e catches. The keepDockOpen hold has NEVER fired through a real drag for this reason. Native addEventListener on the RESOLVED host element is the fix; sweep this class on every reka version bump.

Animating layout properties (width/padding/height) is GPU-expensive vs transform/opacity. The morph scalar should drive transform/scale where the visual permits and reserve real width/padding interpolation for the FLIP measured path; a 40-button dock @800px = 1861px nowrap row is the live overflow symptom (AX.W04 content-driven flex-wrap, not a viewport @media toggle).

PRM must be a fast-path, not a branch. If reduced-motion is handled per-component instead of via SpringProgress's `respectReducedMotion` snap + the global transition-property strip, you get inconsistent freezes and missed elastic-disable. Honor it once at the engine + the global gate.
interpolate-size/calc-size baseline is Chrome/Edge 129+ ONLY (no Safari/Firefox as of 2025). Treat as progressive enhancement behind @supports; never the sole size-morph driver.

notes.facet: Liquid/squish secondary physics — volume-preserving squash-and-stretch, the elastic overshoot, the settle
sotaTechniques: VOLUME-PRESERVING SQUASH-AND-STRETCH (the canonical mechanism). When an element accelerates/decelerates it stretches along the motion axis and thins on the cross axis so apparent volume is conserved: `scale: var(--squash) calc(1 / var(--stretch))`. The reciprocal pairing is the whole trick — a 1.25x stretch on Y pairs with a 1/1.25=0.8x squash on X. `transform-origin` anchors the deform (Comeau's bouncing ball uses `center bottom` so a squash 'glues to the ground'; a dock pill squashing on press anchors `center`). Three phases: anticipation/impact (bulge wide+short), recovery (stretch tall+thin on rebound), settle (scale 1 1). This is Disney's #1 animation principle expressed in two CSS custom properties.

VELOCITY-DRIVEN SQUASH (the SOTA upgrade Comeau's article stops short of). Instead of hardcoded keyframe ratios, derive the squash ratio LIVE from a spring's instantaneous velocity: `stretch = 1 + clamp(|v| * k, 0, maxStretch)`, `squash = 1/stretch`. glass-ui's `SpringProgress.subscribe((v, vel) => ...)` already emits per-frame velocity (useSpring exposes a readonly `velocity` ref) — it is currently UNUSED for any deform. Feeding `velocity` into a `--squash`/`--stretch` calc gives true secondary physics: fast flicks deform hard, slow drags barely deform, and the deform decays exactly as the spring settles (no separate timer to desync). This is the iOS/Family.co 'the thing reacts to how fast you moved it' register.

OVERSHOOT-AS-FIRST-CLASS via linear() springs (already shipped, under-exploited). glass-ui mints `--spring-{smooth,snappy,bouncy,gentle,dock}` as linear() stop-sets whose values exceed 1.0 (e.g. `--spring-bouncy` peaks 1.205 = +20.5% overshoot; `--spring-dock` peaks 1.045 = +4.6%; `--spring-snappy` +6.8%). The overshoot beyond 1 IS the elastic settle — the curve rings past target and damps back. Generated from the analytic ODE by `scripts/regen-spring-tokens.mjs` so the build-time CSS token and the runtime `SpringProgress` integrator are bit-identical (response/dampingFraction parametric). This is Jake Archibald + Adam Argyle's linear-easing-generator technique productized.

INTERRUPTIBLE VELOCITY-CONTINUITY (the iOS fluid-interface contract). On a re-toggle mid-flight the morph RE-SEATS the live solver's target from its current `(value, velocity)` rather than dispose+restart-from-rest (useLayerTransition AV.W9.2; useSpringMount re-targets mid-drag). Apple's 'Building Fluid Interfaces' names this exactly: interfaces are fluid when responsive, interruptible, redirectable — the element never 'hits a wall and reverses', it carries momentum into the new target. Comeau flags this as the ONE thing pure-CSS linear() springs CANNOT do (a transition interrupt reverses instantly with no inertia) — so the JS SpringProgress path is load-bearing precisely where CSS springs fail.

MOMENTUM/VELOCITY HANDOFF from gesture to spring. Apple's projection formula carries pointer release velocity into the settling spring: relative velocity = `velocity / (target - current)`, projection = `(v0/1000) * decel/(1-decel)`. useSpringMount already pipes pointer-drag delta into the spring target; the missing piece is seeding `initialVelocity` from the release flick so a fast swipe-dismiss overshoots and a slow release eases — the gesture and the settle are ONE continuous motion, not a drag followed by a canned animation.

SINGLE-SCALAR ONE-CLOCK MORPH (glass-ui's AX.W01 headline architecture). Drive the ENTIRE morph from one normalized analytic-spring scalar `--dock-morph-t` (0->1) written once per frame to the root, and express EVERY axis — width, padding, border-radius, scale, color, child-stagger AND squash — as pure `calc()` off that one scalar. Squash-and-stretch becomes free: it is just two more `calc()` reads off the same `--dock-morph-t` (or off the spring's velocity), guaranteeing the deform onsets in the SAME frame as the box (no lead/lag). This is the unification path — secondary physics is not a second animation, it is a derived expression of the primary scalar.

RUBBER-BANDING at boundaries (resistance curve). Past a travel limit, displacement compresses via `offset = pow(offset, 0.7)` (Apple) so a drag-past-end gives diminishing-return resistance rather than a hard stop — the elastic 'pull against a wall' feel. Applies to a dock dragged past its max-inline-size, an over-scrolled rail, or a sheet pulled past full.

NATIVE TOP-LAYER ELASTIC ENTRY (@starting-style + linear() spring, already in animations.css). `.glass-top-layer` uses `@starting-style` + `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` + `overlay` to spring-scale popovers/dialogs from 0.96->1 on `--spring-bouncy` with ZERO JS — the platform owns the entry. interpolate-size/calc-size() extends this to spring-animate to-`auto`/intrinsic sizes (the height-auto morph CSS historically couldn't do). Baseline: @starting-style Widely Available, allow-discrete+overlay Newly Available (gate on `@supports (overlay: auto)`), interpolate-size Chrome-only 2024+ (progressive enhancement).
notes.applicability: "glass-ui is unusually well-positioned: the hard part (an analytic spring engine with live velocity output, the linear() token pipeline, the single-scalar morph) is ALREADY BUILT — the squash/stretch facet is mostly a thin derivation layer on top. CONCRETE WIRING: (1) DOCK MORPH — in the AX.W01 single-scalar rebuild, add two more reads off `--dock-morph-t` or off the spring velocity: `--dock-squash`/`--dock-stretch` written per-frame, consumed as `scale: var(--dock-squash) var(--dock-stretch)` on `.glass-dock` so the pill bulges as it expands and thins as it collapses — secondary physics for free on the existing one-clock scalar, no second animation. (2) PRESS SQUISH — `useSpringPress` already returns a 0..1 spring value AND a velocity ref; today only `value` drives `scale: 1 - value*0.05`. Upgrade to volume-preserving: drive `scale: calc(1 - v*sx) calc(1 - v*sy)` with asymmetric sx/sy so a tapped Button/DockIconButton/preset-chip squishes wide-and-short then springs back — this is exactly AX.W38's 'tap-squish press-spring' ask for the Configurator glass-atoms and the W06 hoisted 'tap-squish' dock-control polish. (3) GLASS MATERIAL — the `.glass-material` group + moving-specular `::before` is the iOS-26 material half; pairing it with a velocity-driven squash on the same surfaces (Switch thumb, glass Button, Dialog) makes the WHOLE band read as one liquid material per the AV.W15 'spring half + material half of one Liquid Glass behaviour' cross-ref. (4) SPRING VOCABULARY — AX.W05 excises the legacy `--ease-apple-spring` bezier (+27.5%) onto the governed `--spring-*` linear() register; the squash facility should consume the SAME `--spring-dock` register so a dock and its in-dock Slider squish on one curve. (5) THE MORPH FACILITY — package the whole thing as a small primitive: `useSquishStretch(velocityRef, {maxStretch, axis})` returning `{squash, stretch}` refs (or a CSS-only `--squash:calc(1/var(--stretch))` recipe), composable onto ANY element that already has a spring — the 'iOS-26 morph for EVERY element' goal becomes: have a spring -> get squash for one calc()."
pitfalls: VOLUME-PRESERVATION IS A RECIPROCAL, NOT TWO INDEPENDENT SCALES. `scale: var(--squash) var(--stretch)` with squash and stretch tuned independently breaks the volume illusion (the element visibly gains/loses area and reads as 'breathing' wrong). The cross axis MUST be `calc(1 / var(--stretch))`. This is the single most common squash-and-stretch bug.

TRANSFORM-ORIGIN COLLISIONS WITH THE STACKING-CONTEXT GUARANTEE. dock.css mints `scale: 1` at rest on `.glass-dock` specifically to create ONE stacking context so a portaled popover stays above the dock during a hover scale. A squash that switches to per-axis `scale: x y` or changes `transform-origin` mid-morph can re-mint/move the stacking context and drop a popover behind the dock. Keep the squash on the SAME `scale` property already establishing the context; never introduce a competing `transform`.

DUAL-DRIVER RACE ON ONE PROPERTY. AV.W9.0 already burned glass-ui: a CSS-native width interpolation ran concurrently with the JS spring writing inline width and FROZE the dock (born-RED). A squash driven by BOTH a CSS `transition: scale` AND per-frame JS `style.scale` writes is the same class of bug. Pick ONE owner — if the morph is single-scalar JS, the squash is a `calc()` off that scalar (CSS reads it, JS owns it); never let a CSS transition also animate scale.

OVER-SQUASH READS AS CHEAP/RUBBERY. iOS Liquid Glass is RESTRAINED — `--spring-dock` is only +4.6% overshoot, press scale only 0.96 (4%). A velocity-driven squash with a high `k` or `maxStretch` turns elegant into Saturday-morning-cartoon. Cap maxStretch low (~1.06-1.10 for chrome, the same register as the overshoot) and clamp. Apple's own iOS 26.2 tweaks were about DIALING DOWN, not up.

PRM (prefers-reduced-motion) MUST STRIP THE DEFORM, NOT JUST THE TRANSLATE. The existing PRM gates strip `transform`/`scale`/`translate` from transition-property and `SpringProgress.respectReducedMotion` snaps to target. A velocity-driven squash computed in JS will still emit non-1 scale values under PRM unless the composable also short-circuits to `{squash:1, stretch:1}` when PRM is set. Volume-deform is vestibular-trigger motion — it MUST flatten under reduce.

LINEAR() SPRINGS CANNOT BE INTERRUPTED WITH INERTIA (Comeau's documented limitation). A pure-CSS `transition: scale var(--spring-bouncy)` that is retargeted mid-flight reverses instantly 'as if it hit a wall' — no momentum. For interruptible squish (the iOS fluid contract, the whole point of secondary physics on a draggable dock), the JS `SpringProgress` velocity-continuity path is REQUIRED; the linear() token is only acceptable for non-interruptible one-shot entries (the @starting-style top-layer case).

BIT-IDENTICAL CONTRACT: a new squash spring must be MINTED FROM THE REGEN PIPELINE, not hand-typed. tokens.css + useLayerTransition + regen-spring-tokens.mjs are kept in lockstep (response 0.32, ζ 0.7) by a comment-sync gate; AX.W05 WIDENS that gate. A hand-typed squash curve or a magic `k` constant in a composable rots against the governed register — derive it, gate it, census it for ≥2 consumers (the overfitting-audit invariant).

CONTAINMENT + WILL-CHANGE COST. A per-axis squash on a large surface that is NOT a standing compositor layer can thrash. The dock already uses on-demand `will-change:<dim>` for the gesture duration only (never standing) — a squash must ride the SAME on-demand hint and clear it on settle, or an idle dock holds VRAM. Squash on `transform` is GPU-cheap; squash that forces layout (animating width/height instead of scale) is not — keep it transform-only.

notes.facet: prefers-reduced-motion + the morph — PRM-safe morphing (collapse the motion to instant, keep the state change), the substrate-owned freeze
sotaTechniques: NUANCED PRM, not binary off (web.dev / Comeau / Chrome VT guide). The canonical 2025 principle: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` does NOT mean 'no motion' — it means remove VESTIBULAR-TRIGGERING motion (large transforms: translate/scale/parallax/spin) while KEEPING non-spatial feedback (opacity cross-fades, color, the state change itself). The state must still change; only the kinetic between-frames are removed. This is exactly what glass-ui/src/styles/utilities.css:1048-1060 already does: under PRM it strips `transition-property` down to `opacity,color,background-color,border-color,box-shadow` and shortens to 0.1s — a snap that keeps the cross-fade, not a dead-stop.

VT API: callback runs SYNCHRONOUSLY so the swap is instant-but-real under PRM (Chrome same-document guide). `document.startViewTransition(cb)` executes `cb` synchronously to mutate the DOM BEFORE any animation; under PRM you set `animation: none !important` on `::view-transition-group/old/new` and the DOM swap STILL lands — the state change is decoupled from the motion by construction. `skipTransition()` is the programmatic equivalent (skip the anim, keep the result). glass-ui/src/styles/view-transition.css:27-33 already implements the `animation:none` PRM bracket on all three pseudos.

Spring `immediate`/snap-to-target (React-Spring `immediate`, Family/animations.dev, keyframes.js `respectReducedMotion`). The clean PRM contract for a physics spring is: pass the PRM boolean as `immediate` (React-Spring) — the spring jumps to its target with no integration phase. glass-ui's `SpringProgress({respectReducedMotion:true})` IS this pattern: useSpring.ts, useSpringMount.ts, and the dock's DOCK_SPRING all set it, so under PRM the spring snaps to target (the morph END-STATE is reached instantly, the box just doesn't travel). Because the visual is linear-equivalent at endpoints, the functional outcome is identical.

SUBSTRATE-OWNED freeze via live `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` `change` listener (web.dev, MDN, Smashing). The continuously-running compositor (WebGL/Canvas2D) cannot be reached by a CSS reset, so the SUBSTRATE itself must own PRM: subscribe to the media-query `change` event, and on `reduce` paint ONE static frame then PARK the rAF loop — live, so toggling the OS setting mid-session freezes immediately. glass-ui already ships this: useCanvas2D.ts and createCanvasLifecycle.ts (the WebGL substrate Aurora+GooBlob compose) own + live-monitor PRM and paint one static frame then park (ORed onto the offscreen/hidden/tab-backgrounded park machinery).

Asymmetric / frequency-aware motion (Rauno Freiberg interfaces.rauno.me, Emil Kowalski, macOS precedent). SOTA motion is not symmetric: 'frequent, low-novelty' actions (a dock you open dozens of times, a context menu) should under-animate or even animate-out-but-not-in (the macOS right-click menu precedent). For a dock, this argues the COLLAPSE (frequent dismiss) is the crisp/snappy register and the EXPAND (the reveal) carries the overshoot — which glass-ui's view-transition.css:76-86 already encodes via typed VT directions (dock-expand → overshooting --spring-dock; dock-collapse → non-overshooting --spring-snappy + --duration-fast). Under PRM both collapse to instant.

Apple Liquid Glass: gate the kinetic morph on `accessibilityReduceMotion`, NOT the material (WWDC25 'Meet Liquid Glass', SwiftUI HIG). iOS-26 obligation: the GLASS LOOK (blur/refraction/specular) survives under Reduce Motion, but the ELASTIC/morph between glass elements (`GlassEffectContainer` blend-and-morph) is gated off — 'every glass animation should be gated on accessibilityReduceMotion because the morphing effect is a kinetic effect, not just a fade.' Reduce Transparency is a SEPARATE axis (adds opacity to the material) from Reduce Motion (kills the elastic). The library mirror: PRM freezes the morph + the moving specular (glass-specular-track.css:34) but the static glass tier/blur stays.

`@starting-style` + `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` + `overlay` for native top-layer entry that degrades to instant (MDN, Chrome). The platform-native enter/exit grammar (glass-ui animations.css:325+ `.glass-top-layer`, `@supports (overlay:auto)`-gated) gives a CSS-only reveal whose discrete steps (display/overlay) are PRM-safe: under PRM the `transition` brackets zero out and the element simply appears in the top layer — instant, state-complete, no kinetic.

`interpolate-size: allow-keywords` / `calc-size(auto)` for size morphs to intrinsic — but it is NOT the dock's path (MDN, Frontend Masters). It lets `height`/`width` animate to `auto`/`max-content` in pure CSS (set once on `:root`, inherited). Status: experimental, NOT Baseline (Chrome 129 only) and it FOUGHT the dock's spring driver — glass-ui RETIRED its `interpolate-size`/`calc-size` arm (AV.W9.0, dock.css:584-599) because it dual-drove width against `SpringProgress` and froze the dock. Lesson for the morph facility: ONE driver per property; intrinsic-size CSS interpolation is a fallback-only tool, never co-resident with a JS spring on the same axis.
notes.applicability: ["DOCK (W01/W02/W05): glass-ui's dock is ALREADY at SOTA on PRM and is the reference implementation. useLayerTransition.ts has an explicit PRM fast-path (lines 296-305) that does a single SYNCHRONOUS state swap — no measure/pin/rAF/spring — the textbook 'keep the state change, kill the motion'. The W01 single-scalar rewrite must PRESERVE this: when the morph collapses to one `--dock-morph-t` scalar driven by one SpringProgress, the PRM contract is `respectReducedMotion:true` on that one spring (snap to target) PLUS the synchronous-swap guard so the layer ref flips without the rAF deferral. The global utilities.css:1050 gate already strips width/transform from the transition-property under PRM, so the box reaches its end size instantly and only opacity cross-fades. ACTION for the morph facility: make PRM a first-class input to the single morph orchestrator (W01/W02) — one `prm` ref read once, branching to the synchronous-swap path — so there is ONE PRM gate per dock, not the current belt-and-suspenders double-gate (JS fast-path + spring's own respectReducedMotion + CSS strip). The W02 stagger (`--dock-morph-progress`-keyed child onset) is correctly already PRM-suppressed (it only arms while `data-revealing` is set, which the synchronous swap never sets — useLayerTransition.ts:222-228).", "UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY (the 'every element morphs' goal): the path forward is a single `useMorph` primitive that takes a PRM-aware contract by construction — (a) it drives ONE scalar/spring with `respectReducedMotion`, (b) it exposes a synchronous-swap fast-path for the state change, (c) it routes color/inherited-property changes through DISCRETE class swaps (never per-frame tween — the inheritance-bomb guard already documented at useLayerTransition.ts:94-99) which are PRM-safe for free. Every primitive (dock, dialog via useSpringMount, drawer, expandable-container, the VT list-item swap) then inherits the SAME PRM semantics: instant-but-real. This unifies the three PRM gates that exist today (CSS utilities.css strip, JS spring respectReducedMotion, JS synchronous-swap) into ONE owned contract — currently each surface re-implements its own.", "GLASS PRIMITIVES (W09/W20): the SOTA split (material survives, kinetic dies) is the design rule. The moving specular catch-light (glass-specular-track.css) correctly freezes under PRM (line 34) — keep that. The W09 specular tune-to-subtle should ensure the REST specular (now ~0) means a PRM user sees a clean static plate (no centered catch-light), matching Apple's 'glass look without the elastic'. The `.glass-top-layer` `@starting-style` grammar (W20) is already PRM-safe by construction (the transition brackets zero out → instant top-layer appearance). The W20 native-dialog scrim fix (color-mix dimming) is orthogonal to PRM — the dim is a static state, not motion — so it paints identically under PRM.", "ANIMATION LANGUAGE (W05): the one-iOS-spring vocabulary should make `respectReducedMotion` the DEFAULT on every `--spring-*`-consuming JS driver and ensure every CSS spring rides a transition-property the utilities.css PRM strip can reach (transform/width/height → stripped; opacity/color → kept). The asymmetric typed-VT directions (dock-expand overshoot vs dock-collapse snappy) are the frequency-aware-motion SOTA (Rauno) and should be retained as the non-PRM register; under PRM both directions collapse via the view-transition.css:27 `animation:none` bracket. The W05 govern-the-vocabulary doc should add a 'PRM register' row: every named spring has a defined PRM degrade (snap-to-target).", "SUBSTRATE FREEZE (Aurora/GooBlob, W07/W08/W15/W16): the live-monitored matchMedia freeze in createCanvasLifecycle.ts / useCanvas2D.ts is exactly the SOTA substrate-owned-freeze and must be preserved through the WebGPU re-platforming (W14) — a CSS reset cannot reach the WebGPU rAF, so the GPU substrate must own its own PRM `change` listener and paint one static frame then park. The DockBackgroundToggle (WCAG 2.2.2 pause/play) is the COMPLEMENT, not a substitute: PRM auto-freezes; the toggle is the manual stop for non-PRM users (correctly NOT gated behind PRM). Keep both seams distinct."]
pitfalls: DUAL-DRIVER RACE on the same property is the cardinal hazard and glass-ui already got bitten: the retired `interpolate-size`/`calc-size` arm (AV.W9.0) second-drove `.dock-layers` width on the browser's clock WHILE SpringProgress wrote inline width per frame → the morph cancelled and FROZE the dock (born-RED under proof:dock-animation-live). RULE: exactly ONE driver per animated property, on every engine. The morph facility must enforce this structurally — never co-resident CSS intrinsic-size interpolation + a JS spring on the same axis.

`animation-duration: 0.01ms` (the common PRM idiom) STILL FIRES `animationend` — needed if your JS lifecycle keys cleanup off the event, but a pitfall if you assume 'PRM = no events'. glass-ui's utilities.css:1051 uses `0.01ms !important` precisely so animationend still fires; the morph facility's settle/cleanup must not assume the rAF/transitionend path is the only completion signal under PRM.

Stripping ALL transitions under PRM (the naive `* { transition: none }`) destroys the safe opacity/color cross-fade and makes the UI feel BROKEN, not accessible — the whole point of nuanced PRM. glass-ui correctly keeps opacity/color/box-shadow (utilities.css:1058). Do NOT regress to a blanket kill in the morph rewrite.

Inherited-custom-property tweening per frame under any motion mode forces a whole-subtree style recalc (the 'inheritance bomb' — useLayerTransition.ts:94-99). Under PRM this is doubly wrong (it's motion the user opted out of) AND a perf hazard. The morph facility must route color/phase changes through DISCRETE class swaps, never frame-by-frame interpolation of `--phase-color`/`--shadow-color`.

A standing `will-change` holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an idle surface (useLayerTransition.ts:178-193 F3). Under PRM there is NO morph, so `will-change` must NEVER be set on the PRM synchronous-swap path — only promote for the duration of an actual gesture. A morph facility that sets `will-change` unconditionally leaks layers on every PRM user's idle dock.

Forgetting the LIVE listener: reading `matchMedia(...).matches` ONCE at construction means a user toggling Reduce Motion mid-session keeps the old behavior. The substrate (and ideally the morph orchestrator) must subscribe to the `change` event. glass-ui's canvas substrate does this; a hand-rolled morph that only reads `.matches` once is a latent bug.

VT name COLLISIONS skip the transition SILENTLY (≤1 element per `view-transition-name` per state). Under PRM the swap still lands so the bug is invisible in PRM testing but breaks non-PRM (the fourier two-dock `glass-dock-1` duplicate-name dropped-snapshot class, W01/W02). Test BOTH PRM and non-PRM; a PRM-only test pass hides VT-name collisions.

Apple's split is easy to get backwards: under Reduce Motion you keep the MATERIAL (blur/glass) and kill the KINETIC (morph/elastic); under Reduce Transparency you do the OPPOSITE (add opacity to the material, motion may stay). Conflating the two axes (e.g. removing the blur under Reduce Motion, or freezing motion under Reduce Transparency) is a common Liquid-Glass adoption error flagged in the WWDC25 guidance.

notes.facet: Liquid-glass MATERIAL on the web — backdrop-filter stacks, SVG feDisplacementMap lensing, the @supports-gated SOTA glass, and the unified iOS-26 morph facility for dock + animation + glass primitives
sotaTechniques: SVG feDisplacementMap LENSING (the kube.io/LogRocket recipe) — the canonical 3-primitive graph: feImage (a pre-baked RGB displacement map where R=x-shift, G=y-shift, neutral 128=no shift, computed from a convex-squircle surface profile y=⁴√(1−(1−x)⁴) via Snell's law n₁=1 air → n₂=1.5 glass) → feDisplacementMap (xChannelSelector='R' yChannelSelector='G', scale=max-px) → feImage specular + feBlend screen. Apple's 'lensing' (bend+concentrate light) vs glassmorphism's 'blur' (scatter light) is THE defining iOS-26 distinction. glass-ui ALREADY ships this as the `#glass-refract` data-URI filter in glass-refract.css — it is at the frontier here.

backdrop-filter: url(#filter) @supports-GATING — `backdrop-filter` accepting an SVG filter url() is Chromium-only (WebKit bug 245510 open, Firefox not shipping), and is NOT in the CSS spec, so the displacement decl MUST sit behind `@supports (backdrop-filter: url('#…'))` with the plain blur as the un-gated fallback. This is exactly glass-ui's pattern. The displacement lookup itself is a single-pixel-offset op — cheaper than blur — but rebuilding the map on resize is expensive; only the `scale` attr animates cheaply.

The unified pointer-tracked SPECULAR catch-light — a masked radial-gradient `::before` riding the surface at the pointer position via typed `@property` channels (`--specular-x/y` mapped from the consumer's `--mouse-x/--mouse-y` write), with `mix-blend-mode: screen` and intensity lifting on hover/active in lockstep with the press-squish. This is Apple's 'illuminate-from-within / touch-point illumination' behaviour. glass-ui ships it in `.glass-material::before`; AX.W09 is the tune-to-subtle (warm-cream low-alpha, tokenized `--glass-specular-intensity-{rest,hover,active}`, lift into a `useSpecularTracking()` composable).

GlassEffectContainer + matchedGeometryEffect + glassEffectID (Apple SwiftUI) — the MORPH facility's conceptual core: multiple glass elements in a shared sampling region MERGE and morph fluidly when within a `spacing` threshold (glass cannot sample other glass — the container provides the shared region), and `glassEffectID` + `matchedGeometryEffect` smoothly morph an element between hidden/visible/relocated states with `withAnimation(.bouncy(0.35–0.4))`. The web analog = ONE shared morph orchestrator + View-Transitions `view-transition-name` for the cross-element geometry morph. This is the direct blueprint for AX.W01/W02 (one morph orchestrator per dock).

Single-scalar / single-clock spring morph — drive EVERY animated axis (inline-size, padding, border-radius, scale, color, child stagger) as pure `calc()`/interpolation off ONE normalized analytic-spring scalar (0→1) written once per frame to a CSS custom property, with NO competing CSS `transition` on the root. iOS feel = a damped 2nd-order harmonic oscillator with (response, dampingFraction) — interruptible (velocity-continuity: a re-target re-seats from current (value,velocity), never dispose+reconstruct-from-rest). glass-ui's `useSpring`/`SpringProgress` (response 0.32, ζ 0.7 for `--spring-dock`) is this; AX.W01 collapses the dock onto the single scalar and RETIRES the View-Transitions fork for the COLLAPSE morph.

Native size-keyword animation: interpolate-size: allow-keywords + calc-size() — lets `width/height: auto`/`min-content`/`fit-content` ANIMATE natively (Chrome/Edge 129+, Sept 2024; not yet Safari/Firefox). Replaces the JS FLIP measure-pin-rAF dance for content-driven reflow. CAVEAT for glass-ui: AV.W9.0 deliberately RETIRED the interpolate-size width arm because it second-drove width against the SpringProgress FLIP and froze the dock — so this is a 'know it but one-driver-per-concern' technique, useful for the wrap/overflow reflow (AX.W04) NOT the primary dock morph.

@starting-style + transition-behavior: allow-discrete + overlay — Baseline-Newly (Firefox 129) pure-CSS entry/exit for native top-layer surfaces (`[popover]`, `<dialog>`, `::backdrop`), animating from display:none with no JS coordinator. glass-ui ships this in animations.css `.glass-top-layer` gated on `@supports (overlay: auto)`. The morph facility uses it for the glass dialog/popover bloom-in (scale 0.96→1 on `--spring-bouncy`).

Same-document View Transitions + view-transition-class + active-view-transition-type — the browser snapshots and cross-fades/morphs tagged elements (`view-transition-name`) across a DOM mutation with zero getBoundingClientRect. Correct primitive for ROUTE/page geometry morphs and list-item reorders (glass-ui's `useViewTransition` + `.gl-list-item` recipe), and for DIRECTIONAL asymmetry (snappier exit, softer entry-overshoot via `:active-view-transition-type()`). KEY nuance the AX charter nails: VT is the WRONG primitive for a same-element layout morph (it crossfades rasterized pixels → desync), but RIGHT for the consumer route-morph — these are separable and W01 keeps the named-element seam while retiring the collapse fork.

Anchor positioning (anchor() / position-area / @position-try) — Baseline-2025 native tethering of popovers/menus/tooltips to an anchor with no JS measurement, with fallback positioning. The morph facility uses it so a dock-launched popover/tray visually emanates from the control it morphs out of (the Family.co 'button morphs into tray' pattern) — replaces JS positioning libraries.

corner-shape: squircle (Chrome 139+) — the literal iOS-26 superellipse corner geometry that backdrop-filter, borders, and shadows all follow, `@supports`-gated over plain `border-radius` round. glass-ui already ships this on `.glass-card/.glass-btn/.btn-pill`. It is the correct silhouette for the lens profile (the displacement map is computed off the same squircle curve).

Content-aware adaptive material: under-shadow + tint + edge-rim — Apple raises the under-shadow OVER text (glass reads as lifting off content) and drops it over solid light; tints the surface toward sampled backdrop hue; and carries a full-perimeter `--glass-edge-light` rim that 'defines the silhouette' (WWDC25 sess. 219). glass-ui ships all three: `[data-over-content=text|solid]` under-shadow swap, `color-mix(in oklab, …, --glass-tint-source --glass-tint-strength)` adaptive tint, and the unified `--glass-material-rim`. Chromatic edge dispersion (`.glass-chromatic`, prefers-reduced-transparency-gated) is the polished-glass fringe garnish.

Press-squish + interactive illumination on controls — Apple's `.glassEffect(.interactive())`: scale-on-press, bounce, shimmer, and touch-point illumination radiating to NEARBY glass. glass-ui's `--scale-press-dock`/`--scale-press-btn` squish on `--spring-snappy` is the SPRING half; the specular `::before` intensity-lift is the MATERIAL half — the unification (one momentum-gated press writing BOTH scale and specular intensity) is the morph-facility convergence point.
notes.applicability: "glass-ui is already AT or NEAR the frontier on the MATERIAL axis — the gap is COHERENCE and the MORPH FACILITY, not missing primitives. (1) DOCK (AX.W01–W06): the path forward is the single-scalar/single-clock spring morph. Today the dock has THREE+ overlapping morph authorities (root padding/radius on synchronous CSS-class transitions, inner width on a JS SpringProgress FLIP deferred a frame behind, plus a View-Transitions fork) so the box leads content by ~16ms. The SOTA blueprint = Apple's GlassEffectContainer (one shared morph orchestrator per dock) + the single normalized spring scalar `--dock-morph-t` → every axis via calc() → retire the VT collapse-fork while preserving the `view-transition-name` route-morph seam (fourier consumes it). Model the dock as ONE stack whose layer = (expandedState × activePane) so collapse and pane-swap settle on ONE timeline (W02). (2) ANIMATION language: glass-ui already has the right substrate — `useSpring`/`SpringProgress` (interruptible 2nd-order ODE, velocity-continuity), `useViewTransition` + directional types, `@starting-style`/`allow-discrete` top-layer grammar, scroll-driven + anchor positioning. The unification move is to make the iOS-spring vocabulary ONE register (AX.W05 excises the legacy apple-spring bezier and re-points its 5 consumers onto `--spring-dock`), so collapsed→hover→expand reads as one continuous spring rather than an ease handed to a width-spring. Anchor positioning + View Transitions are the missing connective tissue for the 'control morphs into tray/popover' Family.co behaviour. (3) GLASS primitives: the `.glass-material` mixin is the canonical CSS-native substrate; AX.W20 RETIRES the JS GlassPanel/createGlassFilter/useGlassRenderer SVG-displacement path (it stomps the per-rung CSS with hardcoded non-dark-adaptive white) onto exactly this grammar. The `#glass-refract` feDisplacementMap lens is already shipped @supports-gated — the move is to make lensing a tokenized opt-in garnish (`--glass-refract-scale` animatable, the only cheap axis) layered over the universal blur base, NEVER promoted to the always-on substrate (resize-expensive). (4) THE UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY (the iOS-26 'every element' goal): compose four already-present layers into ONE contract — MATERIAL (`.glass-material`: blur+tint+rim+under-shadow + @supports lens + pointer-specular), MORPH (one shared spring orchestrator writing a single scalar; View Transitions for cross-element geometry; anchor positioning for emanation), PRESS (momentum-gated squish driving scale AND specular-intensity in lockstep), and ACCESSIBILITY (the four prefers-* guards). Expose the rebuilt single-scalar `useLayerTransition` on the `/dock` barrel so value.js deletes its FLIP-width fork (substrate-with-consumer). The research-backed README states: lensing-not-blur is the iOS-26 thesis; glass lives ONLY in the navigation/overlay bands (no glass-on-glass — glass-ui already enforces this); one spring, one clock, one scalar; interruptible physics; and every axis a token."
pitfalls: backdrop-filter: url(#svg-filter) is Chromium-ONLY and NOT in the CSS spec (WebKit bug 245510 open, Firefox not shipping) — the lens MUST stay @supports-gated with a plain-blur fallback, and it must NEVER be the substrate (only a PE-over-blur garnish). A leak onto the un-gated base breaks the round/blur fallback on partial-support engines.

feDisplacementMap map REBUILD is resize-expensive — nearly every geometric/size tweak forces a full displacement-map recompute. ONLY the `scale` attr animates cheaply. So a morphing dock cannot animate the lens geometry per-frame; animate `scale` or freeze the lens during the morph and re-enable at rest.

Competing morph authorities = the cardinal dock bug — synchronous CSS-class transitions on the root racing a JS spring on the inner box (deferred via nextTick→rAF→reflow) makes the box lead content by ~16ms; TWO `useLayerTransition` instances per dock double-animate the same pixels. ONE driver per concern (size=spring, opacity=fade) is mandatory.

View Transitions is the WRONG primitive for a same-element LAYOUT morph — it crossfades rasterized pixels (the uncaptured-animating-ancestor desync) and DROPS the snapshot on a duplicate `view-transition-name` (fourier's two-co-mounted-docks both minting `glass-dock-1` reds ~13 e2e). VT is right for ROUTE/list-reorder morphs, not the dock's own collapse.

interpolate-size/calc-size width-animation SECOND-DROVE the dock width against the SpringProgress FLIP on Chrome 129+ and FROZE the dock at runtime (AV.W9.0 retired it). Know the feature, but never let it co-drive a dimension a JS spring owns. Also not yet in Safari/Firefox.

backdrop-filter creates a new STACKING CONTEXT (a rendering boundary) — a positioned child outside the parent's box can't reach outside to blur the real background; and the blur samples only within its own context. This breaks naive glass-over-portaled-content.

backdrop-filter blur is GPU-expensive and battery-draining — keep blur 8–15px (cost rises super-linearly above), limit to KEY navigation/overlay surfaces, never stack blurred layers (glass-on-glass), and never run perpetual motion. Apple measures ~13% vs 1% battery for continuous glass animation; let glass rest in steady states.

Nested hsl() — `hsl(var(--background) / α)` where the token is already a complete hsl() color is the CLAUDE.md anti-pattern that NEVER paints (the broken native-<dialog> backdrop, AX.W20). Use `color-mix(in srgb, var(--token) N%, transparent)`. Canvas2D also silently rejects light-dark() into fill/strokeStyle (the constellation defect) — use plain-hsl tokens.

Permanent will-change holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an idle surface — set will-change:<dim> ONLY for the gesture duration, clear to auto on settle (glass-ui's AV.W7 F3 pattern). A standing hint on an idle dock is a memory leak.

Accessibility is non-optional and must be REAL, not decorative — `prefers-reduced-transparency` (drop blur+specular, go opaque), `prefers-reduced-motion` (pin specular static, snap the spring), `prefers-contrast` (raise opacity), forced-colors. Apple does these automatically; on the web they are four explicit media guards. The pointer-specular and lens are transparency garnishes that MUST drop under reduce.

The pointer-specular registered-@property var nested in an hsl() alpha computes to 0 in Chromium — drive the layer `opacity` from the intensity multiplier, not a per-stop alpha (glass-ui learned this the hard way in glass.css).

Spring-token drift — the build-time CSS `--spring-dock` token and the runtime SpringProgress driver sample the SAME analytic ODE; a retune MUST touch BOTH the const (response 0.32, ζ 0.7) and the regen-spring-tokens PRESETS row or the CSS-token and JS curves diverge. Hardcoded magnitudes in proof scripts (0.6/0.85 specular) must co-update or the tune lands RED.

notes.facet: Refraction / convex-lens shaders — edge-bend, chromatic dispersion, the WebGL/CSS approaches to real glass refraction (iOS-26 Liquid-Glass lensing)
sotaTechniques: SVG feImage + feDisplacementMap convex-lens (the canonical web refraction).
