A pre-baked displacement map (R=x-shift, G=y-shift, neutral 128=no shift) drives feDisplacementMap with scale=max-px, xChannelSelector=R/yChannelSelector=G; the map encodes a convex SURFACE PROFILE refracted via Snell (n1=1 air, n2=1.5 glass), so the backdrop bends INWARD at the edges like a lens. This is EXACTLY glass-ui's shipped src/styles/glass-refract.css #glass-refract filter. State-of-art mechanism, already in-repo.

Apple's preferred corner curve y=∜√(1 − (1−x)⁴) (the convex SQUIRCLE profile). The displacement magnitude per pixel = numeric-derivative normal of this surface profile run through Snell, normalized so max-displacement=1, then encoded r=128+x*127 / g=128+y*127. A softer edge-bend than a circular arc; glass-ui's filter comment already cites this exact equation — the squircle is the load-bearing shape primitive.

Three-pass RGB chromatic dispersion (the prismatic edge fringe glass-ui LACKS). Run feDisplacementMap THREE times at slightly different scale per channel (e.g. R=scale, G=scale+10, B=scale+20, or opposed offsets), isolate each channel with feColorMatrix (zero the others), recombine with feBlend mode=screen. Shorter wavelengths bend more → rainbow fringe only at high-curvature edges. This is the single biggest fidelity gap vs iOS-26 lensing in glass-ui's current single-pass filter.

Canvas-2D-generated displacement map over inline-SVG-feImage (the rizroze fix for the data-URI limitation). SVG-data-URI feImage RESTRICTS CSS property evaluation in the feDisplacementMap graph (kube.io / rizroze); generating the map on an OffscreenCanvas with globalCompositeOperation:'difference' + ctx.filter:'blur()' and feeding it as a blob/ObjectURL sidesteps that, and lets the map RE-BAKE per size without re-authoring SVG. Also auto-extends the filter region beyond the default 10% so displacement up to ~90px doesn't clip.

feSpecularLighting / dual-feImage specular rim (the polished-glass catch). A stroke-only top-left-bright rim map (or feSpecularLighting keyed to the surface normal vs a fixed light direction) blurred via feGaussianBlur, masked by feComposite operator=in, blended feBlend over the displaced backdrop. glass-ui ships a soft feImage specular in glass-refract.css AND a separate pointer-tracked CSS moving-specular ::before (glass.css) — two specular systems that AX.W09 is consolidating.

WebGL true-backdrop refraction with screen-space sampling (the Chromium-only escape hatch). Capture the DOM/page as a texture (framebuffer / element-capture), then in the fragment shader refract() the view ray per-channel using wavelength-dependent IOR (Cauchy: ior=A+B/λ²), sample uBackground at three offset UVs (uvR/uvG/uvB) for chromatic split, and mix with Schlick Fresnel (more reflective at glancing angles). The ONLY approach that works cross-browser (Safari/Firefox don't support backdrop-filter:url()) AND can bend content beyond the element's own bounds (which CSS backdrop-filter fundamentally cannot).

Schlick-Fresnel rim + wavelength-IOR dispersion in a single parallel pass (no loop). nR/nG/nB from the Cauchy equation, three refract() directions, three texture taps, F=fresnelSchlick(cosθ,F0)*boost, color=mix(refracted,reflected,F). glass-ui's blob already does a Fresnel rim on a curved normal (AX.W08/W15) — the same math generalizes to a glass-panel refraction substrate.

iOS-26 GlassEffectContainer merge-morph (the SHARED-sampling-region morph model). Multiple .glassEffect() shapes inside one container with a `spacing` threshold MERGE into one continuous glass blob when close, and morph between states via glassEffectID() + a shared Namespace. The rule 'glass cannot sample other glass — the container provides the shared sampling region' is the architectural key: ONE displacement/refraction pass over a group, not N independent filters. This is the morph-facility north star for glass-ui's dock layers + adjacent controls.

Lensing-not-blur + specular-from-motion (the Apple material identity). Liquid Glass DEFINES itself by lensing (concentrating/bending light in real time) rather than scattering (blur); specular highlights respond to device motion; elements MATERIALIZE by modulating light-bending rather than fade-in; shadows/tint adapt to backdrop. The web translation: the refraction displacement (not just blur+saturate) is the load-bearing material, and the press/morph spring must drive the refraction `scale`, not a separate opacity tween.

interactive() touch-illumination that radiates to nearby glass. On press: scale-squish + bounce + a shimmer + a touch-point catch-light that spreads to adjacent glass in the same container. glass-ui's pointer-tracked --specular-x/--specular-y ::before is the web analog; the SOTA extension is propagating that illumination across grouped surfaces (dock controls) from one pointer write.
notes.applicability: glass-ui already ships the canonical SVG convex-lens refraction (src/styles/glass-refract.css) baked from the Apple squircle profile and correctly @supports-gated to Chromium with a blur fallback. It is ahead of most web implementations on the lens itself. The concrete facet-application path: (1) add an opt-in three-pass RGB chromatic-dispersion variant tokened as --glass-refract-dispersion (default 0/off) for the prismatic edge fringe it currently lacks; (2) collapse the two competing specular systems (the baked feImage specular vs the pointer-tracked CSS ::before) onto one owner per AX.W09 so refraction carries the lens-bend and the ::before owns the motion-responsive catch-light; (3) drive the refraction filter `scale` off the AX.W01 single-scalar dock morph (--dock-morph-t) and the press spring so glass visibly lenses/thickens through the morph, governed by the AX.W05 one-spring vocabulary; (4) model the unified morph facility on iOS-26 GlassEffectContainer (one shared refraction/specular pass over a dock control group with a pointer write that propagates to siblings), which also matches glass-ui's existing no-glass-on-glass discipline; (5) keep WebGL true-backdrop refraction (which glass-ui's useWebGLCanvas/blob-Fresnel substrate already proves) as a gated premium escape hatch for cross-browser/overflow cases, never the default, and never a style-stomping imperative filter (the exact path AX.W20 is retiring).
pitfalls: backdrop-filter:url(#svg-filter) is CHROMIUM-ONLY and will stay so for the foreseeable future. WebKit bug 245510 is open (not shipping), Firefox explicitly is not implementing SVG-filters-in-backdrop-filter (Mozilla Connect idea still open). Safari 18 unprefixed backdrop-filter supports blur() but NOT url() SVG filters. So the entire CSS refraction effect degrades to plain blur on ~40% of traffic — glass-ui's @supports gate handles this correctly today; never assume the lens paints everywhere.

Displacement-map REBUILD is the perf cliff, not the displacement itself. Per kube.io/LogRocket: animating filter props like `scale` is cheap (single-pixel-lookup, cheaper than blur), but ANY shape/size change forces a full displacement-map rebuild — expensive. Rule: bake the squircle map once, animate ONLY `scale`; never regenerate the map per frame or per resize-tick. glass-ui's comment already warns the filter is 'resize-expensive — only the scale attr animates without rebuilding the map' — keep that discipline.

Three-pass chromatic dispersion TRIPLES the filter cost (3 feDisplacementMap + 3 feColorMatrix + recombine). Real-time backdrop displacement is already heavy GPU rasterization; chromatic aberration multiplies it. Must be opt-in (default --glass-refract-dispersion:0), restricted to small regions (the Apple/LogRocket guidance: toolbars, modals, primary CTAs only), and contain:strict + will-change:transform to isolate the layer. Do NOT promote it to the card/primitive substrate broadly.

SVG-data-URI feImage restricts CSS property evaluation inside the displacement graph (kube.io, rizroze both hit this). glass-ui's static map is fine, but any attempt to make displacement geometry token-driven via CSS vars in the inline SVG will silently fail. The fix is Canvas-2D map generation (blob URL), which is more code and more lifecycle — weigh it before promising adaptive displacement.

Two competing specular systems = the white-blowout AX.W09 is fixing. The feImage specular in #glass-refract STACKS on the pointer-tracked CSS ::before moving-specular AND (on dock controls) a third --glass-highlight hover box-shadow. iOS-26 has ONE specular owner per surface. Adding more lens/highlight fidelity without first collapsing to one owner re-creates the ~0.47 pure-white screen-blend hotspot. Refraction work must compose with W09's single-owner + warm-cream-low-alpha tune, not bolt a fourth light on.

WebGL backdrop refraction has DOM→WebGL synchronization overhead that causes frame drops with multiple panels, and degrades to a static overlay on GPU-less/old devices. It also requires capturing the page to a texture (framebuffer/element-capture) which is fragile (cross-origin, dynamic content, scroll). It is NOT a free upgrade over CSS — reserve for hero surfaces; do not make it the dock default.

Do NOT resurrect a style-STOMPING imperative filter. AX.W20 is RETIRING the JS createGlassFilter/useGlassRenderer path precisely because it hard-overwrote el.style.backdropFilter/border/boxShadow with hardcoded non-dark-adaptive white, collapsing the five CSS rungs to one look and async-loading the dataURL (blank first paint). Any new refraction must be CSS-cascade-additive over .glass-material (dark-adaptive, @supports-gated, fallback-bearing), never an imperative inline-style write.

The nested-hsl trap (AX.W20 witness 1): color tokens are already complete hsl() colors — hsl(var(--token)/α) silently DROPS at parse and never paints. Any specular/rim color in a new filter or chroma pass must use color-mix(in srgb, var(--token) N%, transparent), never nest a token in hsl() alpha. This is a repo-wide anti-pattern with an active gate (proof:no-nested-hsl).

Chromatic fringe must zero out under prefers-reduced-transparency, forced-colors, and (for motion-coupled dispersion) prefers-reduced-motion. A rainbow edge on a forced-colors/high-contrast surface is an a11y regression. AX.W36 owns the forced-colors glass skin; coordinate the dispersion bracket there.

Don't over-promise iOS parity. The web cannot bend content BEYOND an element's bounds with backdrop-filter (it only affects content within the element — ekino-france), and cannot do glass-sampling-glass merge natively. GlassEffectContainer merge-morph requires either a shared single-filter pass (CSS, limited) or WebGL. Frame the morph facility as 'one shared refraction pass over a group + spring-driven scale', not a literal SwiftUI GlassEffectContainer reimplementation.

notes.facet: Specular / moving highlight — the pointer-anchored catch-light (tuned SUBTLE per W09), plus the rest/hover/active intensity floor and the silhouette rim
sotaTechniques: SDF-gradient normal-map specular (Apple/Linear canon) — represent the rounded-rect/squircle shape as a signed distance field, take the SDF gradient as a per-pixel surface normal, and dot it against a moving point-light to get a specular term that brightens along bezel curvature where the normal turns; this is how iOS-26 + Linear compute 'how much light each point catches' on the GPU. Web translation: glass-ui can't run a fragment shader on a backdrop cheaply, so it approximates the same physics with a masked radial-gradient anchored at the pointer (the catch-light = the light's screen-space position) plus a static bezel rim (the SDF-curvature term baked as an inset ring). The pointer-radial IS the moving light; the rim IS the curvature highlight.

Plus-Lighter / screen additive compositing (Linear's blend choice) — the highlight layer is composited additively over the blurred backdrop so it only ever ADDS light (never darkens), matching how a real catch-light works; Linear uses 'Plus Lighter', the web equivalent is mix-blend-mode: screen (already what glass.css uses on the ::before). Screen is the correct primitive: it saturates toward white asymptotically, so a low-alpha warm core reads as a soft sheen rather than a hard white disc.

@property typed-percentage pointer interpolation (web-platform 2025 baseline) — registering --specular-x/--specular-y as syntax:'<percentage>' (and --specular-intensity as '<number>') lets the engine INTERPOLATE the gradient-center position between discrete pointer samples; a bare unregistered var() snaps frame-to-frame. glass-ui already does this (tokens.css §18) — it's the canonical mechanism for a smooth travelling catch-light driven by sparse pointermove events. @property is Baseline 2024-07-09 (Chrome 85+, Safari 16.4+, Firefox 128+).

Pointer-anchored radial-gradient catch-light driven by a JS pointermove → CSS-var write (Family.co / Rauno / practitioner spotlight pattern) — JS reads getBoundingClientRect + clientX/Y, writes --mouse-x/--mouse-y as box-percentages onto the host (style-only, no reflow, no re-render), CSS paints radial-gradient(circle at var(--specular-x) var(--specular-y), ...). glass-ui has this verbatim in DockIconButton.vue + Card.vue — W09 wants it lifted into a shared useSpecularTracking() composable. The write must be cheap: percentages of the element box, .toFixed(2), inert until hover.

Three-rung tokenized intensity ladder with a ~0 rest floor (the W09 'tune-to-subtle' shape) — rest≈0/0.08, hover≈0.22, active≈0.32, each a named token (--glass-specular-intensity-{rest,hover,active} + dark arm) rather than a buried literal. The rest floor at ~0 means a static, un-hovered, un-wired surface is genuinely CLEAN (no dead-centered bloom) — the highlight only blooms on interaction, which is exactly the iOS behaviour ('illuminate under your fingertip'). Apple HIG amplitude cap: specular highlight amplitude ≤ 6px, applied with restraint, navigation/key-element only — not everywhere.

Warm-cream low-alpha core, not pure-white (color-identity discipline) — the inner gradient stop should be a genuinely warm low-alpha cream, not hsl(40 30% 100%) which resolves to pure white; the screen blend already lifts it toward white on contact, so the authored color must START warm-and-dim or it blows out. Keeps glass-ui's warm-cream identity instead of the iOS cold-blue catch-light.

Full-perimeter silhouette rim as the 'defines-the-silhouette' edge light (WWDC25 session 219) — distinct from the moving catch-light: a uniform low-alpha inset ring (--glass-edge-light → --glass-material-rim) on every material rung that reads as the glass thickness catching ambient light around its whole edge. This is the static counterpart to the moving highlight; together they are the two halves of the Liquid-Glass material (moving point-light + curvature rim).

Device-tilt / ambient light parallax (iOS-26 native; web-degradable) — native Liquid Glass moves the highlight from DeviceMotion (gyroscope tilt) so it shifts when you physically move the phone. Web analogue: DeviceOrientation events (mobile) or a slow ambient drift can drive --specular-x/y when no pointer is present, giving the 'alive at rest' quality. Strictly optional/progressive — must respect reduced-motion and battery, and is non-essential motion (WCAG 2.2.2 territory if it auto-runs >5s).

Touch-point illumination radiating to neighbors (GlassEffectContainer pattern) — in iOS-26 a touch on one glass element radiates light to nearby glass in the same container. Web analogue for the dock: a pointer over one DockIconButton could lift a faint shared-intensity floor on sibling controls (a group-scoped --specular-intensity bump), reinforcing the dock-as-one-material read. Currently glass-ui scopes --specular-* per-surface (inherits:false) by design — neighbor-radiance would be an opt-in group layer, not a default.
notes.applicability:
"glass-ui already has a SOTA-shaped implementation — the work is TUNE + UNIFY + TOKENIZE, not build-from-scratch. Current state: (1) ONE unified specular source at glass.css .glass-material::before (AW.W22 folded glass-specular-track.css into the .glass-material selector group — five ladder rungs + .glass-card + .dock-icon-button all compose it); (2) typed @property regs in tokens.css §18 (--specular-x/y/intensity, inherits:false, initial 0); (3) screen blend + masked radial already correct; (4) the silhouette rim unified onto --glass-material-rim; (5) the pointer-write seam duplicated in DockIconButton.vue + Card.vue.

The W09 path forward (already charted, Band B blocker, dependsOn W00): (a) drop the inner stop from pure-white-0.55α to warm-cream-low-alpha — glass.css line 113 hsl(40 30% 100%/0.55) resolves to white, violating its own comment; (b) halve the ladder to rest≈0/0.08, hover≈0.22, active≈0.32 (currently 0.35/0.6/0.85 — too hot, made WORSE by the AW.W22 blast-radius promotion onto EVERY band surface); (c) tokenize the three rungs as --glass-specular-intensity-{rest,hover,active}+dark so magnitude is one overridable cohort (glass.css lines 105/162/173 are buried literals); (d) drop rest floor to ~0 so static unwired surfaces are clean (the @property initial-value is already 0; the ::before's --specular-intensity:0.35 defeats it); (e) RETIRE the dock control's SECOND specular — the --glass-highlight hover box-shadow in dock-controls.css:102 that stacks ON TOP of the moving ::before on the most-hovered surface (the worst blowout); (f) lift the duplicated trackSpecular into useSpecularTracking() in composables/dom or motion; (g) ADD Card specular?:'off'|'subtle'|'full' opt-in prop (keyframes.js consumer ask) so a resting panel is clean by default.

Unified morph-facility fit: the specular is the MATERIAL half of the one Liquid-Glass behaviour whose SPRING half is the press-squish (scale toward --scale-press-dock/--scale-press-btn). glass.css lines 21-28 already cross-reference this. The morph facility wants BOTH wired to the same interaction state machine: on press, the spring squishes AND the catch-light blooms in lockstep (glass.css :hover/:active::before already does the intensity lift in the same rungs the scale keys off — keep that lockstep). For the morph facility, useSpecularTracking() becomes the shared pointer-anchor that any morphing element (dock, button, card, dialog) opts into, so a morph between two glass shapes carries the catch-light across the View-Transition. The intensity tokens become the single dial the morph facility turns to make a morphing surface 'catch light' as it settles. CRITICAL co-update: proof-glass-material-unified.mjs:167,170 hardcodes 0.6/0.85 — the gate lands RED unless re-pointed to assert the TOKENS exist (not literal values)."
pitfalls: A registered-@property var() nested inside an hsl() alpha computes to 0 in Chromium — glass.css already learned this (line 109 comment): drive the LAYER opacity with --specular-intensity, never a per-stop alpha. Any retune must keep intensity on the ::before opacity, not fold it into the gradient stop alpha.

Pure-white inner stop + screen blend = blowout. The screen blend asymptotes toward white on contact, so an already-white authored core saturates instantly into a hard disc. The authored color MUST start warm-and-dim (low-alpha cream). This is the literal root cause W09 names (Slice 14 F0): pure-white MAGNITUDE × AW.W22 BLAST-RADIUS promotion onto every surface.

Double-specular stacking. The dock control composes BOTH the moving ::before catch-light AND a --glass-highlight inset box-shadow on hover (dock-controls.css:102) — two highlights on the single most-hovered surface in the app. Retire one (the box-shadow) or they compound into the worst blowout.

Non-zero rest floor defeats the clean-at-rest intent. The @property initial-value is 0, but the ::before sets --specular-intensity:0.35 unconditionally, so EVERY static glass surface paints a dead-centered bloom (the pointer var floors at 50% 50% with no pointer). Drop the rest floor to ~0 so an un-hovered, un-wired surface is genuinely clean.

prefers-reduced-transparency is NOT Baseline (no Firefox, partial elsewhere) — it cannot be the SOLE guard. glass-specular-track.css uses it to drop the ::before, which is correct as a progressive enhancement, but the reduced-MOTION guard (Baseline, pins --specular-x/y to 50% + transition:none) is the mandatory one. Don't rely on reduced-transparency for the core a11y story.

Auto-running ambient/device-tilt drift at rest is non-essential motion >5s — if added, it falls under WCAG 2.2.2 (pause/stop/hide) and must respect prefers-reduced-motion AND be user-stoppable, same obligation class as the AV backgrounds (DockBackgroundToggle). Don't add 'alive at rest' shimmer without the stop control.

Per-surface ownership (inherits:false) is load-bearing — it's the no-glass-on-glass discipline made mechanical (a hovered parent must not push its specular onto a child). Any 'radiate to neighbors' group feature must be an explicit opt-in layer that does NOT break the inherits:false default, or nested glass will inherit a parent's pointer position.

mix-blend-mode:screen on a ::before forces the element onto its own stacking/compositing context and can interact badly with backdrop-filter ordering and z-index:1 — verify the catch-light still sits ABOVE the blur but BELOW content, and that it doesn't trigger an extra raster layer per surface (cost multiplies across every band rung after the AW.W22 promotion).

Pointer-write must stay style-only. trackSpecular writes CSS vars via :style binding — keep it off any reactive path that re-renders; a getBoundingClientRect per pointermove is a forced layout read, so cache the rect on pointerenter if profiling shows jank on dense dock grids.

Gate coupling: proof-glass-material-unified.mjs hardcodes the OLD intensity literals (0.6/0.85 at :167,170). Tokenizing without co-updating the gate lands the whole tune RED — the charter flags this as the CRITICAL COUPLING.

notes.facet: Adaptive glass tint + glass-over-content legibility — the content-aware tint, the scrim, the contrast guarantee
sotaTechniques: ADAPTIVE TINT MAPPED TO BACKDROP BRIGHTNESS (Apple's core mechanism, WWDC25 s219): selecting a tint color generates a RANGE of tones mapped to the brightness of the content underneath — hue/brightness/saturation shift with what's behind without deviating from the intended color (real-colored-glass model). The tint amount + dynamic range auto-shift so controls stay legible while passing as much content as possible. Web port: bias the surface bg toward a sampled-backdrop value via color-mix(in oklab, <rung>, var(--glass-tint-source) var(--glass-tint-strength)) — exactly glass-ui's AW.W23 recipe, today shipping with strength 0% (no-op).

REGULAR vs CLEAR variant split + DIMMING LAYER (Apple): two materials that are never mixed. Regular is adaptive/self-legible over ANY content (auto light/dark flip on small nav elements, symbols mirror the glass to maximize contrast); Clear is permanently transparent and REQUIRES a dimming layer (a darkening scrim under the glass) — used only over media-rich, bold/bright content the dim won't harm. The dimming can be LOCALIZED to small elements to retain surrounding content vibrancy.

CONTENT-AWARE SHADOW ADAPTATION (Apple s219; glass-ui already ships this): the glass RAISES its drop/under-shadow opacity when over TEXT (so it lifts visibly off the text) and LOWERS it over a solid light background. glass-ui's `.glass-over-text` / `[data-over-content="text"|"solid"]` modifier is a direct, attribute-driven, JS-free port that swaps the `--glass-under-shadow-*` rung per tier.

SCROLL EDGE EFFECT (Apple s219): as content scrolls under a glass bar, a gradient mask DISSOLVES the content into the background at the glass edge, lifting the glass visually above the moving content and maintaining the contrast boundary. Two styles — adaptive (gradual fade) and hard (uniform, for pinned headers). Web port: a `mask-image: linear-gradient()` fade-band or a gradient-tint band at the bar's leading edge (Comeau's 'flickering top' fix is the same move).

PROGRESSIVE / LAYERED BLUR (Family.co / Rauno register; Kenneth Nym, Devs-Love-Coffee): a SINGLE backdrop blur keeps high-frequency color from the backdrop and reads muddy/illegible; STACKING several backdrop-filter layers with increasing blur radius + offset linear-gradient masks produces a smooth blur RAMP that kills the high-frequency noise behind text. The legibility win is the gradient, not a bigger single blur.

DUAL-LAYER SCRIM FILM (Josh Comeau; 2026 a11y-first consensus): never put text directly on a low-opacity blurred surface — composite a SEMI-OPAQUE tint film (~30-50% bg, e.g. hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.5)) ON the glass so text rides a consistent backing regardless of backdrop. saturate(140%) + slight brightness(90%) on the backdrop-filter restores the vibrancy the blur drains (the SwiftUI 'vibrancy' analog) without raising opacity. The scrim film is the contrast guarantee; the blur is decoration.

contrast-color() — NATIVE ADAPTIVE FOREGROUND (CSS Color 6; Baseline April 2026, Chrome 147 / FF 146 / Safari 26): `color: contrast-color(var(--bg))` returns black or white, whichever wins WCAG contrast against the bg — auto-legible foreground with zero JS. Brand-tint it via relative color syntax `oklch(from contrast-color(var(--bg)) l 0.05 var(--hue))`; soften via `color-mix(in oklch, contrast-color(var(--bg)) 80%, var(--bg))`. Caveats: binary output (snaps, no fade; tipping ~18% luminance), composites transparency against opaque white, no gradients/url(), overridden by forced-colors.

RELATIVE-COLOR-SYNTAX LUMINANCE PICKER (CSS-only, ships TODAY pre-contrast-color baseline; Matt Ström / Piccalilli): `color(from var(--c) xyz clamp(0,(.36/y - 1)*infinity,1) ...)` reads the bg's XYZ Y (luminance) and snaps the foreground to black/white at the WCAG threshold — a pure-CSS contrast-color() polyfill usable now as the @supports fallback.

light-dark() + color-scheme AUTO POLARITY (Baseline 2024): `--surface: light-dark(#fff,#121212)` flips the glass tint base with the system scheme in one declaration — the web equivalent of Apple's automatic light↔dark material flip, no `.dark`-class duplication.

APCA / Lc CONTRAST FLOOR FOR TRANSLUCENT TEXT (WCAG 3 candidate; 2026 practitioner default): WCAG 2.x luminance-ratio math has perceptual blind spots over translucent/mid-tone surfaces; APCA's Lc value accounts for polarity, surround, and font weight/size (thin fonts need higher Lc). Use APCA as the verification oracle for text-over-glass even while WCAG 2.x AA stays the compliance gate.

prefers-reduced-transparency + prefers-contrast ESCAPE HATCHES (glass-ui already ships): under `reduce` collapse glass opacity→1 and blur→none (text rides a solid surface); under `prefers-contrast: more` raise the per-rung opacity floor. These are the binding accessibility overrides the adaptive tint must never defeat.

forced-colors STRUCTURE-SURVIVAL SKIN (AX.W36): under Windows-High-Contrast backdrop-filter + inset shadows are dropped entirely; the contrast guarantee becomes a `1px solid CanvasText` border + system-color focus (Highlight), so structure survives when the glass evaporates. The contrast story is incomplete without this skin.

NN/g LEGIBILITY DISCIPLINE (the negative SOTA): tint SELECTIVELY (primary actions only — tinting everything kills emphasis and reads as visual noise); glass belongs on the navigation/overlay band, NOT over dense content; a darker/more-uniform base behind the glass beats a bigger blur for readability. The contrast guarantee is a DESIGN constraint, not just a math check.
notes.applicability: glass-ui is unusually far ahead on this facet — the SOTA largely VALIDATES and EXTENDS machinery already in src/. (1) ADAPTIVE TINT: the AW.W23 recipe is already universal — every ladder rung's bg is `color-mix(in oklab, <rung-bg>, var(--glass-tint-source) var(--glass-tint-strength))` (glass.css L201-262), with defaults `--glass-tint-source: var(--card)` + `--glass-tint-strength: 0%` (tokens.css L714-715) = byte-identical no-op. The morph-facility path: WIRE this seam to a live backdrop sample. A `useBackdropTint(rootRef)` composable samples the dominant backdrop hue/luminance (a 1px hidden-canvas proxy per Lucky Graphics, or reading the Aurora/GooBlob ColorResolver glass-ui already owns) and writes `--glass-tint-source` + a clamped `--glass-tint-strength` (≤30%, the mwg ceiling) onto the glass host — turning the static recipe into Apple's content-mapped tint with ZERO CSS edit. The dock (`--glass-bg-dock`) and overlay band are the first consumers. (2) CONTENT-AWARE SHADOW: already shipped as `.glass-over-text` / `[data-over-content]` (glass.css L265-299) — a direct port of Apple's shadow-raise-over-text. The morph path makes it AUTOMATIC: the same `useBackdropTint` sample that drives tint also sets `data-over-content=\"text|solid\"` from the backdrop's high-frequency/luminance reading, so the under-shadow rung tracks content live instead of being hand-set. (3) SCRIM/DIMMING: glass-ui has overlay-scrim tokens (tokens.css L848-850) for modals but NO per-element scrim FILM and no Clear-variant dimming layer. The gap: a `.glass-scrim` opt-in (a semi-opaque inset film, ~30-50%, behind text-bearing content) is the missing contrast GUARANTEE for glass over busy/media content — the dual-layer Comeau move. This is the one genuinely new primitive this facet needs, and it pairs with a Regular/Clear variant axis on the glass material (Regular = adaptive tint default; Clear = transparent + mandatory `.glass-scrim`). (4) SCROLL EDGE: the dock already masks its scroll ports with a fade (dock.css), but there's no leading-edge content-dissolve band on a glass bar pinned over scrolling content — a `--glass-scroll-edge` mask recipe (composing the existing scroll-driven.css substrate) is the dock/header-ribbon applicability. (5) VIBRANCY: the five-rung ladder uses blur but NOT saturate() — adding `saturate(--glass-saturation)` to the `--glass-blur-*` tokens restores the color the blur drains (the SwiftUI vibrancy analog), a one-token addition. (6) NATIVE FOREGROUND: dock glyph/label colors are hand-tokenized; `contrast-color(var(--glass-tint-source))` (with the relative-color-syntax XYZ fallback as @supports) would make EVERY glass-control foreground auto-legible against the live adaptive tint — the keystone that closes the loop (adaptive tint → auto-contrasting foreground). UNIFIED MORPH FACILITY: the single-scalar `--dock-morph-t` clock (AX.W01) should ALSO drive a `--glass-tint-strength` ramp — as the dock morphs/lifts, its tint can deepen toward the backdrop, making the tint part of the same one-clock motion rather than a separate channel. This binds the MATERIAL half (adaptive tint/scrim) to the SPRING half (the morph) the dock README already frames as one behaviour.
pitfalls: contrast-color() SNAPS (binary black/white, no smooth transition; tipping at ~18% luminance not 50%) — animating a control's foreground across a moving backdrop will pop, not fade. Mitigate with `color-mix(... 80%, bg)` softening or accept the discrete flip on a debounced sample, never per-frame.

contrast-color() composites transparent inputs against assumed-opaque WHITE before the math — feeding it a `--glass-tint-source` that is itself translucent gives a WRONG contrast pick. Sample/flatten to an opaque value first.

Live backdrop sampling (canvas readback / getImageData) is a MAIN-THREAD, GPU-readback cost — sampling per scroll/rAF frame will jank. Debounce hard (on settle, on scroll-end, on IntersectionObserver), cap to a low-res proxy, and gate it behind the existing useIntersectionPause/offscreen-park machinery so an offscreen dock samples zero frames.

backdrop-filter is the dominant GPU cost — each filter forces a screen-buffer copy + kernel reblur; Lucky Graphics cites ~3 concurrent glass panels before mobile chokes. The 'no glass on glass' discipline (already in glass.css/dock README) is the load-bearing perf guard — stacking adaptive-tint layers multiplies it. Keep glass to the nav/overlay band.

A bigger single blur does NOT fix legibility — high-frequency backdrop color survives a flat blur and muddies text. The SCRIM FILM (semi-opaque backing) or progressive-blur RAMP is the actual contrast fix; do not let 'increase blur' substitute for the scrim.

Adaptive tint defeats WCAG if the sampled strength pushes the surface toward the text color — clamp `--glass-tint-strength` (≤30%) and verify the worst-case sampled tint still passes contrast for the foreground; the tint must never be the SOLE legibility mechanism (it complements the scrim, per NN/g).

WCAG 2.x ratio math has perceptual blind spots over translucent/mid-tone surfaces (medium blue passes math, fails perception) — use APCA/Lc as the real oracle for text-over-glass even though WCAG 2.x AA is the compliance gate. A green proof:contrast under WCAG 2.x can still be illegible.

Over-tinting is the NN/g failure: tinting EVERY element (not just primary actions) kills emphasis and reads as visual noise. The adaptive-tint facility must default OFF/subtle (strength 0% today) and be applied selectively — the library default must stay neutral, presets-in-consumer.

forced-colors:active drops backdrop-filter AND inset shadows entirely — the whole adaptive-tint + scrim + under-shadow contrast story EVAPORATES. The W36 `1px solid CanvasText` structure-survival skin is mandatory or the contrast guarantee is a lie under Windows-High-Contrast.

prefers-reduced-transparency must FULLY win over adaptive tint — glass.css already flattens opacity→1/blur→none under reduce, but a JS `useBackdropTint` writing `--glass-tint-strength` could re-introduce translucency; the composable must read the media query and no-op (write 0% / opaque) under reduce.
saturate() in the blur stack can over-saturate dark/vivid backdrops into garish fringing — token it (`--glass-saturation`, ~120-140%) with a dark-arm override, don't hardcode 140% globally.

Clear-variant glass without its mandatory dimming layer is the single worst Apple-cited mistake — if glass-ui ships a Clear/transparent variant it MUST bundle `.glass-scrim` (the dimming layer is not optional), or the variant is a legibility footgun by construction.

notes.facet: CSS 2025 glass capabilities baseline — backdrop-filter, color-mix, light-dark, @supports gating, the fallback ladder
sotaTechniques: backdrop-filter + saturate() blur stack (Baseline Newly Available 2024) — the frosted-glass primitive: blurs+desaturates the backdrop behind a navigation/overlay surface. Safari dropped the -webkit- prefix at 18; glass-ui already single-sources the unprefixed form and lets Lightning CSS emit the legacy alias per browserslist (glass.css:184-198 documents this exactly). State of the art: AUTHOR ONE unprefixed decl, never both manually (the manual dual caused Lightning CSS dedup-keep-prefixed → dropped from modern Chromium CSSOM).

color-mix(in oklab, ...) for adaptive tint + alpha derivatives (Baseline Widely Available) — mixes a rung background toward a sampled backdrop hue in a perceptual space. glass-ui already ships this as the AW.W23 adaptive-tint recipe (`color-mix(in oklab, <rung bg>, var(--glass-tint-source) var(--glass-tint-strength))`, default 0% = no-op). oklab is the correct mix space; the house rule (NEVER `oklch(from ...)` lightness-shift — browsers don't gamut-map yet) is the current SOTA caveat. This is the web analogue of Apple's 'glass color is informed by surrounding content'.

light-dark() function (Baseline Newly Available 2024) — returns one of two colors based on the element's resolved color-scheme, collapsing a `.dark`-class color pair into one token without a selector. glass-ui currently uses a `.dark`-class cascade (re-resolving --foreground/--shadow-color) instead — a deliberate choice that survives Canvas2D consumers (the constellation Canvas2D-leak pitfall: light-dark() returns a computed value Canvas can't read). SOTA: light-dark() for DOM glass tokens, plain-hsl for any token a <canvas> samples.

@supports feature-gating as the fallback-ladder spine — the progressive-enhancement contract: `@supports (corner-shape: squircle)` over a `border-radius` round base, `@supports (overlay: auto)` for the @starting-style top-layer grammar, `@supports not ((backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: ...))` for the opaque solid-fill fallback. glass-ui ALREADY ships all three exactly. The discipline (corner-shape decl ONLY inside the @supports block, never leaking onto the un-gated base) is the SOTA correctness rule.

@starting-style + transition-behavior: allow-discrete + overlay (Baseline Newly Available 2024) — pure-CSS entry/exit for native top-layer surfaces ([popover], <dialog>) animating from a closed starting state through display/overlay discrete properties. glass-ui ships this verbatim as the AQ.W5 `.glass-top-layer` grammar (animations.css:325-366), gated on `@supports (overlay: auto)`. This is the platform-owned replacement for per-frame JS entry animation.

View Transitions API (same-document SPA: Baseline Newly Available as Firefox 144 shipped per Interop 2025) — snapshots old+new DOM states tagged `view-transition-name`/`view-transition-class` and morphs geometry + crossfades as ONE browser-owned mutation, with `:active-view-transition-type()` for directional curves. glass-ui uses it for the dock layer morph today — but AX.W01 RETIRES the VT fork for the dock-COLLAPSE morph (VT rasterizes pixels = wrong primitive for a layout morph; it desyncs the uncaptured animating ancestor) while PRESERVING the per-instance view-transition-name for consumer ROUTE morphs (fourier). SOTA distinction: VT for page/route geometry morphs, an analytic spring for an element's own continuous morph.

interpolate-size: allow-keywords + calc-size() (Chrome 129+, NOT Safari/Firefox as of 2025) — enables transitions between a length and an intrinsic keyword (auto/max-content/fit-content), i.e. animate-to-height:auto in pure CSS. glass-ui DELIBERATELY retired this from the dock (AV.W9.0): on Chrome 129+ it second-drove `width` on the browser clock while the SpringProgress wrote inline width per frame — a dual-driver race that froze the dock. SOTA lesson: one driver per axis; this stays rejected until cross-engine support + a way to make it the SOLE driver lands.

linear() easing built from an analytic spring ODE (Baseline Widely Available) — a 48-stop `linear()` sample of a damped-harmonic-oscillator, so a CSS transition and a runtime JS spring trace the SAME curve. glass-ui's `--spring-{dock,snappy,bouncy,smooth}` tokens are generated by `regen-spring-tokens.mjs` and bit-mirror the keyframes.js SpringProgress (DOCK_SPRING response 0.32 ζ 0.7 = --spring-dock). This is the web transposition of Apple's `spring(response:dampingFraction:)` two-knob control language. SOTA: the build-time CSS token and the runtime integrator share one ODE so they cannot drift (proof:spring-tokens-synced).

corner-shape: squircle / superellipse() (Chrome 139+ only, 2025) — the literal iOS-26 superellipse corner geometry that backdrop-filter, border, and shadow all follow; interpolable between keywords. glass-ui ships it @supports-gated over the border-radius round (glass.css:615, dock.css:416). SOTA framing (already in-code): the round arc is the CONTRACT, the squircle the better tier — NOT a degraded fallback.

SVG feDisplacementMap refraction as backdrop-filter (Chrome/Edge ONLY, 2025 frontier — NOT Safari/Firefox) — the true 'liquid glass' lensing Apple ships natively: a precomputed RGBA displacement map (R=x-shift, G=y-shift, neutral 128) encoding Snell's-law refraction along the surface normal, applied via `backdrop-filter: url(#filter)` to bend (not just blur) the backdrop, with per-channel scale offsets for chromatic aberration. This is the ONE genuine capability glass-ui does NOT have — its specular `::before` catch-light approximates the highlight but there is no lensing. The kube.io/rizroze technique is the reference. Falls back to plain backdrop-blur on non-Chromium (graceful).

prefers-reduced-transparency / prefers-contrast / prefers-reduced-motion media gates — the accessibility fallback ladder Apple auto-applies (Reduced Transparency increases frosting, Increased Contrast adds borders, Reduced Motion tones elastic effects). glass-ui already maps all three: `@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce)` sets every blur to none + opacity to 1 (glass.css:626), `prefers-contrast: more` lifts opacities, and the chromatic edge-dispersion is gated `@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: no-preference)`. This is the WCAG-binding half of the material and is the SOTA mandatory complement to any glass.
notes.applicability: GLASS PRIMITIVES: glass-ui is already at or near the 2025 baseline for this facet — the .glass-material ladder (glass.css) ALREADY ships color-mix(oklab) adaptive tint, the unified --glass-edge-light rim, the pointer-tracked moving-specular `::before` catch-light (the 'illuminate-from-within' iOS behaviour via @property --specular-* + --mouse-x/y), OKLCh under-shadows, content-aware under-shadow (glass-over-text/[data-over-content]), chromatic edge-dispersion (--glass-edge-dispersion gated on reduced-transparency), corner-shape squircle, and the full @supports fallback ladder to opaque solid fills. The single missing SOTA capability is TRUE REFRACTIVE LENSING (feDisplacementMap as backdrop-filter) — the specular `::before` is the highlight half; there is no light-BENDING half. Path forward for the morph facility: add an opt-in `.glass-refractive` class wiring a Chrome-only SVG feDisplacementMap backdrop-filter (precomputed per-corner-radius displacement map, scale-animatable for the squish), @supports-gated over the existing backdrop-blur as a pure enhancement — zero regression on Safari/Firefox/the reduced-transparency ladder. DOCK + ANIMATION: the unified morph facility AX wants ('iOS-26 morphing/springy/liquid for EVERY element') already has its spring spine — useSpring/useLayerTransition wrap the keyframes.js analytic ODE, and the --spring-dock linear() token bit-mirrors it so CSS transitions and JS springs share one curve. The CSS-2025 baseline contributes the COMPLEMENTARY pieces: (1) AX.W01's single-scalar `--dock-morph-t` written once per frame, with every axis (width/padding/radius/scale/color/stagger) expressed as calc() off that one scalar — this IS the platform-correct unification (one clock, one driver, no VT-vs-FLIP fork, the platform's own interpolate-size race avoided by construction). (2) corner-shape squircle interpolating on the SAME spring as the pill↔card radius morph (dock.css already transitions border-radius on --dock-motion-resize) gives the literal iOS shape-blend. (3) @starting-style/allow-discrete is the native entry grammar for any dock-hosted popover/dialog so the morph facility never hand-rolls entry JS. (4) View-Transitions stays for consumer ROUTE morphs (preserve the named-element seam) but is the WRONG primitive for an element's own continuous morph — that is the single analytic spring. The 'liquid/morphing for every element' goal is reachable by generalizing the dock's one-scalar pattern into a `useMorphScalar(stateRef)` primitive that ANY glass surface (Card, Sheet, Switch thumb, Button) consumes to drive its size/shape/specular from one spring — exactly the material↔spring duality the dock README already documents.
pitfalls: DUAL-DRIVER RACE on the same axis — interpolate-size/calc-size() on Chrome 129+ second-drives width on the browser clock while a JS spring writes inline width per frame, cancelling the morph and FREEZING the element (the AV.W9.0 dock-freeze, born-RED under proof:dock-animation-live). RULE: exactly one driver per animated axis per engine; never let a CSS-native intrinsic-size interpolation coexist with a JS spring on the same property.

VIEW-TRANSITIONS IS THE WRONG PRIMITIVE FOR A LAYOUT MORPH — VT crossfades RASTERIZED pixel snapshots of `::view-transition-*` pseudos, so an animating ANCESTOR is captured as a static image and desyncs from a child that morphs on a different clock (the dock root-chrome-vs-inner-width desync). It also has unmeasurable timing (181 rAF getBoundingClientRect samples captured NO morph per keyframes' device probe) and duplicate-view-transition-name collisions DROP the morph (fourier two-co-mounted-docks → glass-dock-1 collision). Use VT only for whole route/page geometry morphs; use an analytic spring for an element's own continuous morph.

backdrop-filter blur is GPU/battery-EXPENSIVE — each blurred surface mints a compositor layer and REPAINTS the entire backdrop every scroll frame; Apple measured 13% vs 1% battery drain in iOS 26. Animating a large blur radius on a low-end device drops frames and heats the device. RULE: backdrop-filter on STATIC/RARE navigation+overlay surfaces only (the no-glass-on-glass discipline already enforces this — nested glass stacks blurs); never on a list of cards or a per-frame-animating surface. Reduce/drop blur on small viewports + reduced-transparency.

SVG-filter-as-backdrop-filter is CHROME/EDGE-ONLY (2025) — feDisplacementMap refraction via `backdrop-filter: url(#f)` does NOT work in Safari or Firefox; plain `filter:` works cross-browser but backdrop-filter+SVG is Chromium-exclusive. Any refractive lensing MUST be @supports-gated as an enhancement over backdrop-blur, never the contract. Also: a shape change requires recomputing the whole displacement map (only the feDisplacementMap `scale` is cheaply animatable) — so a squish animates scale, but a radius morph would need a precomputed map per radius.

OVER-ANIMATION + LEGIBILITY COLLAPSE (the NN/g critique) — 'restless, less predictable, less legible, constantly pulling focus'; transparent controls over noisy backgrounds drop contrast below WCAG 2.2 AA, and ambient bounce/jitter is visual noise. RULE (already in the dock README): bounce belongs on USER-INITIATED changes (tap/expand), NEVER ambient idle motion; honor prefers-reduced-motion as binding; keep the warm-cream low-alpha specular (NOT iOS blue, NOT a blowout — the AX-audited specular blew out white). Glass stays in the navigation/overlay band; content layer is never glass.

light-dark() / oklch(from ...) leak into Canvas2D — light-dark() returns a context-resolved value and oklch(from) relative-color isn't gamut-mapped by browsers yet; a <canvas> (constellation/aurora overlay) that samples these reads garbage or transparent. RULE: DOM glass tokens may use light-dark(); any token a canvas reads must be a plain hsl()/rgb() resolved value (the constellation Canvas2D-safe-plain-hsl precept).

MANUAL -webkit- prefix duplication on backdrop-filter — authoring both -webkit-backdrop-filter and backdrop-filter manually made Lightning CSS (Tailwind v4) dedup-and-keep-PREFIXED, which modern Chromium then DROPPED from the CSSOM (the prefixed alias is parser-rejected post-Chrome 113). RULE: author ONE unprefixed decl; let the build pipeline emit the legacy alias per browserslist (glass.css already documents and follows this).

@property var() nested in an hsl() alpha computes to 0 in Chromium — a registered-@property custom property used inside an hsl() alpha channel resolves to zero (the specular layer would vanish). glass-ui already works around this by driving the specular layer OPACITY off --specular-intensity rather than a per-stop alpha. Any new typed-property-driven glass channel must drive opacity/a separate layer, not an inline hsl alpha.

notes.facet: Glass DEPTH / layering / elevation — the z-stack, the shadow ladder, the sense of stacked liquid sheets
sotaTechniques: THREE-BAND ELEVATION HIERARCHY (content / navigation / overlay) — Apple's hard rule: glass is reserved EXCLUSIVELY for the navigation layer that floats above content; content is never glass; overlay is vibrancy/fills ON glass. The three bands ARE the z-stack; elevation is band-membership, not a free-floating shadow value. glass-ui already encodes this exactly (tokens.css §3 --z-* registry + glass.css 'no-glass-on-glass' header).

SIZE-COUPLED THICKNESS/SHADOW/LENSING (WWDC25 sess.219 'Meet Liquid Glass') — when glass flexes/morphs to a LARGER size (toolbar button -> menu), it simulates a THICKER material: it casts deeper, richer shadows, gains more pronounced lensing+refraction, and softer light scattering. Elevation is a CONTINUOUS function of the surface's current extent, not a discrete rung. This is the single biggest SOTA gap vs a static shadow ladder.

ADAPTIVE / CONTENT-AWARE SHADOW (WWDC25 + conorluddy reference) — shadow OPACITY increases over text (so glass reads as lifting OFF the text) and decreases over solid/white backgrounds; as text scrolls underneath, the shadow becomes more prominent to add separation. Inverse-brightness coupling, sampled from the backdrop at runtime.

GlassEffectContainer + glassEffectID + spacing (SwiftUI iOS 26) — multiple glass shapes share ONE sampling region (glass cannot sample other glass) and morph into one another via a matched-geometry transition; the `spacing` parameter is a morph THRESHOLD — shapes within that distance visually blend/merge as they approach. The web analogue is a single shared backdrop-filter context + a measured FLIP/View-Transition morph, NOT N independent blurred plates.

BACKDROP DE-EMPHASIS ON OVERLAY (Rauno 'Designing Depth') — when an overlay launches, push the layer beneath DOWN the z-axis by blurring it, dimming it, and SCALING it down slightly (the iOS context-menu / home-screen recipe). The recede of the backdrop is what sells the lift of the overlay — depth is RELATIVE motion between two layers, not an absolute shadow on one.

INFINITE-BOUNDARY EDGE FADE (Rauno 'Designing Depth') — fade out the bottom edge of a container (mask-image gradient) so the boundary reads as 'continuing beneath' rather than a hard stop; combined with inner-background blur this lowers a layer on z without any 3D transform.

FULL-PERIMETER EDGE RIM / CATCH-LIGHT (WWDC25 sess.219) — a 0.5-0.75px inner light ring 'defines the silhouette' of a glass plate and is the cheapest depth cue: it separates the plate edge from whatever is behind it independent of the drop shadow. glass-ui already ships this as --glass-edge-light on every rung.

UNDER-SHADOW HAIRLINE (iOS Liquid Glass thickness cue) — a sub-pixel dark hairline along the BOTTOM edge reads as the physical THICKNESS of the glass slab (the floor), composed UNDER the diffuse lift shadow. A two-part shadow recipe: under-shadow lays the floor + the broad soft shadow lays the lift. glass-ui already ships --glass-under-shadow-{quiet,default,vivid}.

MULTI-SHADOW ELEVATION RECIPE (Material 3 / Josh Comeau) — each elevation level = 2-4 stacked box-shadows of increasing blur+offset and DECREASING opacity (key-light + fill-light + ambient-occlusion), all sharing one --shadow-color, NOT a single shadow. 4-6 named rungs is the practitioner ceiling; more is noise. glass-ui's --shadow-xs..2xl + glass-shadow-* ladder already follows this.

SHARED-ELEMENT MORPH ACROSS Z (Family.co / Benji 'Family Values') — trays/sheets morph between elevation levels with shared persistent elements (a card moves between screens, a button glides into a tray); each subsequent tray VARIES IN HEIGHT so the depth progression is unmistakable. Depth is communicated by continuity + size delta, not by re-mounting a new modal.

SAME-DOCUMENT VIEW TRANSITIONS — now Baseline (Oct 2025) — view-transition-name + startViewTransition morph an element's position/size/shape between two DOM states; view-transition-class styles snapshot collections; match-element auto-names. The native primitive for a depth/elevation morph BUT it crossfades rasterized pixels (the wrong primitive for a live layout/shadow morph — see pitfalls).

interpolate-size: allow-keywords + calc-size() — lets height/width animate to/from intrinsic keywords (auto/min-content/fit-content), so an expanding sheet can grow to its natural size on a real transition instead of a magic pixel cap — the size axis of a depth morph becomes declarative.

STAGGERED / CHOREOGRAPHED LAYER MOTION (Rauno) — layers must NOT move in perfect synchrony; staggering onset makes a flat swipe read as 3D (the iOS unlock); sequence the recede of the lower layer to COMPLETE before the upper layer surfaces, so they never visually collide.

INTERRUPTIBLE SPRING DEPTH (Emil Kowalski 'Great Animations') — springs retain velocity when interrupted; CSS keyframes restart from zero. An elevation morph the user can reverse mid-flight (collapse-while-expanding) MUST run on a live spring scalar, not a fixed-duration transition. Keep UI motion <300ms; default ease-out for one-shot, spring for gesture-reversible.

CSS perspective + translateZ scale-by-depth — scale factor = perspective / (perspective - translateZ); a small translateZ on a parent-perspective container yields a physically-correct size+parallax depth cue at 60fps with no JS, the cheap web stand-in for true lensing on hover/tilt.
notes.applicability: DOCK is the navigation band (already correct at --z-dock=40). The headline gap is morph-coupled elevation: drive the dock shadow/rim/under-shadow off the W01 --dock-morph-t scalar so it continuously deepens as the dock expands/wraps (W04's --shadow-dock-wrap on the same resize spring) — the literal 'thicker material when morphed larger' mechanic. W02's one-orchestrator-per-dock IS the web GlassEffectContainer analogue (one shared morph context; --dock-stagger-step == the SwiftUI `spacing` morph threshold). GLASS is genuinely at SOTA on the STATIC ladder (three-band rule, uniform rim, 3-rung under-shadow, content-aware .glass-over-text modifier all shipped). backdrop-filter: blur() is GPU-EXPENSIVE and COMPOUNDS — 'glass-on-glass' stacks the blur twice (muddy + doubled rim), and N independent blurred plates spin up fans on mobile. The no-glass-on-glass discipline is a PERF rule as much as an aesthetic one; nest FLAT tiers inside glass, share ONE blur context (the GlassEffectContainer lesson).

ANIMATING box-shadow / backdrop-filter directly is a repaint-heavy non-composited property — morphing shadow per-frame off the spring can drop frames. Prefer animating opacity of a pre-rendered shadow pseudo-element, or transform/translateZ for the lift, and clamp shadow updates; gate live backdrop-luminance sampling behind requestIdleCallback / IntersectionObserver (the useIntersectionPause seam already exists).

DEEPER SHADOWS REDUCE CONTRAST — a richer drop shadow + heavier specular over text can fail WCAG legibility; Apple's adaptive shadow EXISTS to protect legibility (raise over text). Any size-coupled deepening must respect the content-aware rung, not blow past it. Coordinate with W09 (specular tune-to-subtle: the dock is currently the hottest surface; do not let elevation deepening re-inflate it).

RUNG PROLIFERATION — practitioners cap at 4-6 elevation levels; a continuous morph-t elevation must still SNAP to / interpolate BETWEEN the named --shadow-* / --glass-shadow-* rungs, not invent unbounded shadow values, or the system loses its token-first overridability (J invariant) and consumers can no longer retune by overriding a rung.

prefers-reduced-motion — depth-by-MOTION (parallax, staggered recede, scale-on-overlay) must degrade to a static dim/blur under PRM; the WebGL substrate already freezes, but the CSS depth-morph recipes need their own @media(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) fallback.

translateZ/perspective 3D depth creates a new stacking + compositing context that can clip children, break position:fixed, and fight the top-layer (popover/dialog) — keep true-3D depth to leaf interaction surfaces (card tilt), NOT structural layers that host overlays.

ADAPTIVE-SHADOW SAMPLING needs a luminance source — there is no CSS 'read my backdrop brightness' primitive; runtime sampling means getComputedStyle/canvas readback or a hand-fed --backdrop-luminance token. Don't over-engineer: the shipped attribute-driven .glass-over-text / [data-over-content] modifier is the pragmatic 80% and is already at SOTA for the static case.

SwiftUI glassEffectID/GlassEffectContainer has NO 1:1 web primitive — do not promise 'glass shapes that merge'; the web morph is FLIP/measured-geometry + a shared blur container, and metaball-style glass MERGING needs WebGL (the goo-blob substrate), not CSS. notes.facet: A unified useLiquidMorph composable DESIGN — the matched-geometry seam, the API surface, how a component opts in. sotaTechniques: SINGLE-SCALAR MORPH CLOCK — an analytic damped-harmonic spring writes ONE normalized progress 0 to 1 into a CSS var --morph-t once per frame; every animated axis (width, padding, radius, scale, color-mix, child-stagger threshold) is a calc off that one scalar, so the element morphs in a single paint on one clock with zero per-axis desync. FLIP First-Last-Invert-Play, retargetable — measure First and Last rects, apply an inverting transform so it looks unmoved, Play to identity; a re-toggle mid-flight RE-SEATS the spring target from the live value and velocity instead of reconstructing from rest (iOS interruptible-spring contract). glass-ui useLayerTransition already does pixel-space FLIP with velocity-continuity (AV.W9.2); useLiquidMorph promotes it from a dock-private closure to the shared substrate.

Motion framer-motion layout, layoutId and LayoutGroup, the JS prior-art for the matched-geometry seam — layout auto-animates render-driven size and position via FLIP; layoutId connects two elements rendered at different times so one morphs into the other; LayoutGroup synchronizes layout animations across siblings. Ergonomic target: useLiquidMorph of elRef is like layout, a morphId is like layoutId, a MorphGroup is like LayoutGroup.

interpolate-size allow-keywords with calc-size — native CSS animation to and from intrinsic sizes (auto, fit-content, min-content). - Composable tier: useLiquidMorph of elRef for an element owning its own reshape (dock root, a panel). One call; the substrate owns spring, FLIP, will-change, PRM and clip-aperture lifecycle.
- Group tier: wrap children in MorphGroup for coordinated and nested morphs (dock plus DockLayerGroup, a toolbar of glass controls that merge).

W01 (one spring to --dock-morph-t to every axis; retire the VT fork; useLayerTransition 479 to about 130 lines) becomes re-derive useLayerTransition AS a thin dock-flavored wrapper over useLiquidMorph. ANIMATION W05: useLiquidMorph standardizes on the ONE governed iOS-spring register (excise ease-apple-spring; the dock register pins to the published 0.32 0.7 spring-dock). REUSE — useLiquidMorph is about 70 percent assembly: keyframes.js SpringProgress (analytic ODE, retargetable, settle-aware), useSpring (Vue wrapper), useLayerTransition (FLIP plus velocity-continuity plus will-change plus clip-aperture lifecycle, promote to substrate), createStrictContext (typed DI), useViewTransition (route-morph seam), useSpecularTracking (W09 pointer-light seam). NET-NEW: the unifying API surface plus the MorphGroup orchestrator plus the axes-declaration that lets CSS calc off one scalar.
pitfalls: MULTIPLE MORPH AUTHORITIES equals desync (the cardinal AW scar). The dock had three-plus overlapping authorities (root CSS-class-flip transitions vs inner JS spring deferred a frame via nextTick to rAF to reflow, box leads content by about 16ms). useLiquidMorph MUST enforce ONE authority per concern: size equals spring, opacity equals class-driven CSS transition on a separate host, color equals discrete class swap.

VIEW TRANSITIONS IS THE WRONG PRIMITIVE FOR A LAYOUT MORPH. VT crossfades rasterized snapshots; for a continuous self-reshape it desyncs the uncaptured animating ancestor and, with duplicate names (fourier two co-mounted docks minting glass-dock-1), DROPS the morph snapshot plus reds about 13 e2e. STANDING will-change holds a compositor layer plus VRAM for an idle element. Promote will-change ONLY for the gesture duration; clear to auto on settle or transitionend AFTER the final paint (clearing early flashes the last frame). TWEENING AN INHERITED CUSTOM PROPERTY equals whole-subtree style recalc every frame (the inheritance bomb). --morph-t on the morphing element is fine, but never per-frame-tween an INHERITED color var (phase-color, shadow-color) across a subtree. ORPHAN-ABLE ASYNC LISTENERS race the morph driver. keepDockOpen was a ref-counted token across a window listener that raced the morph data-held writes. A morph-state input must be a SYNCHRONOUS reactive edge into the one state machine, with scope-disposed cleanup (onScopeDispose), no side-channel attribute write-race, no orphaned setTimeout.

OVER-GENERALIZING THE SUBSTRATE equals substrate-without-consumer (L invariant 8 and the overfitting-audit precept). useLiquidMorph must ship with at least 2 real consumers AT LANDING (the dock plus at least one glass primitive), not a speculative options surface no one uses. Each API knob needs a named consumer or it is overfit.

GLASS-ON-GLASS SAMPLING plus specular blowout. Glass cannot sample other glass (containers provide one shared sampling region); a moving specular at high alpha blows out white (AX.W09: pure-white at 0.55 alpha on the most-hovered surface, doubled by a second glass-highlight box-shadow). The morph facility composes with ONE specular source at SUBTLE rungs (rest about 0, hover about 0.22, active about 0.32, warm-cream not pure-white) and retires any second stacked highlight.

LIQUID GLASS IS FOR THE FUNCTIONAL OR NAVIGATION LAYER ONLY, never on content (lists, tables, media). Every element morphs (the directive) does NOT mean every element wears full liquid-glass material; the material plus heavy morph belong to the floating functional layer, content elements get at most a lightweight entrance or reshape (Apple HIG plus the clear-variant-needs-bold-foreground rule).

HEADLESS-GREEN OVER VISUALLY-BROKEN (the governing AX precept). A morph wave does NOT close on a numeric or token gate alone; it closes on a live Playwright plus frontend-design audit that it reads as one continuous iOS spring with no occlusion or blowout. Build the substrate against the W00 fail-CLOSED visual-runtime (pi) lane.
