notes.facet: "Every element morphs" as ONE idiom — making the morph facility GENERAL (button/card/dialog/dock/sheet all compose it), not per-component bespoke
sotaTechniques: GlassEffectContainer + glassEffectID identity-merge (Apple iOS-26 / WWDC25 sess.219) — the canonical generalization mechanism. A CONTAINER establishes a shared morph context; each child glass view declares a stable identity (`.glassEffectID(id, in: namespace)`) and a `spacing` threshold governs when neighbors visually FUSE into one blob. SwiftUI then computes the morph path between matched identities automatically — there is NO per-component morph code; an element opts in by (a) joining the container and (b) declaring an id. This is exactly the 'one idiom, every element composes it' shape glass-ui's facet wants: the web analogue is a single `.glass-material`/`useMorph` substrate + a `morph-id` (the `view-transition-name`/`glassEffectID` equivalent) per surface.

Single-scalar morph driver on ONE clock (analytic spring -> CSS custom property) — drive the whole morph from one normalized 0->1 scalar written once per frame to a `@property`-typed custom property on the root; express EVERY animated axis (inline-size, padding, radius, scale, bg/border color, child stagger) as pure `calc()`/interpolation off that one scalar. No per-axis `transition`, no per-engine fork. This is literally AX.W01's `--dock-morph-t` plan and the keyframes.js `SpringProgress` already in `useSpring`; the SOTA contribution is GENERALIZING it past the dock to a `useMorphScalar(target)` primitive every primitive (card/dialog/sheet) can mount.

Interruptible / re-targetable springs with velocity continuity (Family.co fluid-interfaces, jtrivedi/Wave, b3ll/Motion, Emil Kowalski) — a spring re-seats its target from the CURRENT (value, velocity) on interrupt rather than restarting from rest, so a re-toggle mid-morph redirects smoothly (CSS `transition` restarts from zero; springs don't). Parameterize by (response, damping) not duration. glass-ui's `useLayerTransition` already does the AV.W9.2 velocity-continuity re-seat on the FLIP path; the generalization is making interruptibility a property of the shared `useMorphScalar`, not dock-local.

Native same-document View Transitions, now Baseline (Oct 2025) — `view-transition-name` morphs an element's position/size/shape between two DOM states; `view-transition-name: match-element` AUTO-NAMES every matched element (no hand-minted ids), `view-transition-class` applies ONE shared curve to a whole family of morphing surfaces, nested `view-transition-group` restores clipping during the morph, and `:active-view-transition-type(<t>)` authors DIRECTION-specific curves (snappier collapse, softer expand). This is the browser-native `glassEffectID` analogue for cross-state/route morphs.

interpolate-size: allow-keywords + calc-size() — animate TO/FROM intrinsic sizes (`auto`, `fit-content`, `max-content`) which `transition` historically could not. Declared once on `:root` (it inherits), it lets a card/dialog/dock grow to content-size with a real eased morph instead of a JS measure-pin-tween dance. `calc-size(auto, size - 10px)` does arithmetic on the intrinsic size. Chromium-only (129+) -> progressive enhancement behind `@supports`, with the JS FLIP/spring as the fallback.

@starting-style + transition-behavior: allow-discrete + overlay — pure-CSS entry/exit morph for top-layer surfaces (popover, native `<dialog>`, and the `::backdrop`). The element interpolates FROM the `@starting-style` values on insert and animates `display`/`overlay` discretely on exit, so a dialog/sheet materializes-and-morphs with zero JS coordinator. glass-ui already ships this as `.glass-top-layer` in animations.css; SOTA move is making it the universal materialize path for every floating surface.

corner-shape: squircle (Chrome 139+) + @property-typed channels — the literal iOS-26 superellipse corner geometry that `backdrop-filter`/border/shadow all follow, so a radius morph reads as the Apple continuous-corner curve, not a circular arc. Pairing it with `@property` registration of the morph scalar + specular channels makes those custom properties actually INTERPOLATE (an unregistered custom property animates discretely). glass-ui ships both today (glass.css squircle block, typed `--specular-*`).

Unified material substrate (one selector group, every surface joins by membership) — Apple's rule 'glass is the navigation/overlay layer, never glass-on-glass' + the WWDC25 'rim defines the silhouette' light model. glass-ui's `.glass-material` group already does this: wash/quiet/resting/floating/overlay/card/dock-control all inherit the moving specular `::before`, the `--glass-edge-light` rim, and the pointer interaction-light in lockstep by being a comma-entry in ONE selector. Adding a surface to the material is one comma, not a new class — the structural template for the morph generalization.

Pointer-tracked specular / interaction light as a shared behavior — the iOS-26 'illuminate-from-within, flex-and-energize-with-light-on-touch' response, expressed as a `@property`-typed radial-gradient `::before` driven by `--mouse-x/--mouse-y` -> `--specular-*`, with hover/active lifting `--specular-intensity` in the SAME rungs the scale-press squish keys off. Already unified in glass.css; the SOTA framing is that 'material light' and 'spring squish' are the two halves of one Liquid-Glass behavior every interactive surface should compose.
notes.applicability: "see facet field"
pitfalls: VT is the WRONG primitive for a live in-place layout morph (AX.W01 root cause): View Transitions snapshot and crossfade RASTERIZED pixels, so an animating ancestor desyncs and two co-mounted docks minting the same `view-transition-name` DROP the morph snapshot (fourier's CanvasControlsDock+EditorControlsDock collision reds ~13 e2e). Use the live single-scalar spring for in-place box morphs; reserve VT for cross-state/cross-route ELEMENT morphs. Per-instance unique names (`useId()`) are mandatory.

Animating an INHERITED custom property is a whole-subtree style-recalc bomb — tweening `--phase-color`/`--shadow-color` per frame forces a recalc on every descendant each frame. Keep per-frame motion on `transform`/`opacity`/`width`/`height` (and the typed morph scalar); route color shifts through a DISCRETE class swap, never frame interpolation (glass-ui's `useLayerTransition` F5 convention).

An UNREGISTERED custom property animates DISCRETELY (jumps, no tween). The morph scalar and any percentage/length channel it feeds MUST be `@property`-registered with a `syntax`/`inherits`/`initial-value` or the morph snaps. Also: a registered `@property` var() nested inside `hsl()` alpha computes to 0 in Chromium (glass-ui hit this) — drive layer `opacity`, not per-stop alpha.

interpolate-size / calc-size() / corner-shape: squircle are Chromium-ONLY (129+/139+); Firefox + Safari have no support. They MUST be `@supports`-gated progressive enhancement with the JS spring/FLIP + `border-radius` round as the live fallback — never the sole path, or non-Chromium degrades to instant/wrong-shape with no error (silent clean-break breakage, the same class as deleting `--ease-apple-spring` and leaving consumers resolving empty).

Standing `will-change` on an idle morph surface pins a compositor layer + VRAM forever. Set `will-change:<dim>` ONLY for the gesture's duration (just before the spring drives, cleared to `auto` on settle/transitionend) — glass-ui's AV.W7 F3 discipline. A general morph primitive must own this lifecycle or every mounted surface leaks a layer.

Glass-on-glass is a discipline violation (Apple HIG + glass-ui AV.W15 D5): a `.glass-*` surface nested inside another stacks blur, doubles the rim, and collapses legibility. The generalized material must enforce the navigation/overlay-band-only rule — inside a glass panel, compose FLAT tiers, not a second plate. A morph that fuses two glass surfaces (the container-merge) must merge them into ONE plate, not paint two.

Reduced-motion + reduced-transparency are NON-NEGOTIABLE and SEPARATE: PRM must flatten the scale/scalar morph to a fade and shorten duration (the spring `respectReducedMotion` snap); reduced-transparency must drop blur/grain/specular to opaque. A WebGL/JS rAF morph driver must LIVE-monitor `prefers-reduced-motion` (a matchMedia change listener) — a CSS reset cannot reach a JS rAF loop (glass-ui's useWebGLCanvas owns this).

Build-time `linear()` spring token and runtime `SpringProgress` driver can DRIFT — the dock pins `{response:0.32, damping:0.7}` in BOTH the JS const and the regen PRESETS row; a retune touching only one desyncs the CSS-token curve from the JS-driven curve. A shared vocabulary needs a gate that renders the overshoot at runtime from the imported constant, not a hand-typed number.

Don't over-generalize into dead substrate (overfitting invariant): a morph primitive or `--spring-*` preset with <2 real consumers is substrate-without-consumer. Ship the generalized facility only where button/card/dialog/dock/sheet ACTUALLY compose it; gate the spring generator on consumer coverage (AX.W05 census).

notes.facet: The morph STATE MACHINE — idle/morphing/settled lifecycle, the data-morphing attribute, the set/clear seam
sotaTechniques: data-state lifecycle attribute as the CSS<->JS seam (Radix/reka-ui convention): the JS owns a small enumerable state (open|closed|delayed-open), writes it to a data-* attribute, and ALL declarative styling keys off the attribute selector — the attribute flips the instant state changes, before any animation logic runs. Applied to morph this is exactly glass-ui's `data-morphing` boolean, generalized to a 3-state enum.

Presence/suspend-unmount lifecycle (Radix Presence): the framework holds an element mounted through its EXIT animation by listening for animationend/transitionend on the correct element + the current animation, then clears state. This is the canonical 'don't clear until the final paint lands' settle-seam — exactly what `useLayerTransition` does with its onTransitionEnd + spring.settled clear, but Radix proves it as a reusable Presence primitive.

Single normalized progress scalar drives every axis (the analytic-spring-to-CSS-custom-property pattern): one spring solver writes a normalized 0->1 value to one CSS var per frame; every animated axis is a pure calc() read off it, so the whole composite moves on ONE clock. glass-ui already does this with `--dock-morph-progress` for the child stagger; W01 generalizes it to `--dock-morph-t` for the WHOLE box (size/padding/radius/scale/color/stagger).

Interruptible spring with velocity continuity (Emil Kowalski / iOS spring contract): springs retain velocity when retargeted mid-flight; a re-toggle re-seats the live solver's target from its current (value, velocity) instead of dispose+reconstruct-from-rest. CSS keyframes restart from zero and CANNOT do this. glass-ui's AV.W9.2 retarget seam (springEl===el && !spring.settled -> set target) is exactly this — the genuinely load-bearing piece of iOS feel to PRESERVE through any rewrite.

Apple Liquid Glass morph lifecycle vocabulary (WWDC25 'Meet Liquid Glass'): elements MATERIALIZE in/out by modulating light-bending/lensing rather than fading; they FLEX (gel-like, moves in tandem with interaction); ENERGIZE (illuminate from within under the fingertip, glow spreads to nearby glass); LIFT (rise into glass on touch, resting state stays quiet). This is Apple's named state taxonomy: rest(quiet) -> engaged(lift/energize) -> morphing(flex/materialize) -> settled. It maps cleanly onto an idle|engaged|morphing|settled enum.

glassEffectID + GlassEffectContainer shared-namespace morph (SwiftUI iOS 26): each glass element carries a unique ID in a shared @Namespace; a state change INSIDE withAnimation morphs related IDs into one another (merge/separate), and a container `spacing` threshold controls when nearby shapes blend. This is the multi-element morph-grouping primitive — the SwiftUI analogue of View-Transitions named elements; the morph is ONLY armed inside an animation context (state-change-alone does not morph).

View Transitions API for same-document state morphs (Baseline-newly-available Oct 2025 w/ Firefox 144): startViewTransition(cb) snapshots old/new, the browser tweens named elements; `types` + :active-view-transition-type author directional curves; `view-transition-class` shares styling; document.activeViewTransition + .skipTransition() give interruptibility; element.startViewTransition() (scoped) isolates a sub-tree. CRITICAL: VT crossfades RASTER snapshots — correct for opacity/transform shared-element morphs, WRONG for a layout/size morph (the taffy-stretch + box-leads-content desync glass-ui W01 retires).

CSS-native lifecycle primitives for the morph endpoints — @starting-style (entry-style for a transition's from-state), transition-behavior: allow-discrete (animate display/visibility across the discrete boundary), interpolate-size: allow-keywords + calc-size() (animate to/from height:auto/fit-content). These let the IDLE->MORPHING->SETTLED transition run with NO JS measure/pin dance for the simple cases; glass-ui already ships @starting-style top-layer grammar + scroll-driven recipes (AQ.W5).

Family.co fluid-interface morph taxonomy (Benji Taylor): trays morph into full screens, buttons glide across trays, buttons morph into trays and back; the app has 'unbreakable physical rules', motion is 'moving through water', and morphs are LEGIBLE (directional cues, shared-letter text morph Continue->Confirm, persistent components move rather than disappear/reappear). The governing principle: every morph serves wayfinding (A->B), and a persistent element must stay consistent across the morph, never duplicate.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD — a unified morph state machine for every glass element, grounded in what glass-ui already has. (1) PROMOTE `data-morphing` from a boolean to a 3-state lifecycle attribute `data-morph-state=idle|morphing|settled` (mirrors Apple rest->flex/materialize->settled and the Radix data-state convention). The current set/clear seam in useLayerTransition.ts (setMorphing/clearMorphing on the .glass-dock root via morphRoot(el)?.setAttribute) becomes setMorphState(el,'morphing') at gesture START and setMorphState(el,'settled') on spring.settled/transitionend, with a rAF-deferred return to 'idle' so a 'settled->idle' cleanup pulse can fire (e.g. clear will-change, lift the clip). This gives CSS three distinct hooks instead of one presence/absence — the clip-reveal aperture, the will-change promotion, and the at-rest overflow:visible all key off the enum rather than :not([data-morphing]). (2) EXTRACT the set/clear seam into a tiny reusable composable — `useMorphState(rootRef)` returning { state, begin(), settle() } that owns the data-attribute write + the will-change/clip/stagger arm-disarm lifecycle as ONE established seam (Apple's glassEffectID and Radix Presence both prove the morph-lifecycle belongs in a shared primitive, not re-hand-rolled per consumer). This is the natural home for W01's --dock-morph-t scalar write and the W02 single-orchestrator DI — the orchestrator IS the useMorphState instance, provided through dockMorphContext. Every glass primitive (Card surface=glass on hover-lift, GlassDock collapse, a future tray-morph) drives the SAME composable so the whole library breathes on one state machine. (3) PRESERVE the velocity-continuity retarget (AV.W9.2) as the single non-negotiable iOS-feel piece through the W01 479->130 rewrite — it is the interruptibility Emil/Family demand and the one thing CSS transitions/VT cannot give. (4) KEEP the live SpringProgress as the universal driver and RETIRE the VT collapse fork (W01) — VT raster-snapshots are the wrong primitive for the box layout morph (the taffy/box-leads-content hazard the 2025 VT pitfall corpus confirms); but PRESERVE the per-instance view-transition-name route-morph seam for the consumer's PAGE morph (the separable concern W01 ratifies). (5) For NEW capability: a glassEffectID-style multi-element morph-grouping (the SwiftUI GlassEffectContainer analogue) is the door to 'every UI element morphs' — a container that registers participating glass shapes and drives them off one shared --morph-t with a spacing/threshold blend, so trays-morphing-into-buttons (Family) becomes a library primitive rather than a per-consumer hand-roll. The idle/morphing/settled enum is the substrate that makes this composable across primitives.
pitfalls: View Transitions raster-snapshot hazard: VT screenshots old+new states as FLAT rasters and stretches between them — a 150x150 morphing to 600x300 becomes 'taffy'; animating width/height/top/left during a VT forces layout recalc and can register as CLS. This is precisely why glass-ui's box LAYOUT morph must NOT ride VT (W01 retires the collapse fork); VT is only correct for opacity/transform shared-element/route morphs. Do not regress the layout morph onto VT.

The box-leads-content desync (multi-clock smell): glass-ui's HEAD defect is that the root box CSS-transitions on one clock while the inner content springs on another (the nextTick->rAF->void offsetWidth deferral pushes content ~16ms behind). ANY morph state machine that writes the lifecycle attribute on a different element/frame than it drives the geometry re-introduces this. The fix is one scalar, one element, one frame-origin — the data-morph-state write and the --morph-t write must be co-temporal.

Standing will-change / compositor-layer leak: a permanent will-change holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an idle surface. The morph state machine MUST promote will-change ONLY for the morphing state and clear it on settle (glass-ui's AV.W7 F3 on-demand lifecycle) — clearing on settle AFTER the final paint, never before (racing the last frame flashes).

The inheritance bomb: animating an INHERITED custom property (--phase-color, --shadow-color, or a --morph-t set high in the tree) forces a whole-subtree style recalc EVERY frame. Keep the per-frame scalar local to the morphing element; route color/phase shifts through a DISCRETE class/state swap at the lifecycle boundary, never a per-frame interpolation of an inherited var (glass-ui's AV.W7 F5 convention).

interpolate-size/calc-size are NOT Baseline (Chrome/Edge 129+ only; no Firefox/Safari as of 2025): a morph that relies on animating to height:auto via interpolate-size needs a JS measure-to-pixels fallback. Do not ship a CSS-only intrinsic-size morph as the sole path — the spring-in-pixel-space driver stays the universal arm.

Orphaned-timer / stale-settle race: a fixed-ms setTimeout cleanup that outlives an interrupted morph clears state mid-next-morph. The lifecycle must be progress-keyed (settle fires on spring.settled, not a timer) with the setTimeout ONLY as a missed-settle safety, transitionId-guarded — exactly glass-ui's current guard pattern; preserve it.

Over-animation / ambient-motion fatigue (NN/g + Apple HIG): Liquid Glass elements should stay 'visually quiet' at rest and come to life ONLY on interaction/intent — never ambient idle motion. The idle state must be genuinely static (the dock README already encodes this). A morph state machine that idles in a low-amplitude breathing loop violates the rest-quiet contract and the reduced-motion floor.

prefers-reduced-motion must collapse the morph to a synchronous state swap (no spring, no stagger, no rAF). The state machine needs an explicit PRM fast-path that goes idle->settled in one tick (glass-ui has this in both the FLIP gate and SpringProgress respectReducedMotion); a CSS-only PRM reset cannot reach a JS rAF driver, so the JS gate is load-bearing.

Same-author gate false-GREEN + un-measurable morph: keyframes device-proved the dock morph is NOT reliably live-measurable via getBoundingClientRect polling (the spring clock has no handle; gates collapse behind delays). A morph-lifecycle gate must drive the morph deterministically (test-flag/PRM, real page.hover) or expose the spring as a test seam + parse the token peak — not a naive rAF box poll (the W00/W01 design).

notes.facet: Morph + the dock LAYERING system — DockLayerGroup/DockLayer, the FLIP, the single-scalar driver, the clip-reveal aperture
sotaTechniques: SINGLE-SCALAR ANALYTIC-SPRING DRIVER (the iOS-26 core) — one normalized progress scalar (0->1) from ONE physics solver is written once per frame to a CSS custom property on the morphing root, and EVERY animated axis (width/inline-size, padding, border-radius, scale, bg/border color, child-stagger onset) is a pure calc()/interpolation read off that one scalar; this is the only way the whole box and its contents provably move on one clock. SwiftUI's `withAnimation(.spring/.bouncy)` is exactly this: one analytic spring drives all matchedGeometry/glassEffectID axes simultaneously. glass-ui already proves the seed with `--dock-morph-progress` for the child stagger — generalize it to `--dock-morph-t` for the whole box.

iOS-26 GlassEffectContainer + glassEffectID MORPH MODEL — Apple groups multiple glass shapes into a shared sampling region (`GlassEffectContainer`); matching `glassEffectID`s within one `@Namespace` make shapes PHYSICALLY MORPH (interpolate geometry + retain the translucent material) into one another as conditional visibility changes, with a `spacing` parameter as the merge-distance threshold — a layout-geometry morph, NOT a cross-fade. The web analogue of glassEffectID is a single shared driver + a named element seam; the merge-distance is the dock's clip aperture deciding when adjacent children are 'revealed' together.

SwiftUI 2-parameter spring (response, dampingFraction) + perceptualDuration — the canonical iOS spring API is `(response: time-to-target, dampingFraction: overshoot decay)`, unit mass, ω0=2π/response, ζ=dampingFraction; the CORRECT bounce->physics conversion is stiffness=(2π/perceptualDuration)^2, damping=((1-bounce)*4π)/perceptualDuration. This maps 1:1 onto keyframes.js `SpringProgress({response, dampingFraction})` — glass-ui's `(0.32, 0.7)` dock register is a deliberately tighter, less-bouncy retune of SwiftUI's default `(0.55, 0.825)`.

INTERRUPTIBLE / VELOCITY-CONTINUOUS SPRING (Emil Kowalski; Family.co) — springs preserve velocity across a re-target while CSS keyframes restart from zero, so a re-toggle mid-flight must RE-SEAT the live solver's `target` from its current (value, velocity) rather than dispose+reconstruct-from-rest; this is the load-bearing iOS 'feel' for gesture-cancellable UI. keyframes.js `set target` already re-seats the closed-form from live (value, velocity) (keyframes.d.ts:805) — glass-ui's AV.W9.2 retarget path is correct; W01 makes it universal (today FLIP-only).

linear() AS THE DECLARATIVE SPRING CHANNEL (dual-channel sampling) — `linear()` easing recreates an arbitrary spring/bounce curve as a stop-set, baseline across all modern browsers since 2024; sampling the SAME analytic ODE into both a `SpringProgress` JS clock and a `--spring-dock` `linear()` token means the imperative driver and the declarative CSS transition are bit-identical. glass-ui already does this (the `regen-spring-tokens.mjs` mirror + the `--spring-dock` token). This is how non-morph decorative dock transitions stay on-curve without a JS frame loop.

CLIP-REVEAL APERTURE (content-stable, box-as-window) — lay content out ONCE at natural size, then grow/shrink only the BOX with `overflow:clip` on the morph axis so the box itself is the reveal window; nothing reflows mid-morph, no per-child layout animation, GPU-cheap. This is the web idiom that matches iOS where content is stable and the container reveals it. glass-ui's AW.W2 `data-morphing`-gated single-axis `overflow-x/y: clip` is exactly this and the charter (W01.5) keeps it as the SOLE reveal model.

SPRING-KEYED PROGRESSIVE STAGGER (choreography off the physical clock) — instead of fixed `setTimeout`/`nth-child` delay ladders, key each child's opacity/transform onset to a per-child THRESHOLD against the single morph scalar, so a fast flick and a slow hover-open both choreograph correctly and an interrupted morph carries its cascade with it (no orphaned timers). glass-ui's AW.W3 `--dock-morph-progress` per-child onset is SOTA-correct; W02 replaces the hand-typed 0.08/0.16/0.24 nth-child ladder with one `--dock-stagger-step` token.

View Transitions = WRONG PRIMITIVE for a continuous layout morph (the 2025 consensus) — Chrome's own 2025 VT guidance states VT captures RASTERIZED SNAPSHOTS, 'limiting their effectiveness for continuous morphing or dynamic resizing animations'; VT cross-fades pixels of old vs new, and an uncaptured animating ancestor desyncs. VT IS right for discrete shared-element ROUTE/PAGE morphs (named element across two states). This is the exact mechanism behind W01's retire-the-VT-collapse-fork while PRESERVING the route-morph `view-transition-name` seam — the two are separable concerns.

View Transition TYPES + :active-view-transition-type (directional asymmetry) — `startViewTransition({update, types})` (Chrome 140+) tags a transition so `:active-view-transition-type(forward|back)` CSS authors DIRECTION-specific curves (snappier exit, softer entry-overshoot — the iOS asymmetry); feature-detected, degrades to one symmetric curve. glass-ui already wires this (`directionTypes` -> layer-forward/layer-back, dock-expand/dock-collapse) — the asymmetry concept SURVIVES the VT-collapse-fork retirement by moving onto the single-scalar driver (two spring configs keyed on direction).

NESTED view-transition-group + view-transition-class + match-element — 2025 VT adds nested groups (restores clipping during a transition), `view-transition-class` to style a snapshot COLLECTION with one rule, and `view-transition-name: match-element` for browser-auto-generated identities; child pseudos now inherit animation longhands from the parent group (synchronized cross-fades). Relevant ONLY to the preserved route-morph seam — the dock's OWN collapse no longer uses any of it.

interpolate-size / calc-size() — DELIBERATELY REJECTED for the dock morph — `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` + `calc-size(auto, ...)` let CSS transition to/from intrinsic keywords (height:auto), Chromium-only (Chrome 129+, no Safari/Firefox as of 2025). glass-ui TRIED this (AV.W9.0) and RETIRED it — it second-drove width on Chrome and froze the dock. The lesson: a Chromium-only sizing channel CANNOT co-drive a box the spring already owns; one driver only. Keep this as the cautionary boundary, not an adoption target.

@starting-style + transition-behavior:allow-discrete + overlay (entry/exit, top-layer) — the Baseline (FF129+) recipe for animating an element in from `display:none`/into the top-layer: `@starting-style` seeds the from-state, `allow-discrete` flips `display`/`overlay` at the right frame so the element stays painted through exit. Not the dock-collapse mechanism (the dock stays mounted), but the canonical primitive for the dock's POPOVER/dropdown CHILDREN entry-exit and any glass surface that mounts/unmounts; glass-ui already has the `.glass-top-layer` `@starting-style` grammar (AQ.W5).

ONE ORCHESTRATOR PER MORPH (DI-folded nested groups) — a nested layout-morph container must DEFER to the parent's single driver via provide/inject, never spin up a second spring; two independent springs writing inline-size onto parent+child with zero coordination double-animate the same pixels. This is W02's fold of the inner DockLayerGroup pair onto the outer GlassDock driver — the web analogue of nesting inside ONE `GlassEffectContainer` rather than two.

TRANSFORM/OPACITY-FIRST + on-demand will-change + inheritance-bomb guard (perf discipline) — animate only transform/opacity/clip on the compositor; NEVER tween an INHERITED custom property per-frame (forces a whole-subtree style recalc — the 'inheritance bomb'); promote `will-change` ONLY for the gesture duration (a standing hint holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an idle surface). glass-ui's F3/F5 folds already encode this; the single-scalar caveat is that `--dock-morph-t` is set on the ROOT and read by descendants via calc — that read is cheap, but any per-frame COLOR interpolation must route through a discrete class swap, not an inherited-var tween.

ANCHOR POSITIONING (position-area / position-try-fallbacks) — Baseline 2026 (Chrome 125+, FF145+, Safari 26): tether an element to an anchor with automatic fallback positioning during layout (no JS/rAF/ResizeObserver), and anchored container queries (Chrome 143) match on which fallback is active. Adjacent to the morph facility — the right primitive for dock-attached popovers/tooltips and for keeping a morphing dock anchored to a viewport edge without JS measurement.
notes.applicability: "DIRECT, HIGH-FIT — this facet is the exact subject of AX charter waves W01-W06, and the SOTA validates the charter's thesis end-to-end. THE PATH FORWARD (unified morph facility): (1) W01 — collapse the dock collapse<->expand onto ONE `SpringProgress` whose normalized scalar is written once per frame to `--dock-morph-t` on the `.glass-dock` root; re-express width/padding/border-radius/scale/bg/border + child-stagger as pure calc() reads off it; this is iOS-26's single-spring-drives-all-axes model expressed in CSS custom properties. The current `useLayerTransition.ts` (479 lines, 3 forked codepaths: NATIVE_VT / PRM-fast-path / FLIP) re-derives to ~130 lines = ONE live ODE on every engine, with the velocity-continuity retarget (the one genuine iOS-value piece) kept. (2) RETIRE the VT-for-COLLAPSE fork (lines 108, 262-288) — Chrome's own 2025 guidance is the citation: VT rasterizes snapshots and is the wrong primitive for a continuous resize morph, and the source of the box-leads-content desync. PRESERVE the per-instance `glass-dock-${useId()}` route-morph `view-transition-name` seam (separable concern — the consumer's PAGE/route geometry-morph). (3) Keep the AW.W2 clip-reveal aperture as the sole reveal model (content laid out once, box-as-window) and the AW.W3 spring-keyed child stagger (onset keyed to the scalar threshold, not a timer). (4) W02 — fold the nested DockLayerGroup orchestrator onto the outer driver via DI (one `GlassEffectContainer`, not two springs). (5) GENERALIZE beyond the dock: the `--dock-morph-t` pattern is the template for a library-wide morph facility — any glass primitive that resizes/reshapes (card<->expanded, drawer detents, glass-panel grow) drives a single `--morph-t` scalar from one `SpringProgress`, reads every axis off it via calc, and uses single-axis overflow:clip as the reveal aperture. The dual-channel substrate (SpringProgress JS clock + `--spring-dock` linear() token sampled from the SAME ODE) is already in place, so cheap declarative-only morphs (no JS frame loop) get the identical curve. This is glass-ui's web expression of 'the iOS-26 Liquid-Glass morphing facility for EVERY UI element.'"
pitfalls: VIEW TRANSITIONS RASTERIZE — do not reach for VT to do a continuous layout/resize morph. VT cross-fades pixel snapshots of old vs new; an uncaptured animating ancestor desyncs, and the 'box shrinks first, content lags a frame' defect is partly this. VT is correct ONLY for discrete shared-element route/page morphs. (Chrome 2025 VT guidance states this explicitly.)

TWO CLOCKS = DOUBLE ANIMATION — the HEAD defect: the root box morphs on a CSS transition while the inner width morphs on a JS spring deferred a frame behind via nextTick->rAF->reflow, so the box leads content by ~16ms. Any second driver (a stray root CSS `transition` on a morph property, a second `useLayerTransition` in a nested group, or a Chromium calc-size() arm) re-introduces the desync. The single-scalar rule is absolute: exactly ONE authority per morph.

interpolate-size/calc-size() CANNOT co-drive a box the spring owns — it is Chromium-only AND, when layered on top of the JS spring (as glass-ui tried in AV.W9.0), it second-drives width and FREEZES the dock. Treat it as a rejected boundary, not an enhancement.

INHERITANCE BOMB — tweening an inherited custom property (e.g. `--phase-color`, `--shadow-color`) per frame forces a whole-subtree style recalc every frame. `--dock-morph-t` on the root read via descendant calc() is cheap; but any per-frame COLOR shift must go through a DISCRETE class swap, never an interpolated inherited var.

STANDING will-change holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an IDLE dock — promote `will-change:<dim>` only for the gesture duration, clear to auto on settle/transitionend AFTER the final paint (so it never races the spring's last frame and flashes). A permanent hint on `[data-morphing]` left in CSS is the anti-pattern.

DUPLICATE view-transition-name DROPS THE SNAPSHOT — the fourier two-dock co-mount (CanvasControlsDock + EditorControlsDock both minting `glass-dock-1`) silently drops the route-morph and reds ~13 e2e specs. The mint source MUST be app-unique (`useId()`); `proof:vt-names` polices it. Preserve this seam through the VT-collapse-fork retirement.

SINGLE-AXIS overflow:clip degrades to `hidden` on the OTHER axis (MDN caveat) — `overflow-x:clip; overflow-y:visible` is correct, but setting clip on one axis forces the visual-overflow other axis to behave as if `hidden` unless explicitly `visible`. glass-ui handles this; a naive copy that omits the explicit `visible` will clip grown content / focus rings at rest.

LIFTING THE CLIP AT FRAME 0 KILLS THE APERTURE — binding `overflow:visible` to `.expanded` (synchronous with the open intent) lifts the clip before the morph runs, leaving no window to reveal through. The clip must be keyed to `data-morphing` (held for the WHOLE gesture, lifted only on settle), not to the expanded class.

MORPH NOT LIVE-MEASURABLE BY getBoundingClientRect ALONE — keyframes proved 181 rAF rect samples over 1.5s captured NO morph (VT runs on invisible `::view-transition-*` snapshots; the FLIP SpringProgress clock is internal with no public handle). The live gate MUST deterministically drive the readable arm (force the FLIP/spring path via test-flag/PRM, real page.hover, lowered collapse-delay) and sample root-box geometry vs a representative child on ONE rAF timeline — do not rely on naive live rect timing.

PRM (prefers-reduced-motion) needs an explicit synchronous fast-path — under reduce, run a single synchronous state swap (no measure/pin/animate/rAF/spring, no child stagger arming). keyframes.js `respectReducedMotion` handles the solver, but the orchestrator must gate the stagger + clip-aperture arming too, or a reduced-motion user gets a frozen half-morph.

ANIMATING width/height IS a layout property (not compositor-only) — Emil/web.dev say transform/opacity only for 60fps. The dock morph animates the actual box `width`/`height` (a layout morph is intrinsically not transform-only). This is acceptable BECAUSE the content is laid out once and clipped (the clip-reveal aperture means the morph is paint-bounded, not reflow-per-frame), but it caps the perf headroom — keep the morphing subtree small and never nest two width-animating boxes.

notes.facet: Morph reusability + the cost budget — the perf ceiling for ubiquitous morphing, when NOT to morph, the taste of restraint
sotaTechniques: GlassEffectContainer one-sampling-pass batching (Apple WWDC25): Apple groups multiple glass shapes into a single container so the whole group is sampled+lit+blurred in ONE render pass instead of N independent passes — 'glass cannot sample glass', so batching is both a correctness AND a cost mechanism. The container's `spacing` parameter sets the morph-merge threshold (elements within it blend into one shape). This is the canonical answer to 'what is the perf ceiling for ubiquitous glass': you do not pay per-element; you pay per-CONTAINER.

The web-animation performance tier list (Motion.dev, 2025): S-tier = compositor-only (`transform`, `opacity`, `filter`, `clip-path`) run off the main thread and survive jank; C-tier = paint-triggering (`background-color`, `color`, `border-radius`, `box-shadow`) force a layer redraw, cost scales with layer size; D-tier = layout-triggering (`width`, `height`, `margin`, `padding`, `display`) recalc geometry every frame and 'can be a massive hit to your frame budget'; F-tier = read/write layout thrashing. The morph budget is the inversion of this list: express every morphable axis as transform/opacity/clip-path, never as width/padding/border-radius tweened per frame.

The 16.67ms frame budget decomposition (web.dev/Chrome): per 60fps frame = JS 3ms + style 4ms + layout 4ms + paint 4ms + composite 1.67ms. At 120fps the whole budget is ~8ms. A morph that touches layout+paint spends ~12ms before it has rendered anything; a transform/opacity morph spends ~1.67ms. This is the literal cost ceiling that decides how many elements can morph at once.

Layer-count / will-change discipline (MDN + Motion + Rauno): `will-change` and forced GPU promotion create a compositor layer per element; 'creating too many layers or layers that are too big can blow out GPU memory budgets, particularly on mobile.' SOTA practice (Motion, Rauno): toggle `will-change` ONLY for the gesture's live duration, clear to `auto` on settle — never a standing hint. A permanent or sprayed `will-change` holds VRAM for idle elements and inverts the win.

Inherited-CSS-custom-property recalc bomb (Motion tier list, measured): mutating a GLOBAL/inherited CSS variable forces a style recalc across the whole subtree that reads it — a cited production case hit 8ms/frame over 1300 elements. Mitigation: write the morph scalar LOCALLY (on the morphing root, not :root), and register interaction channels with `@property … { inherits: false }` so the var does not cascade-invalidate descendants. This is the cost-correct way to drive 'one scalar → every axis'.

View Transitions cost model (Chrome/CSS-Tricks 2025): VT snapshots old+new state as FLAT RASTER bitmaps and morphs between them — each `view-transition-name` mints an additional snapshot layer; cross-document VT adds ~70ms to LCP on repeat mobile views and inflates INP via snapshot/composite work; a stretched bitmap (150×150 → 600×300) scales poorly because it is a raster, not a live layout. The SOTA rule: 'only name elements that truly benefit from individual animation' — VT is the wrong primitive for a continuous LAYOUT morph (which is exactly what a collapsing dock is).

Spring-as-shared-clock, interruptible-by-construction (Family/Benji Taylor, iOS): one analytic spring drives the morph; an interrupted gesture RE-TARGETS the live spring from its current (value, velocity) instead of restarting from rest, so the motion is continuous through interruption. One spring instance per morph (reused across re-toggles) is both the iOS feel AND the cost win — no second clock, no second timeline competing for the same pixels.

Restraint as a first-class rule — 'when NOT to animate' (Emil Kowalski + Rauno + Benji): Every animation must answer 'why does this animate?' (spatial consistency / state / feedback / preventing jarring change). If the answer is 'it looks cool' and the user sees it OFTEN, do NOT animate. Concretely: never animate keyboard-initiated or high-frequency actions (Emil), skip motion on right-click menus / list add-remove / trivial-button hover (Rauno), keep interaction animations ≤200ms (Rauno), and disable transitions during theme switches (Rauno). Benji: persistent components must NOT duplicate themselves during a transition; for frequent features 'the value of adding further delight gradually diminishes.'

Content-flat / glass-for-chrome-only (Apple HIG, WWDC25): Liquid Glass is for navigation and CONTROLS (tab bars, sidebars, docks, toolbars, notifications) — 'content views stay flat.' Glass over busy imagery must be minimal. This is the taxonomy that bounds the cost: the expensive material (backdrop-filter sampling + specular + morph) lives on the small, finite chrome layer, NOT sprayed across the content plane.

Offscreen / hidden / reduced-motion park (Rauno + Apple + web.dev): looping or continuous animations pause when not visible to offload CPU/GPU; `prefers-reduced-motion` and Apple's system Reduce Motion drop intensity and disable elastic/spring properties automatically. SOTA continuous-effect substrates (and glass-ui's own `useWebGLCanvas`) park the rAF loop on content-visibility/intersection/tab-hidden and paint one static frame under reduce. A morph facility must inherit the same park machinery — a morph that runs offscreen is pure waste.
notes.applicability: "OUR DOCK (W01/W02): AX.W01's single-scalar one-clock redesign is the textbook application of the spring-as-shared-clock + local-scalar principles — one analytic SpringProgress writes `--dock-morph-t` once per frame to the `.glass-dock` root, every axis is a `calc()` read off it. pitfalls: Tweening layout properties per frame (width/inline-size, padding, height) is D-tier — recalcs geometry every frame and 'can be a massive hit to your frame budget.' The W01 plan re-expresses padding + inline-size as calc() off `--dock-morph-t`; this is correct for ONE-clock coherence but each of those reads still drives a layout pass per frame. Audit which axes can be transform/clip-path (S-tier) instead. A dock morphing width+padding+border-radius+background+border-color simultaneously per frame is ~4 properties spanning layout+paint — the most expensive corner of the budget.

border-radius, background-color, border-color, box-shadow are C-tier paint-triggers; the W01 morph drives all of them off the scalar. Paint cost scales with layer size — fine for a small dock pill, but if the same morph facility is sprayed onto large surfaces (a full-width sheet, a content card) the paint-per-frame cost multiplies. The morph facility must NOT let a consumer animate background/box-shadow on a large layer without flagging the cost.

Animating an inherited CSS custom property forces a whole-subtree style recalc every frame — measured at 8ms/frame over 1300 elements. The dock already guards this (AV.W7 F5: never tween `--phase-color`/`--shadow-color`; route color shifts through a discrete class swap), but a NAIVE unified morph facility that writes its scalar to :root or an inherited var would re-introduce the bomb library-wide. The scalar MUST be local + `@property inherits:false`.

will-change sprayed or left standing holds a compositor layer + VRAM per element and 'can blow out GPU memory budgets, particularly on mobile.' A ubiquitous morph facility is the highest-risk place to get this wrong — every morph-capable element a standing hint = layer explosion. Toggle for the gesture window only, clear on settle (the dock already does this; the facility must enforce it for every consumer).

View Transitions is the WRONG primitive for a continuous layout morph: it rasterizes old+new to flat bitmaps (poor quality on non-uniform resize), mints a snapshot layer per `view-transition-name`, adds ~70ms LCP on repeat mobile + inflates INP, and double-clocks against a live CSS/spring morph. Reaching for VT to 'morph the dock' is the desync the whole AX.W01 wave exists to fix. Use VT only for discrete state/route morphs that benefit from individual naming.

Two morph clocks on the same pixels (the W02 born-RED: outer collapse spring + inner pane spring both writing inline size with zero coordination) doubles the cost AND desyncs. This is the GlassEffectContainer anti-pattern inverted — N independent samplers/springs instead of one batched group. The same hazard recurs anywhere a nested morphable composes inside a morphing parent.

Over-morphing as a taste failure: morphing high-frequency or keyboard-initiated interactions makes them feel slow and 'disconnected from the user's actions' (Emil); duplicating a persistent component during a transition is a known fluid-interface mistake (Benji); animating a right-click menu / list add-remove / trivial hover is gratuitous (Rauno). A facility that makes morphing ubiquitous and frictionless makes THIS the dominant risk — the easier it is to morph, the more it will be over-applied. Restraint must be built into the facility (a required 'purpose', sensible no-op defaults for frequent actions), not left to consumer discipline.

backdrop-filter promotes elements to layers and large blur values cause perf issues (Rauno); 12 backdrop-filter sites in glass.css + a moving specular + a per-frame morph stacked on the SAME glass surface is three independent GPU costs co-located. Apple's answer is the one-sampling-pass container; the web has no automatic equivalent, so glass + specular + morph on one surface must be budgeted deliberately, not assumed free.

Forgetting the offscreen/reduced-motion park: a morph or specular that keeps a spring/rAF alive while the dock is scrolled away or the tab is hidden is pure waste, and elastic/spring motion under Reduce Motion is an accessibility violation Apple disables automatically. Easy to omit when morphing is everywhere; the facility must inherit the park machinery the WebGL substrate already has.

Driving the morph through JS per-frame style writes when a pure-CSS interpolation (one transition + interpolate-size / @property registered custom props) would suffice adds main-thread JS cost (3ms slice) the compositor path avoids. Reach for the analytic spring only where interruptibility/velocity-continuity is genuinely needed (the dock); a non-interruptible decorative morph can ride a CSS transition with zero JS clock.

sotaTechniques: Apple Liquid Glass material model (WWDC25 HIG): glass is a SINGLE adaptive 'material' that lenses (bends + concentrates light at edges, not just gaussian blur), carries real-time specular highlights that react to motion, casts adaptive shadows (denser over text, lighter over white), and 'materializes' by modulating light-bending on entry. Two variants — `.regular` (default, adaptive to any background) and `.clear` (high-transparency, media-only, REQUIRES a dimming layer for legibility) — plus `.identity` (toggle glass off with no layout shift).

SwiftUI glass-morph API surface (the canonical iOS-26 morph facility to mirror): `glassEffect(_:in:)` applies the material in a shape; `GlassEffectContainer(spacing:)` groups multiple glass shapes into ONE shared sampling region so they blend/merge and morph together (glass can't sample other glass — the container is the shared backdrop); `glassEffectID(_:in:namespace)` is matched-geometry morphing (one glass blob fluidly splits/merges into another across a state change — the shared-element morph); `glassEffectUnion` welds adjacent shapes into one capsule; `.interactive()` bundles press-scale + bounce + shimmer + touch-illumination-radiating-to-neighbours into one modifier.

Concentricity (HIG geometric law): nested rounded shapes must share a common center so inner corner-radius = outer-radius − gap; SwiftUI exposes `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: .containerConcentric)`. Eliminates harsh edge collisions and is the geometric backbone of the 'controls nest perfectly into window corners' look.

No-glass-on-glass + navigation-layer-only discipline (HIG): glass is reserved for the navigation/overlay band (tab bars, toolbars, floating chrome, sheets over content) — never the content layer (lists/tables/media) and never nested glass-in-glass (the inner surface reads as a flat tier). This is both an aesthetic and a GPU-cost rule.

Browser liquid-glass refraction recipe (kube.io / LogRocket / Shu Ding 2025): a 3-primitive SVG filter graph — `feImage` carries a pre-baked displacement map computed from a squircle surface profile y=⁴√(1−(1−x)⁴) via Snell's law (n=1.5), R-channel=x-shift / G-channel=y-shift / 128=neutral; `feDisplacementMap` warps the backdrop by it (`scale`=max-px); a soft `feImage` specular highlight `feBlend mode='screen'` over the top. Mounted via `backdrop-filter: url(#filter)` (Chromium-only, non-standard) behind `@supports`. Chromatic aberration = three displacement passes at slightly different scales, isolated per-channel with `feColorMatrix`, screen-blended.

Spring physics as the motion substrate (Emil Kowalski / Family / iOS): use analytic damped-harmonic springs (response + dampingFraction ζ) NOT fixed-duration beziers, because springs preserve VELOCITY across interruption — a re-target mid-flight continues from the live (position, velocity) instead of snapping from rest. iOS-feel presets: ζ≈0.7 for a slight playful overshoot (~+4.6%), ζ≈0.86 for a smooth no-ring settle, ζ=1 critically damped. UI motion stays under ~300ms; keyboard-initiated actions skip animation entirely.

Transform/opacity-only + compositor-hint hygiene (Emil/Chrome): animate only `transform` + `opacity` (and width/height through a single driver) to stay on the compositor at 60fps; never animate padding/margin (layout) or an INHERITED custom property (whole-subtree style recalc — the 'inheritance bomb'); promote `will-change` ONLY for the gesture duration, never standing (a permanent hint holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an idle surface).

View Transitions API for state/layout morphs (web platform, same-doc Baseline Oct-2025; cross-doc Chrome 126+/Safari 18.2+): `document.startViewTransition(cb)` snapshots old→new and tweens `view-transition-name`-tagged elements with zero getBoundingClientRect; Level-2 adds the `types` overload for direction-specific curves (`:active-view-transition-type()`). Caveat: VT crossfades RASTERIZED pixels — correct for a shared-element/route morph, WRONG for a continuous layout-size morph of an animating-ancestor box (the desync the AX W01 wave excises).

Modern CSS keyword-morph primitives (Baseline 2024-2025): `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` + `calc-size()` animate height/width to/from `auto`/`fit-content`/`max-content` (the height:0→auto accordion long impossible in CSS); `@starting-style` + `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` give entry/exit transitions on `display:none`↔top-layer popovers; CSS anchor positioning (`anchor()`/`position-area`, cross-browser early-2026) tethers floating chrome to an anchor natively. These let glass surfaces reveal/expand/anchor without JS measurement.

Progressive (gradient) blur (Family.co idiom): stack layered backdrop-filter:blur() divs each masked by a `linear-gradient` alpha ramp (rgba 0→1) so blur intensity FADES across an axis — the soft top/bottom scrim under iOS navigation/tab bars. CSS-only; Chromium struggles with stacked backdrop-filters + mask + overflow:hidden so isolate carefully.

Native scroll-driven + clip-reveal choreography (Rauno/Family craft + web platform): drive reveal/parallax off `animation-timeline: scroll()/view()` so motion tracks the physical gesture not a fixed timer; choreograph a container EXPAND as a clip-reveal aperture (content laid out once at natural size, the morphing box uncovers it) rather than reflowing children — and key child-stagger onsets off the morph's normalized scalar so a fast flick and a slow open both choreograph correctly and an interrupt carries the cascade.

One-scalar one-clock morph orchestration (Benji Taylor/Family 'fluid interface' principle + iOS): a fluid morph is hundreds of small decisions converging on ONE driver — express EVERY animated axis (size, padding, radius, scale, color, child-stagger) as pure calc() off a SINGLE normalized spring scalar written once per frame, so the whole element morphs in one paint with no lead/lag between box and content and no per-engine personality fork.

pitfalls: VT is the WRONG primitive for a continuous layout-size morph: it crossfades rasterized pixels and desyncs when an ancestor is itself animating (the box-leads-content ~16ms lag the AX W01 fold names). Reserve VT for shared-element/route morphs; drive the dock's own collapse off the spring scalar. Also: two co-mounted docks minting the same `view-transition-name` (fourier `glass-dock-1` collision) DROPS the snapshot — names must be per-instance (`useId()`).

backdrop-filter: url(#svgfilter) is Chromium-ONLY and non-standard (WebKit bug 245510 open, Firefox not shipping) — the refraction MUST sit behind `@supports (backdrop-filter: url(#…))` with the plain-blur base ungated as fallback (already correct in glass-refract.css). Never ship the displacement filter as the only blur path.

feDisplacementMap is resize-expensive: any size/shape change forces a full displacement-map REBUILD; only the `scale` attribute animates cheaply. Keep refraction PE-only over the blur base, never on the card/primitive substrate, and isolate filtered nodes with `contain: strict` + minimal viewport dimensions. Simultaneous real-time blur + displacement is heavy GPU rasterization (iOS itself shows ~13% battery drain vs ~1% pre-glass).

Specular blowout: a registered `@property` var() nested in an hsl() alpha computes to 0 in Chromium — drive intensity via layer `opacity`, not per-stop alpha (already learned in glass.css). And the current pure-white 0.55α core violates the 'warm-cream' identity and reads as a white screen; the W09 tune to low-alpha warm-cream + a rest floor of ~0 is mandatory so static unwired surfaces are clean. Don't stack a SECOND specular (the dock `--glass-highlight` hover box-shadow on top of the moving ::before — the worst blowout).

The inheritance bomb: animating an INHERITED custom property (`--phase-color`, `--shadow-color`) per frame forces a whole-subtree style recalc every frame. Route color shifts through a DISCRETE class swap; keep per-frame motion on transform/opacity/width/height only (the convention useLayerTransition F5 already enforces).

Standing will-change holds a compositor layer + VRAM for an idle surface — promote it ONLY for the gesture duration and clear to auto on settle AFTER the final paint (not before, or it flashes). The dock is idle-mostly, so a permanent hint is a real cost; the always-animating goo-blob canvas is the only place a standing hint is defensible.

No-glass-on-glass is a HARD rule, not a preference: a glass surface nested in another stacks blurs (muddy), doubles the rim, and collapses legibility. The `.clear` high-transparency variant ALWAYS needs a dimming layer or legibility breaks. Reserve glass for the navigation/overlay z-bands; inside a glass panel compose FLAT tiers (--card/--muted).
Stacked progressive-blur (layered backdrop-filter + mask + overflow:hidden) is fragile in Chromium — it mis-renders the combination; isolate layers and test, don't assume it composes.

Over-animation on glass: HIG explicitly warns against multiple continuous animations on a glass surface (GPU + distraction); let glass REST in steady states. And honor prefers-reduced-motion as a real fast-path (synchronous swap, no spring) — the substrate must paint one static frame and park, since a CSS reset can't reach a JS rAF loop.

interpolate-size/calc-size can FIGHT a JS spring driving the same axis: AV.W9.0 already retired an interpolate-size arm that second-drove the dock width and froze it. Use the CSS keyword-morph for pure-CSS reveals (accordion/collapsible) but NEVER alongside a JS size driver on the same element.

# AX Liquid-Glass Morph Synthesis — Path-Forward + Research-Backed README

**Synthesizer verdict in one line:** glass-ui is already ~70% of the iOS-26 vocabulary; the SOTA corpus is **mostly convergence, three genuine material additions (lensing, shape-fusion, squash), and one net-new substrate (`useLiquidMorph`)** — and the corpus **unanimously ratifies the AX.W01 single-scalar/single-clock thesis and the retire-VT-for-the-collapse decision** while preserving the per-instance `view-transition-name` route seam. Every facet that touches the dock independently re-derives the same architecture, which is the strongest signal in the corpus.

Grounded against HEAD (`at-dock-convergence @ eaba94f`): `useLayerTransition.ts` (479 lines) STILL forks `NATIVE_VT`/`startViewTransition` (L108/L275) and writes only `--dock-morph-progress` for the child stagger — not a unified box scalar; `interpolate-size`/`calc-size` already retired (AV.W9.0); no `useMorph`/`useLiquidMorph` exists; REQUIREMENTS §18.3 mandates testing exactly that net-new substrate.

---

## PART 1 — THE PATH FORWARD

### 1.0 The decision spine (the one rule the whole corpus converges on)

**ONE driver per concern, per axis, per clock.** Every catastrophic finding in the corpus and in glass-ui's own scar-history is a violation of this: the AV.W9.0 dock-freeze (`interpolate-size` second-driving width against the JS spring), the box-leads-content ~16ms desync (root chrome on CSS transitions vs inner width on the spring deferred a frame), the fourier two-dock `glass-dock-1` name collision (dropped VT snapshot, ~13 red e2e). The unified morph facility must make single-authorship **structural**, not a discipline (facets: single-scalar morph kernel ×8; dual-driver-race pitfall ×11).

The corpus splits the morph problem into **two separable concerns the AX charter already disentangles** — and the path forward keeps them separate:

| Concern | Correct primitive | Wrong primitive | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| An element's OWN continuous reshape (dock collapse↔expand, pill↔card, press-squish) | **One analytic spring → one normalized scalar → every axis via `calc()`** | View Transitions | VT crossfades *rasterized* snapshots → taffy-stretch, text-blur, box-leads-content desync, uninterruptible (facets: VT-wrong-primitive ×9) |
| Element-to-element / cross-ROUTE morph (card→detail, fourier viz↔workspace) | **View Transitions named-element (`view-transition-name`)** | A live spring | VT *is* the web `glassEffectID`/matchedGeometry for genuinely-different DOM; cheap and browser-owned |

This is the AX.W01 CONVERGE fold verbatim: **retire the VT collapse fork, preserve the per-instance `glass-dock-${useId()}` route seam.** The corpus corroborates it from every angle (facets on matched-geometry, view-transitions-for-morphing, the keyframes.js runtime, compositor-perf, and the morph-state-machine all independently reach this verdict).

### 1.1 Deepening the DOCK waves (W01–W06)

**W01 — single-scalar one-clock morph** (the headline; SOTA-blessed). The corpus upgrades the existing plan in three concrete ways beyond "retire the VT fork":

1. **`--dock-morph-t` MUST be `@property`-registered** `{ syntax:'<number>'; inherits:false; initial-value:0 }`. An unregistered custom property animates *discretely* (jumps, no tween) and runs on the main thread; a registered `<number>` interpolates composited (facets: single-scalar kernel, FLIP+scalar, compositor-perf). `inherits:false` is also the inheritance-bomb guard.
2. **Drive the MATERIAL off the same scalar, not just geometry.** Apple's "material thickens when it flexes larger" (deeper shadow, more pronounced lensing, softer light scatter — WWDC25 §219) becomes a free fold: `--shadow-dock-wrap` (W04), `--glass-refract-scale` (the lens), and `--glass-specular-intensity-*` (W09) all read `calc(… * var(--dock-morph-t))`. This is the single highest-value *new* iOS-26 behavior achievable cheaply, and it's why W01 and W09/W20 are coupled, not sequential.
3. **Preserve the velocity-continuity retarget (AV.W9.2) as the one load-bearing iOS-feel piece** through the 479→~130 line rewrite. A re-toggle mid-flight re-seats the live `SpringProgress` from `(value, velocity)` — the thing CSS `linear()` springs and VT fundamentally cannot do (facets: interruptible-spring ×6; iOS-spring-physics).

**Audit-feasibility caveat the corpus surfaces (load-bearing):** the W01 box morph drives D-tier (`inline-size`, `padding`) and C-tier (`border-radius`, `background`, `border-color`) properties per frame — the *expensive* corner of the 16.67ms budget. This is acceptable ONLY because the clip-reveal aperture makes it paint-bounded (content laid out once, box-as-window) not reflow-per-frame. The path forward must audit which axes can move to S-tier `transform`/`clip-path` and keep the morphing subtree small. And the W01 gate cannot be `getBoundingClientRect` polling — keyframes device-proved 181 rAF rect samples captured NO morph (VT runs off the DOM clock); the gate must deterministically drive the readable spring arm and assert box-geometry vs a child's opacity onset on ONE rAF timeline (facets: compositor-perf, morph-state-machine).

**W02 — one orchestrator per dock = the web `GlassEffectContainer`.** Fold the inner `DockLayerGroup` onto the outer driver via DI (the existing `dockContext`/`createStrictContext` seam) so a dock is ONE morph orchestrator whose state = `expandedState × activePane`. Two independent springs writing inline-size = double-animation + desync (the W02 born-RED). This is *exactly* Apple's "one shared sampling region, glass cannot sample glass" rule expressed as motion. Replace the hand-typed `0.08/0.16/0.24` nth-child stagger ladder with one `--dock-stagger-step × index` token, keyed off the morph scalar (facets: GlassEffectContainer ×7; morph-choreography).

**W03 — held as a first-class morph-state input.** `useDockHold(rootRef)` attaches *native* `pointerdown`/`touchstart` on the **resolved host element** — the reka-ui forwarding-drop fix (`@pointerdown` on a `SliderRoot` Slot/forwardRef is silently dropped; vue-tsc + units pass, only e2e catches; the `keepDockOpen` hold has *never* fired through a real drag). `held`/drag-velocity feed the spring target synchronously. The corpus flags this binding-verification class as a recurring footgun to sweep on every reka version bump (facets: morph-state-machine, useLiquidMorph-design, interruptible-spring).

**W04 — concentric radius + content-driven wrap.** Inner radius = `calc(outer − padding)` off the same scalar (pill stadium → finite card glides with width); `corner-shape: superellipse()` interpolating on the morph clock gives the literal iOS continuous-corner curve (Chrome 139+, `@supports`-gated over `border-radius` round). The 40-button @800px = 1861px nowrap overflow is fixed by content-driven intrinsic `flex-wrap`, NOT a magic-640 `@media` toggle. **Do NOT reintroduce `interpolate-size`/`calc-size` on the morph axis** — it is viable only as a one-time *measurement* primitive (`width: calc-size(max-content, size)` read once), never a co-driver (facets: shape-interpolation, interpolate-size ×4).

**W05 — one iOS-spring vocabulary** (the corpus adds a re-parameterization the existing plan should adopt). Excise the legacy `--ease-apple-spring` cubic-bezier (+27.5% bezier-approx overshoot — a *second* spring vocabulary); re-point its 5 internal + 4 speedtest consumers (silent clean-break: a deleted token leaves `var()` resolving empty → instant transitions, no error — sweep consumers before excising). **New from the corpus:** the iOS-17+ canon is `(perceptualDuration, bounce)`, not `(response, dampingFraction)`. Adopt `(duration, bounce)` as the *authoring* surface in `regen-spring-tokens.mjs` (`bounce = 1 − ζ`; stiffness `=(2π/duration)²`; damping `=(1−bounce)·4π/duration`), so settle/control/playful map cleanly to Apple's `smooth(0.0)/snappy(0.15)/bouncy(0.3)`. Keep the governed set SMALL — Apple ships literally three; glass-ui's smooth/snappy/bouncy/gentle/dock is already at the edge, justify each against ≥1 consumer (overfitting census). **`duration` is PERCEPTUAL** (time-to-meaningful-part), NOT settle time — gate on the spring's `settleThreshold`, never `duration` (facets: iOS-spring-physics, keyframes-runtime, every-element-morphs).

**W06 — dock polish + the press-squish atom.** Hoist tap-squish onto the dock controls. The corpus adds **volume-preserving squash** as a thin derivation already buildable from `useSpringPress` (which exposes a `velocity` ref that is currently *unused* for deform): `scale: var(--squash) calc(1/var(--stretch))` with `stretch = 1 + clamp(|v|·k, 0, maxStretch)`. **Cap `maxStretch` LOW** (~1.06–1.10 — iOS Liquid Glass is restrained; `--spring-dock` is only +4.6%; iOS 26.2 *dialed down*). The reciprocal pairing is non-negotiable or volume reads wrong (facets: liquid-squish-physics, interaction-feedback).

### 1.2 Deepening the ANIMATION-language wave (W05)

W05 is the governance wave; the corpus reframes it as **the spring-vocabulary half of the unified facility**. Beyond the excision, three structural points:

- **The two-track CPU/GPU model is correct and already shipped.** Live JS `SpringProgress` integrator for the interruptible/gesture path; build-time `linear()` tokens (sampled from the SAME ODE via `regen-spring-tokens.mjs`) for fire-and-forget declarative transitions. Keep both; the rule is `linear()` for non-interruptible one-shots (entrances, `@starting-style` pops), the live spring for anything a user can interrupt mid-flight (facets: keyframes-runtime, iOS-spring-physics, every-element-morphs).
- **`linear()` sample-count fidelity is a live gate input.** 24 samples clips the bouncy peak (ζ=0.45 analytic peak ≈1.2054 reads ~1.1833); 48 lands it. The proof must render overshoot at runtime from the imported constant, not a hand-typed literal — and a retune MUST touch BOTH the JS const and the regen PRESETS row or the curves drift.
- **Asymmetric/frequency-aware motion is SOTA, not decoration.** Collapse (frequent dismiss) → snappier/non-overshoot register; expand (the reveal) → softer overshoot. This is already encoded in the typed-VT directions; it survives the VT-collapse-fork retirement by moving onto **two spring configs keyed on direction**. And the corpus is firm: **never animate keyboard-initiated or high-frequency actions** (press-squish is pointer-only) (facets: morph-choreography, reduced-motion, cost-budget).

### 1.3 Deepening the GLASS waves (W09 specular, W20 primitives)

**W09 — specular tune-to-subtle** (the lowest-risk, highest-signal concrete fix in the corpus). HEAD `glass.css` paints `hsl(40 30% 100% / 0.55)` — pure white, contradicting its own "warm-cream" comment; rest floor 0.35 not 0; made worse by the AW.W22 blast-radius promotion onto *every* band surface. The fix:
- Warm-cream low-alpha core (~`hsl(40 40% 96%)`), tokenized `--glass-specular-intensity-{rest≈0, hover≈0.22, active≈0.32}` + dark arm; rest floor → ~0 so static unwired plates are genuinely clean.
- **Retire the dock's SECOND specular** — the `--glass-highlight` hover box-shadow stacking on the moving `::before` on the most-hovered surface in the app (the worst blowout).
- Lift the duplicated `trackSpecular` pointer-write (verbatim in `Card.vue` + `DockIconButton.vue`) into `useSpecularTracking()`.
- **Critical gate coupling:** `proof-glass-material-unified.mjs` hardcodes 0.6/0.85 — re-point it to assert the *tokens exist*, or the tune lands RED.
- Tie specular intensity to the press spring (lockstep) — Apple's `.glassEffect(.interactive())`: light and squish on one clock (facets: specular ×3, material ×4).

**W20 — primitive material fixes + GlassPanel retire.** Two concrete defects the corpus surfaces:
- The native-`<dialog>` backdrop uses `hsl(var(--background) / α)` — `--background` is *already* a complete `hsl()` color, so the double-wrap NEVER paints; the scrim dim is **dead**. Fix to `color-mix(in srgb, var(--background) N%, transparent)`. (`proof:no-nested-hsl` polices this class.)
- Retire the JS `createGlassFilter`/`useGlassRenderer` SVG-displacement path onto CSS-native `.glass-material` — it hard-stomps `el.style.backdropFilter/border/boxShadow` with hardcoded non-dark-adaptive white and async-loads a dataURL (blank first paint). Any new refraction must be **CSS-cascade-additive, dark-adaptive, `@supports`-gated**, never an imperative inline-style write.

**The genuinely-missing material atom — LENSING (opt-in, Chromium-only).** glass-ui's `#glass-refract` already bakes the Apple squircle profile `y=⁴√(1−(1−x)⁴)` but with a crude radial-gradient map and a single pass. The SOTA upgrade: (a) a Snell-derived squircle normal map, (b) **three-pass RGB chromatic aberration** (the single biggest visual tell of "thick glass" vs "glassmorphism"). Keep `@supports (backdrop-filter: url(#…))`-gated over the blur base (WebKit bug 245510 open, Firefox not shipping). **Only `scale` animates cheaply** — any shape/size change forces a full displacement-map rebuild, so wire `scale` to `--dock-morph-t` and NEVER regenerate the map mid-morph. Register `--glass-refract-scale` as a typed `@property` so the lens can spring (facets: refraction ×2, material, CSS-baseline).

### 1.4 THE UNIFIED MORPH SUBSTRATE — `useLiquidMorph` (IS it net-new wave-worthy?)

**Verdict: YES — net-new and wave-worthy, but ~70% assembly, not greenfield.** REQUIREMENTS §18.3 explicitly mandates testing this, and the corpus answers decisively (facets: useLiquidMorph-design, every-element-morphs, morph-state-machine, dock-layering, cost-budget). The justification:

- It is the **direct web transposition of SwiftUI's `GlassEffectContainer` + `glassEffectID` + Motion's `LayoutGroup` + `layoutId`** — a proven, named API shape, not a speculative one.
- It makes "every element morphs" ONE idiom instead of per-component bespoke (the §18.1 directive). The dock `--dock-morph-t` (W01) becomes its **first consumer**, not a dock-local trick — which satisfies the substrate-with-consumer invariant *by construction* (dock + ≥1 glass primitive at landing).
- It is the natural home for the perf/a11y invariants the corpus repeats — on-demand `will-change`, inheritance-bomb guard, PRM fast-path, one-driver-per-axis — so every consumer inherits them rather than re-hand-rolling.

**Proposed API surface (two-part seam, mirroring `GlassEffectContainer`+`glassEffectID` / `LayoutGroup`+`layoutId`):**

```ts
// (1) Per-element driver — owns ONE SpringProgress, writes ONE @property-registered
//     scalar --morph-t to elRef once/frame; exposes progress, isMorphing, retarget().
const { progress, state, retarget } = useLiquidMorph(elRef, {
  state: 'collapsed' | 'expanded',      // the discrete model state
  axes: ['inlineSize', 'radius', 'specular'], // CSS calc()s off --morph-t; JS owns only the scalar + the one FLIP-measured size axis
  spring: 'dock',                       // the governed W05 register (default), or settle/control/playful
})

// (2) Shared orchestrator — the GlassEffectContainer / LayoutGroup analog.
//     Nested elements INJECT this; they NEVER spin up their own engine (W02).
provideMorphGroup({ spacing })          // spacing = the gel-merge threshold
```

**Three opt-in tiers (cheapest first):**
- **CSS-only:** an element joins a `.glass-material`/morph-aware class and reads `--morph-t` from an ancestor `MorphGroup` — zero JS (child stagger, color, radius).
- **Composable:** `useLiquidMorph(elRef)` for an element owning its own reshape (dock root, panel). One call; substrate owns spring + FLIP + will-change + PRM + clip-aperture lifecycle.
- **Group:** wrap children in `MorphGroup` for coordinated/nested morphs (dock + DockLayerGroup; a toolbar of fusing glass controls).

**The matched-geometry seam stays bifurcated:** `useLiquidMorph` drives self-reshape via spring+FLIP (no VT); it ALSO exposes an opt-in `morphId` that sets a `view-transition-name` for the shared-element/route case (preserving the fourier seam). The substrate offers both and documents which to reach for; conflating them is the AW regression.

**Reuse ledger (the ~70% already built):** `keyframes.js SpringProgress` (analytic ODE, retargetable, settle-aware) · `useSpring` (Vue wrapper) · `useLayerTransition` (FLIP + velocity-continuity + will-change + clip-aperture lifecycle → *promote* from dock-private to substrate) · `createStrictContext` (typed DI) · `useViewTransition` (route seam) · `useSpecularTracking` (W09 light seam). **Net-new:** the unifying API surface + the `MorphGroup` orchestrator + the `axes`-declaration that lets CSS `calc()` off one scalar + the 3-state `data-morph-state=idle|morphing|settled` lifecycle attribute (promote the existing boolean `data-morphing` to the Radix-style enum so will-change/clip/stagger arm-disarm key off three distinct hooks).

**Where it slots:** a net-new substrate wave (the §18.3 "likely net-new" the charter flags), authored so W01 re-derives `useLayerTransition` as a thin dock-flavored wrapper over it. Guard hard against over-generalization: ship ONLY with ≥2 real consumers at landing; every API knob needs a named consumer or it is overfit substrate.

### 1.5 The 2025 web baseline — achievable now vs graceful degradation

| Capability | Status | glass-ui posture |
|---|---|---|
| `linear()` spring easing | **Baseline 2024** (all engines) | Shipped; the GPU half of the two-track model |
| `@property` typed customs | **Baseline 2024** | Shipped (specular trio); ADD `--dock-morph-t`, `--glass-refract-scale` |
| `color-mix(in oklab)`, `light-dark()` | **Baseline** | Shipped (adaptive tint; `.dark`-class kept for Canvas2D-readability) |
| Same-doc View Transitions + `view-transition-class` + typed directions | **Baseline Newly Available** (FF 144, Oct 2025) | Shipped; KEEP for route/list morphs, RETIRE for dock collapse |
| `@starting-style` + `allow-discrete` + `overlay` | **Baseline Newly Available** | Shipped (`.glass-top-layer`); the native entry/exit lobe |
| **`interpolate-size`/`calc-size()`** | **Chromium-only 129+, NOT Baseline** | RETIRED on the morph axis (correct); usable only as a one-time measurement or a standalone reveal the spring never touches |
| **`corner-shape: squircle`** | **Chrome 139+ only** | Shipped `@supports`-gated; the squircle is the *better tier*, the arc is the *contract* |
| **`backdrop-filter: url(#svg)` lensing** | **Chromium-only** (WebKit bug open, FF not shipping) | The one genuinely-missing atom; opt-in `@supports`-gated PE over blur, never the substrate |
| `anchor()`/`position-area` | **Baseline ~2026** | Future: tether dock-launched popovers, derive transform-origin so menus "grow from the control" |
| `contrast-color()` | **Baseline April 2026** | Future: auto-legible glass-control foregrounds against the live adaptive tint |

**Universal baseline (every engine):** the single-scalar spring + FLIP + clip-aperture + `linear()` tokens + `@property` scalars + `color-mix` tint + warm-cream specular + edge rim + under-shadow + `@starting-style` entry. **Graceful degradation (Chromium-better, never load-bearing):** squircle corners (→ round arc), SVG lensing (→ blur), `interpolate-size` (→ FLIP measure). **A11y floor (non-optional, four guards):** `prefers-reduced-motion` (snap the spring, drop lensing animation, flush the stagger — substrate-owned via live `matchMedia` change-listener since CSS can't reach a JS rAF); `prefers-reduced-transparency` (flatten blur/specular to opaque); `prefers-contrast` (raise opacity floor); `forced-colors` (W36 structure-survival skin: `1px solid CanvasText`).

### `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` + the Liquid Morph facility

**1. What this is — the iOS-26 fidelity bar.** Liquid Glass is a *material*, not a blur: it LENSES (bends light at the rim), carries a motion-tracked specular, casts an adaptive shadow, and MORPHS between states on one interruptible spring. The dock is its headline surface — a singular floating plane that reshapes/merges/splits as a liquid body. State the bar plainly: lensing-not-blur; glass lives ONLY in the navigation/overlay band (never content, never glass-on-glass); one spring, one clock, one scalar; interruptible physics; every axis a token. *(facets: Apple HIG, material model, reference-surveys.)*

**2. Use cases.** Dock collapse↔expand · multi-layer pane swap (`DockLayerGroup`) · vertical/horizontal orientation · slider-in-dock keep-open · scroll-reactive shrink/expand · the generalized facility on dialog/drawer/card/sheet/popover.

**3. The two morph concerns (the decision boundary — front and center).** A one-table rule: **self-reshape → single-scalar spring** (the dock's own collapse); **element-to-element/route → View Transitions named element** (card→detail, route morph); **surface fusion → gooey SVG filter** (two glass pills merging). With the load-bearing caveat: VT crossfades rasterized snapshots — it is the WRONG primitive for a same-element layout morph and the RIGHT one for a route morph. *(facets: matched-geometry, view-transitions-for-morphing, dock-layering.)*

**4. The spring vocabulary.** The governed register table — `smooth(bounce 0)` / `snappy(0.15)` / `bouncy(0.3)` / `gentle(critically-damped)` / `dock(0.32, ζ0.7, +4.6%)` — keyed `(perceptualDuration, bounce)`, with the PRM degrade row (snap-to-target) for each. The two-track note: `linear()` tokens for fire-and-forget, live `SpringProgress` for interruptible. The restraint rule: structural morphs ride the *control* register (snappy/dock), bouncy is reserved for celebratory one-shots; never animate keyboard/high-frequency actions; cap overshoot — iOS *dialed down*. *(facets: iOS-spring-physics, animation-runtime, cost-budget, every-element-morphs.)*

**5. `useLiquidMorph` API.** The two-part seam (per-element driver + `MorphGroup` orchestrator); the three opt-in tiers; the `morphId` route-seam escape hatch; the reuse ledger; the morph state-machine (`idle|morphing|settled`). *(facets: useLiquidMorph-design, morph-state-machine.)*

**6. Best practices / pitfalls (the scar list).** One driver per axis (the AV.W9.0 dock-freeze witness) · per-instance `view-transition-name` via `useId()` (the fourier collision witness) · `@property`-register or it jumps · never tween an inherited custom property (the inheritance bomb) · on-demand `will-change` only · the reka forwarding-drop (native listeners on the resolved host) · clip-aperture keyed to `data-morphing` not the expanded class · the live-audit gate (drive the spring deterministically, never poll `getBoundingClientRect`). *(facets: every pitfall block; ratified against HEAD.)*

**7. Examples.** Minimal `<GlassDock>` collapse · `DockLayerGroup` pane swap · slider-in-dock · `useLiquidMorph(cardRef)` on a card→expanded morph · a `MorphGroup` of fusing controls · the route-morph `morphId` consumer pattern.

**8. The fidelity ladder (achievable vs degrade).** The §1.5 table verbatim: universal baseline / Chromium-better / a11y floor — so a consumer knows exactly what paints everywhere and what is a progressive garnish.
